- Support and develop the Logistics Managers in Agrigento, Palermo and SAR through functional management, capacity building, coaching and mentoring
- Coordinate technical matters with the project teams and, for SAR, among the onshore team, maritime crew and external Technical Superintendent (TSI)
- Enable the OCB vessel to conduct continuous and safe search and rescue activities
- Oversee security measures across the programme and support the Captain, who holds final responsibility for security on board, with MSF expertise and resources
- Ensure that bases, vehicles and the vessel provide safe environments for all staff members
- Analyze reported data to improve the quality and efficiency of the Department’s activities
- Strengthen safeguarding across the Department by identifying and reducing risks beyond those covered by safety and security measures
- Integrate DEI into all processes, including recruitment

**Vessel Management**

- Oversee the overall management of the SAR vessel
- Define the most appropriate fleet management model
- Integrate input from the maritime crew and external Technical Superintendent into the annual Vessel Management plan and budget
- Define internal and external technical support needs, draft Terms of Reference, organize tenders and contract the most appropriate service providers
- Coordinate vessel needs and non-operational periods across departments, including planned maintenance and dry docks, to support programme-wide planning
- Coordinate IT and telecommunications needs and identify appropriate solutions
- Control Vessel Management costs in line with the Authorization Table
- Oversee all Port Agent matters related to supplies and services, delegating tasks to the project team where appropriate, and liaising with relevant counterparts on legal compliance matters such as customs and duties
- Facilitate coordination among the Logistics Managers, maritime crew and Vessel Management Technical Superintendent
- Provide the Country Management Team and functional manager in Brussels with technical planning information, including ordinary and extraordinary maintenance
- Report on all matters related to Vessel Management

## **REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & Experience**

- Degree in engineering or mechanics is desirable
- Previous experience with MSF or other INGOs, including at least 12 months as Logistic Manager, is mandatory
- MSF experience is a strong asset
- Experience in fleet management is strong asset
- Experience in emergency responses and emergency preparedness is an asset
- Experience in strategic engagement with authorities is an asset
- Knowledge of the Italian context is an asset

**Languages**

- Proficiency in **English and Italian**, both written & spoken is mandatory

## **CONDITIONS**

- Expected starting date: **As soon as possible**
- Location\*: based in **Rome, Italy**

***\*Candidates must already have the legal right to work in Italy, either as an Italian/ EU citizen or by holding a valid residence/ work permit that authorizes employment in Italy, with unrestricted access to the Italian labor market***

- Mobility: Frequent stays at the shipyard in Sicily until April 2027, followed by regular travel to projects
- Contract type: Fixed-term contract – full-time
- Contract duration: **12 months (extendable)**
- The contract will be a local contract, under labour Italian legislation; with salary according to MSF **Italy Programmes Country Based** salary grid
- Family position not possible
- ***Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment***
- ***Adhere to the MSF Behavioral Commitments***

**Deadline for applications: 6th of December 2026**

jobs.title: General Coordinator (Head of mission) (F/M) - Myanmar
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Myanmar**

MdM has been operating in Myanmar since 1994. Its strategic objective is to increase access to Harm Reduction and Sexual and Reproductive Health services by addressing health, social, legal and normative barriers though a community-led approach and partnerships. MdM aims to further strengthen its partnership-based approach and advance localization efforts across Myanmar.

In Kachin, MdM works closely with and strengthens a local civil society organization (CSO) to deliver essential PHC and SRH services through dedicated clinics for conflict-affected populations in the context of protracted crisis.

In other parts of the country, MdM - in partnership with 3 CBOs - aims at complementing Harm Reduction intervention in integrating Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) for supporting high-risk groups of people to prevent STIs and GBV.

*Whenever required and possible, MdM could also respond to disaster-related crisis and launch tailored relevant response*.

**About the role**

As General Coordinator, you oversee a range of sites within the country, ensuring that the programmes meet operational, administrative, financial, human, material, safety and organizational objectives by coordinating and leading a team. You ensure the deployment of MdM frameworks, policies and procedures. You lead the implementation of MdM projects in each area by integrating it into a socio-political context. Whenever possible, you lead and develop advocacy work and partnerships.

**What you’ll do**

In close collaboration with the Desk Manager in HQ, the General Coordinator is responsible for:

Strategic and program management: program planning and implementation in accordance with 2027-2028 Country Strategy document, strategy reviews and strategic planning on regular basis.

Human Resources: Support the mission in its changes and defining human resources needs in line with operational requirements. Support all coordinators in their role as managers. Direct management of a multi-level team composed of Coordinators, Manager and Advisor (defining objectives, conducting appraisals…).

Donor relationship: Explore new funding opportunities, representation with donors, negotiations regarding proposals for ongoing and new and/or renewed contracts, copying with major changes in programming including force majeure.

Partnership strengthening: reinforce pre-existing partnerships and encourage the identification of new potential partners to consider progressive handover of MdM activities to partners or health authorities.

Provides technical support to the MdM team: in-country (trainings, workshops, etc.) and using MdM resources globally, linking with Technical Department in HQ and technical Groups.

Security and safety management: be responsible for security management; updating the security guidelines on bi-annual basis; ensure constant monitoring and analysis on contextual geopolitical and security issues.

Administrative, Financial and Logistics: As budget holder, ensure proper use of funds allocated, reporting to donors, yearly budget construction and review. Ensure that appropriate logistics, administrative and financial structures and procedures are maintained in accordance with MdM rules and/or donors’ guidelines.

Reporting: Supervise timely and quality proposals and report submission to donors, submit mission coordination reports to HQ.

**Who you’ll work with**

Based in Yangon, under the supervision of the Regional Desk Manager, you will be the direct line manager of one Deputy General Coordinator, one Medical Coordinator, one Liaison Advisor, one Project Coordinator, one Training Manager and one Field Coordinator located in Kachin State.

You will manage a team composed of 1 expatriate, and more than 50 national staff.

You must liaise with all departments and services located at MdM Headquarters to ensure smooth mission management.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree level, ideally with a background in Public Health and/or in Human rights, political science
- Have a successful coordination experience in development/humanitarian context of minimum 7 years, having already been Country Director/Head of Mission during minimum three years
- Have a past experience in sexual and reproductive health and/or harm reduction related interventions
- Have a proven experience with localization of aid and partnership approach, it will be a strong asset
- Have a past experience in Myanmar, it will be is a strong asset
- Have proven your ability to coordinate, plan, anticipate in collaboration with HQ counterparts
- Are praised for your ability to mobilize around a common project/strategy
- Are recognized for your strong problem solving and organizational skills
- Have proved your leadeship with good listening and diplomacy skills
- Have a good command of the MS Office Suite
- Have an extensive experience in project cycle management, with an excellent konwledge of the donor’s landscape
- Are described as a good team manager with a strong leadership and representation skills
- Have experience in communicating via INGO forum and bilaterally
- Have a solid experience in leading organizational changes, transition processes (program and Human Ressources)
- Are talented in negociating partnership development agreements with local authorities, local Civil Socialty Oorganizations and INGOs
- Are perfectly fluent in English (writing/speaking)

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach
- Are not flexible and not able to cope with last-minute changes
- Are not capable to work and to live in a multicultural environment
- Are reluctant to travel for field visits and regional/international travels

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of December 2026.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info:
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 4'067 €
- Fixed-term contract of 12 months starting as soon as possible
- Single/couple or family posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Yangon with frequent travels to field locations

**Benefits:**

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Individual guesthouse with housing allowance (USD 1'484 for a single person / if family: according to MdM's grid depending on the family composition); Living allowance (per diem) for the accompanying member if unemployed and half per diem per child. Tuition/Schooling allowance for children (as from from 3 years old)
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info:

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: SYRIA - Field Coordinator - (M/F) - Aleppo
jobs.description:
- **Référence :** SRH06852
- **Statut :** Salarié
- **Domaine de compétence :** Coordination régionale / Direction pays
- **Type de poste :** Missions
- **Type de contrat :** Salarié - CDD
- **Pays :** Syrie

## About us

**Desired start date:** 15/01/27
**Duration of the mission:** 6 months
**Location:** North-West Syria (NWS) Base, Aleppo

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Solidarités International operates in Syria since 2013 with a very diversified programs portfolio in Hassake & Raqqa (NES), Aleppo and Idleb (NWS) governorates. To achieve its humanitarian objectives the mission employs 350 staffs and developed meaningful partnerships with international and local NGOs.

In NES, SI is one of the leading agencies in the WaSH sector, responding to emergencies, protracted situations and recovery needs. The strategy is complemented with a significant FSL component, addressing market rehabilitations, business development and agriculture.

In NWS, SI operates in Idleb and Northern-Aleppo with large WaSH programs, with a focus in camps settings for IDP populations, and rehabilitation programs, especially after the earthquake. SI also responds to new emergencies, including regular displacements, natural disasters and epidemics.

SI is also heavily involved in humanitarian coordination, both at strategic and technical level with relevant fora and stakeholders, including key donors.

Since regime's change, SI is redefining it operational model as well as its geographical scope and programmatic priorities. The organizational set up is being deeply reviewed with a Damascus-based coordination office, the reshaping of the base level structure. Assessments are being carried out in new areas including rural Damascus, South, Aleppo and Hama and new partnerships are being envisioned. This is to ensure relevance and efficiency, maximize impact through secured access and more generally ensuring the mission remains fit for purpose in a quickly evolving environment.

## About the job

GENARAL OBJECTIVES :

The NWS Field Coordinator has the role of delegated from the CD for NWS.
He/she proposes an area strategy according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated.
He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures
He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management.
He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.
He/she is the Country Director’s direct contact and representative.

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGE :

Management of short-term and unpredictable funding streams: Ability to prioritise and adapt programming under predominantly one-year grants, with frequent changes in scope and funding continuity risks.
Ongoing mission restructuring and shifting ways of working: Capacity to lead teams through organisational changes (structures, roles, decision-making lines), maintaining clarity, accountability, and team cohesion.
Unpredictable geopolitical and security environment: While day-to-day security may appear stable, the broader context remains volatile; requires strong anticipation, scenario planning, and contingency thinking.
Maintaining operational continuity under sudden context shifts: Ability to rapidly adjust programmes, access approaches, and team deployment in response to political or security developments.
Balancing delegation and control in a changing leadership setup: Ensuring effective oversight while empowering managers, particularly in a context of evolving team composition and responsibilities.
Access and stakeholder management in a fragmented environment: Navigating multiple authorities and stakeholders, maintaining acceptance, and ensuring principled humanitarian action.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

Lead base-level right-sizing and restructuring efforts – Conduct rapid review of structure, staffing, and costs; propose and initiate adjustments in line with funding and priorities, ensuring fair and compliant HR processes.
Stabilise teams through structured change management – Provide clear communication, role clarification, and prioritisation to maintain continuity and reduce disruption.
Align base systems and ways of working with Country Office standards – Ensure operational, programmatic, and support processes are consistent with CO objectives and procedures.
Strengthen delegation and accountability within the base team – Clarify roles, reinforce ownership at manager level, and reduce unnecessary escalation.
Ensure continuity and quality of programme implementation during transition – Maintain oversight of WASH, FSL, and CVA activities to ensure compliant and relevant delivery.
Reinforce planning and anticipation capacity – Strengthen HR, supply, and activity planning tools to improve predictability and reduce last-minute issues.
Maintain strong coordination, access, and external engagement – Sustain stakeholder relationships and preserve access conditions during transition.
Success indicator – Clearer and leaner structure, improved role clarity, and base systems functioning in line with Country Office expectations.

SECURUTY CONTRAINTS :

Recent political and contextual shifts in Syria have brought significant changes to the security dynamics in the NWS region. While Aleppo is currently experiencing a relative calm, the situation remains fragile. The city is now fully under central government control, following agreements with various OAGs that had been active in the area. However, criminal activity persists, though often underreported. As such, continuous vigilance and heightened alertness are necessary in the city.

## Your profile

DIPLOMAS : Masters degree in a related field (humanitarian response, international cooperation, development studies, political sciences…).

EXPERIENCE IN HUMANITARIAN SECTOR: 5 years

EXPERIENCE IN SILILAR EXPERIENCE : 0 - 2 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

1\. Experience of multi-department team management

2\. Experience in security management in unstable contexts

3\. Excellent understanding of sub-office management, including financial, HR, log and project cycle management

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

1\. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, together with the capacity to remain calm under pressure and not lose sight of strategic priorities. Must be organised and efficient.

2\. A sound understanding of the importance of gender.

3\. Sensitivity to cultural differences and the ability to work in a wide variety of cultural contexts.

LANGUAGES :

1\. English necessary

2\. Arabic would be an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**

**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions** : All international staff based in Aleppo will be accommodated in the SI guest house. The telecommunications network is generally good, though it may vary depending on the specific location within the city. Electricity blackouts are common during the day. Staff will have access to local restaurants and markets. A curfew may be implemented depending on the security situation.

jobs.title: Senior Core Services Caseworker
jobs.description:
***This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.***

***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

**Job Overview:** The Senior Core Services Caseworker delivers trauma-informed support to refugee clients during their resettlement and post-resettlement periods, as well as to other eligible immigrant populations, including Cuban, Haitian, and Ukrainian clients. The Caseworker is responsible for promoting a positive resettlement experience and helping clients achieve self-sufficiency. This role involves close collaboration with clients, internal teams, and external partners to create individualized service and self-sufficiency plans. The Caseworker connects clients with a range of financial, medical, social, and vocational resources in alignment with program guidelines and client eligibility criteria.

**Major Responsibilities:**
The Senior Core Services Caseworker plays a critical role in ensuring that clients successfully transition to life in their new community and achieve self-sufficiency. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

**Client Intake, Assessment & Planning**

- Conduct comprehensive intake services to assess individual and family needs, including housing, health, education, employment, and social services.
- Develop tailored self-sufficiency plans in collaboration with clients, outlining specific goals, timelines, and action steps to achieve self-reliance.
- Identify immediate needs and prioritize services such as securing housing, enrolling in benefits, and accessing medical services.

**Pre- and Post-Arrival Coordination**

- Ensure clients receive essential services upon arrival, including temporary or permanent housing, access to nutritious food, healthcare, and transportation support.
- Coordinate with internal departments and external service providers to facilitate timely delivery of services and resources.
- Provide ongoing orientation to clients on accessing services in their new community, including healthcare systems, public benefits, financial literacy, and transportation.

**Direct Support, Advocacy & Case Management**

- Offer individualized support to clients, ensuring they receive appropriate referrals to community resources such as schools, legal services, and mental health providers.
- Advocate on behalf of clients to help them overcome barriers in accessing services and exercising their rights.
- Monitor and assess client progress regularly, addressing challenges and updating self-sufficiency plans as needed to ensure successful outcomes.
- Facilitate connection to employment services in coordination with the employment team to support clients in gaining job readiness skills and securing suitable employment.
- Assist clients in completing critical documents, including benefit renewals, address change notifications (AR-11 forms), and other legal documentation.

**Home Visits & Community Integration**

- Conduct home visits to assess living conditions, provide follow-up services, and ensure clients are safe and stable.
- Help clients build community connections by facilitating their engagement with local services, cultural events, and educational workshops.

**Financial Assistance & Budgeting**

- Plan, request, and track direct assistance funds, ensuring expenditures are aligned with program requirements and client needs.
- Assist clients with financial planning, helping them budget for rent, utilities, and other essential expenses.
- Manage Matching Grant Program client finances, ensuring compliance with program guidelines and accurate reporting of funds disbursed.

**Documentation & Reporting**

- Maintain detailed case files and documentation for each client interaction, ensuring accuracy and compliance with program standards.
- Enter data into client databases and assist with program tracking and reporting requirements.
- Prepare reports as required by internal leadership and external funders.

**Collaboration & Relationship Building**

- Collaborate with internal teams such as Employment, Health, and Youth Services to ensure seamless service delivery.
- Build and maintain relationships with external service providers, such as healthcare organizations, schools, and community groups, to expand the support network for clients.
- Participate in cross-departmental meetings and community coalitions to strengthen partnerships and identify additional resources for clients.

**Client Education & Workshops**

- Develop and facilitate educational workshops for clients on topics such as navigating healthcare, job readiness, budgeting, tenant rights, and U.S. culture.
- Encourage and support client participation in group activities that promote learning, self-advocacy, and social integration.

**Supervision & Volunteer Engagement**

- Train, supervise, and coordinate the activities of interns and volunteers, ensuring they understand program goals and the needs of clients.
- Provide ongoing feedback and support to volunteers to maximize their contribution to client success.

**Compliance, Ethical Standards & Safety**

- Ensure compliance with all organizational policies, program guidelines, and ethical standards in the delivery of services.
- Maintain confidentiality and uphold the highest professional standards in all client interactions.
- Participate in ongoing training and professional development to stay current on best practices and program regulations.

**Transportation & Logistics**

- Use a personal, insured vehicle or public transportation to transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Assist clients in learning how to use public transportation to access essential services independently.

**Other Responsibilities**

- Support special projects and initiatives that enhance client services and improve program outcomes.
- Perform other duties as assigned to meet the evolving needs of clients and the organization.

**Job Requirements:**

**Preference:** Bilingual or multilingual candidates are strongly preferred. Proficiency in additional languages relevant to the client population is a plus.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- **Required:** Minimum of 2 years of professional experience in the human services field.
- **Preferred:** Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant communities.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- **Relationship Building & Networking:** Proven ability to build and maintain effective internal and external relationships through strong diplomacy, communication, and collaboration skills.
- **Cross-Cultural Communication:** Demonstrated success in working and communicating in a multicultural environment.
- **Initiative & Problem-Solving:** Self-motivated with excellent problem-solving abilities, capable of managing multiple tasks, setting priorities, and meeting deadlines efficiently.
- **Detail-Oriented:** Strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
- **Digital & Technical Skills:** Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook) and skilled in using the internet and digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving.
- **Transportation:** Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $24.10-$25.37/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Consultoría Veterinaria para apoyar en Acciones Anticipatorias de El Niño en el Sur del Lago, estado Zulia– DRC Venezuela
jobs.description:
**1. Antecedentes**

El Danish Refugee Council (DRC) es una organización humanitaria internacional que trabaja en más de 40 países. Brinda protección y asistencia a personas refugiadas, desplazadas internas, retornadas, migrantes y comunidades de acogida, siguiendo los principios humanitarios de humanidad, neutralidad, imparcialidad e independencia.

DRC Venezuela opera desde Caracas y cinco bases: Maracaibo, Guasdualito, Carúpano, Sur del Lago y La Guaira. En el estado Zulia, DRC implementa acciones de preparación frente a los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño en los municipios de Colón, Catatumbo y La Guajira, donde la agricultura y la ganadería constituyen medios de vida fundamentales. Los análisis climáticos y las consultas comunitarias realizadas en 2026 evidencian una disminución de las fuentes de agua, el deterioro de los pastizales, el aumento de la salinidad (Guajira) y mayores dificultades para mantener la producción agropecuaria, generando riesgos para la seguridad alimentaria y los ingresos de los hogares rurales.

Las comunidades identificaron una afectación creciente sobre los rebaños bovinos, ovinos y caprinos, reflejada en pérdida de condición corporal, reducción de la producción y mayor vulnerabilidad a enfermedades asociadas al estrés hídrico y nutricional. En respuesta, DRC desarrollará acciones anticipatorias para fortalecer la salud animal mediante campañas de vacunación y desparasitación, suplementación vitamínica y mineral, evaluación sanitaria de rebaños y capacitación para reducir los efectos negativos del niño sobre sus ganados y animales traspatio, con el fin de proteger los activos productivos y la resiliencia de las familias más expuestas a los efectos de la sequía.

**2. Objetivos**

**Objetivo general:**

Fortalecer las capacidades de los hogares productores de los municipios Colón y Catatumbo del estado Zulia para la protección y manejo adecuado de sus activos pecuarios, mediante acciones de asistencia técnica, formación e implementación de medidas preventivas de sanidad animal que contribuyan a la sostenibilidad de sus medios de vida frente a los efectos de la sequía.

**Objetivos específicos:**

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario**, mediante diagnósticos de campo que permitan determinar la elegibilidad de los hogares y el estado sanitario de sus animales, de acuerdo con los criterios establecidos por DRC.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva**, dirigido a pequeños productores u hogares que poseen cría de animales para la subsistencia (auto-consumo), abordando temas relacionados con alimentación animal en condiciones de sequía, suplementación nutricional, vacunación, desparasitación, bioseguridad y otras medidas para la protección de los medios de vida pecuarios.
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio**, incluyendo actividades de evaluación sanitaria, vacunación, desparasitación y orientación técnica a productores, contribuyendo a mejorar la salud animal y la capacidad de recuperación de los hogares frente a los impactos de la sequía.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**, que documente la implementación de las actividades, los principales logros alcanzados, las mejoras observadas en las capacidades de los hogares participantes y las recomendaciones para el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de los medios de vida pecuarios frente a eventos climáticos adversos.

**3. Alcance del trabajo**

La consultoría cubre los siguientes componentes:

1. **Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario.** Meta: Evaluar al menos a 110 hogares, para seleccionar 90 hogares que cumplan con los criterios (línea de base). Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo.
2. **Diseñar e impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva.** Meta: 1. Diseñar un programa formativo de 4 sesiones, para un total de 16 horas formativas por cada grupo. 2. Brindar formación a al menos 3 grupos de 30 personas, para un total de 90 personas formadas. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacios comunitarios ubicados por DRC para realizar la formación
3. **Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio.** Metas: Brindar jornadas veterinarias a los 90 participantes seleccionados en el programa. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacio puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para la formación de los participantes.
4. **Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados**.Metas: 1. Aplicar una línea de salida a los participantes (74 encuestas) 2. Elaborar 1 informe técnico de resultados. Zonas de implementación: Comunidades del Municipio Colón y Catatumbo: Espacio para realizar línea de salida puede ser mediante visitas domiciliarias o acordando con la comunidad un espacio céntrico para los participantes

Nota: la persona consultora no tendrá que cubrir los costos de traslados a las comunidades ni la adquisición de materiales formativos, toda vez que serán cubiertos por DRC.

A su vez, la lista de personas pre-identificadas a diagnosticar será proporcionada por el equipo de Recuperación Económica de DRC.

**4. Productos esperados**

Los productos se entregan de forma progresiva durante el contrato, según las prioridades que fije el Líder de recuperación económica con el Gerente de base. Los plazos y productos son indicativos y se cuentan desde la firma del contrato.

1. Diagnóstico inicial y plan de trabajo con estimación de horas por componente. Semana 1.
2. Realizar la evaluación y selección técnica de los potenciales beneficiarios del componente pecuario. Semanas 2-4.
3. Diseñar un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva de forma general y con énfasis en situaciones de altas temperaturas a fenómenos asociados (El Niño). Semanas 5-6.
4. Implementar jornadas veterinarias preventivas para bovinos, caprinos, porcinos y aves de traspatio. Semanas 6-8.
5. Impartir un programa de formación en manejo y sanidad animal preventiva. Semanas 9-12.
6. Desarrollar una evaluación final de los beneficiarios y elaborar un informe técnico de resultados. emanas 13-16.

**5. Dedicación, modalidad y supervisión**

- **Período:** desde la firma del contrato, prevista para noviembre de 2026, hasta febrero de 2027. Puede extenderse por enmienda según necesidades y presupuesto.
- **Dedicación:** por horas, según las necesidades del Gerente de base y Líder de Recuperación Económica. El total no puede superar **640 horas**, DRC no garantiza un mínimo de horas.
- **Modalidad:** Presencial. El consultor deberá trasladarse con el equipo de DRC a las comunidades de intervención del proyecto, en el cronograma acordado con la oficina de la base de DRC.
- **Supervisión:** Gerente de base. La coordinación diaria es con la Líder de equipo de Recuperación Económica. También habrá coordinación con Supply cuando aplique\*\*.\*\*
- **Recursos que aporta DRC:** acceso a la documentación interna necesaria, costos de traslado a comunidades y material didáctico requerido. La persona consultora usa su propio equipo y conexión, así como la propiedad intelectual del desarrollo de las formaciones.

**6. Perfil requerido**

Requisitos obligatorios

- Profesional universitario en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería en Producción Animal, Biología o carreras afines relacionadas con la producción pecuaria y la sanidad animal.
- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia profesional comprobable en el diseño, implementación o acompañamiento de proyectos vinculados a la sanidad animal, producción pecuaria, extensión rural o fortalecimiento de medios de vida agropecuarios.
- Experiencia en la ejecución de jornadas veterinarias preventivas, incluyendo vacunación, desparasitación, evaluación sanitaria y manejo de especies pecuarias como bovinos, caprinos, porcinos, ovinos y aves de traspatio.
- Experiencia en el desarrollo e implementación de procesos de formación y asistencia técnica dirigidos a productores agropecuarios, organizaciones comunitarias o promotores locales.
- Conocimiento y experiencia en enfoques de adaptación al cambio climático y gestión de riesgos en sistemas productivos agropecuarios, incluyendo medidas orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia de los medios de vida rurales frente a eventos climáticos extremos.
- Experiencia de trabajo de campo con comunidades rurales, poblaciones vulnerables, personas desplazadas, migrantes, refugiadas y/o comunidades de acogida.
- Capacidad demostrada para facilitar procesos participativos, relacionarse con diversos actores comunitarios e institucionales, coordinar actividades en terreno y trabajar de manera efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios.
- Habilidades para la elaboración de informes técnicos, sistematización de resultados y presentación de recomendaciones derivadas de procesos de diagnóstico, capacitación y asistencia técnica.
- Disponibilidad para iniciar en noviembre de 2026 y trasladarse a las comunidades de los municipios indicados, de preferencia en horarios de la mañana.

Requisitos deseables

- Experiencia previa de trabajo con organizaciones humanitarias, agencias de cooperación internacional o programas de recuperación temprana y resiliencia.
- Conocimiento de los sistemas productivos pecuarios predominantes en el estado Zulia o en otras zonas rurales de Venezuela.

**7. Contenido y presentación de la oferta**

Las ofertas deben incluir:

1. **CV** de la persona consultora, con tres referencias profesionales verificables.
2. Propuesta de contenido formativo (preliminar), detallando la siguiente información: - Número de módulo, - Nombre de la sesión, - Contenido a abordar propuesto, - Horas requeridas, - Total horas, -Material didáctico requerido.
3. **Oferta financiera:** tarifa diaria en USD, **todo incluido** (honorarios, impuestos, equipo, conexión y cualquier otro costo), por una jornada de 8 horas. La tarifa horaria se calcula como la tarifa diaria dividida entre 8. El consultor deberá proveer de cuenta internacional para el pago del servicio a contratar o en su defecto pago en Bs.
4. **Documentos administrativos:** RIF vigente, documento de identidad o registro mercantil, y formulario de registro de proveedor de DRC.
5. Declaración firmada de ausencia de conflicto de interés y aceptación del Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC.

No se solicita propuesta técnica.

**8. Criterios de evaluación**

Las ofertas que cumplan los requisitos administrativos y obligatorios se evalúan con una ponderación de 70 % técnica y 30 % financiera. La evaluación técnica se basa en el CV y las referencias. Solo pasan a la evaluación financiera las ofertas con al menos 49 de 70 puntos técnicos. DRC puede entrevistar a las personas mejor puntuadas.

- Formación académica en Medicina Veterinaria, Zootecnia, Ingeniería de Producción Animal o áreas afines. **20** puntos.
- Experiencia en sanidad animal, producción pecuaria y ejecución de campañas de vacunación, desparasitación o atención veterinaria preventiva. **20** puntos.
- Experiencia demostrable en el diseño e implementación de intervenciones para el fortalecimiento de medios de vida pecuarios, incluyendo diagnósticos técnicos, capacitación de productores, asistencia veterinaria preventiva y acciones de resiliencia frente a riesgos climáticos en comunidades rurales. **15** puntos.
- Calidad de la propuesta metodológica para la ejecución de la consultoría. **15** puntos.

**Total técnico: 70 puntos.**
- Oferta financiera: tarifa diaria más baja / tarifa evaluada × 30. **30** puntos.

**Total: 100 puntos.**

**9. Condiciones contractuales**

- **Contrato:** Contrato de Servicios de Consultoría de DRC, con las Condiciones Generales de Contrato y el Código de Conducta de Proveedores de DRC como anexos obligatorios.
- **Pagos:** mensuales, por transferencia, según las horas efectivamente trabajadas, a la tarifa horaria derivada de la tarifa diaria ofertada. Cada pago requiere factura válida y timesheet aprobado por el Gerente de base. Se aplican las retenciones de ley. El monto total no puede superar el equivalente a 640 horas. El consultor deberá proveer de cuenta internacional para el pago del servicio a contratar o en su defecto pago en Bs. •
- **Confidencialidad:** toda la información de DRC, de sus donantes, de su personal y de las personas participantes es confidencial. Los productos de la consultoría son propiedad de DRC.
- **Protección de datos:** el tratamiento de datos personales, incluidos los de personas beneficiarias de CVA, sigue las políticas de protección de datos de DRC.
- **Conducta:** la persona consultora firma y cumple el Código de Conducta de DRC, incluida la tolerancia cero frente a la explotación y el abuso sexual, el fraude y la corrupción.
- **Conflicto de interés:** no pueden participar personas de DRC Venezuela ni que tengan vínculos con personal involucrado en esta contratación.
- **Derecho de DRC:** DRC puede aceptar o rechazar cualquier oferta, total o parcialmente, sin obligación de justificar su decisión.

jobs.title: Communications Adviser IDMC (Maternity Cover)
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

Are you a strategic communications professional passionate about using storytelling, media engagement and digital platforms to drive awareness and influence change?

IDMC-JIPS is seeking an experienced **Communications Adviser (Maternity Cover)** to lead the strategic direction, development and delivery of external communications, amplifying the organisation’s mission to raise awareness and drive action on internal displacement. In this role, you will work collaboratively across teams and with external partners to shape compelling narratives, strengthen the organisation’s visibility and ensure consistent messaging across key audiences. You will oversee the organisation’s primary communication channels, including media relations, website, email campaigns and social media.

You will also play a pivotal role in shaping the communications landscape of the newly merged IDMC-JIPS organisation, leading the evaluation, development and rollout of a shared brand identity while coordinating communications throughout the transition. Working closely with the Global Insights Manager, Director, colleagues and external service providers, you will help build a coherent organisational voice and strengthen the reach and impact of its work.

If you thrive at the intersection of strategic communications, brand development and social impact, this could be your next opportunity!

*Applications close on 6 December 2026. Interviews may take place on a rolling basis, so we encourage early applications.*

**What You Will Do:**

Here are some of your generic responsibilities:

## Strategic Direction and Planning

- Develop and adapt the organisation’s communications strategy in alignment with evolving organisational priorities and capacity, ensuring consistent messaging and audience engagement.
- Lead and coordinate strategic direction of IDMC’s communications outputs, in close alignment with the Global Insights Manager and Director, ensuring messaging supports institutional priorities and is evidence-based.
- Support the Director with the development of key organisational messaging, speeches, and public statements.
- Establish and use performance analytics to refine content strategies and improve communications impact across platforms.
- Work closely with the Insights and Policy teams to align communication outputs with IDMC’s analytical agenda and flagship products.
- Coordinate the evaluation, review and development of the organisation’s brand identity, working with management and external service providers as needed.
- Coordinate the review, alignment and integration of communications platforms and digital tools to support the merger transition and maintain continuity of audience engagement.

## Content Development and Editorial Oversight

- Oversee writing and editing and refinement a wide range of communication materials including website content, newsletters, social media content, and press releases.
- Collaborate with internal teams to identify compelling content from IDMC’s global monitoring, insights, capacity strengthening and policy for dissemination.
- Maintain an editorial calendar and coordinate content input from across the organisation.

## Digital Content and Channel Management

- Design and produce basic visual assets, such as quote cards, infographics, and animations using internal tools or free software.
- Manage IDMC’s social media accounts in line with the overall communications strategy and brand guidelines.
- Produce and distribute email newsletters, optimising performance through testing and analytics.
- Manage media engagement, including drafting press releases, responding to media enquiries, preparing spokespeople, and identifying reactive media opportunities.

## Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

- Work with colleagues across teams to ensure communications outputs reflect the relevance and accessibility of IDMC’s work.
- Coordinate with NRC communications teams to align messaging and amplify shared content.
- Supervise consultants involved in content creation, knowledge dissemination, uploads, technical website maintenance, and data visualisation design.
- Ensure website content is regularly updated and aligned with best practice in architecture and accessibility.

Please download a more detailed[**JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQB4iEgg6uXLTJOUPW6YoKwuAU1AB5njGMMEnx7xhfysiAg?e=mgx0q3) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- At least 7 years’ professional experience in communications, journalism, public affairs, or related field.
- Proven track record in strategic communication and digital media management.
- Strong writing and editorial skills, with the ability to translate complex issues into accessible content.
- Familiarity with performance analytics, media monitoring tools, and content management systems.
- Fluency in English; working knowledge of another UN language is an asset.
- Experience in humanitarian, development, or policy-focused organisations is highly desirable.
- Ability to manage multiple projects and coordinate across diverse teams and stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to distil complex research and data into engaging communications for diverse audiences.
- Experience in managing social media, media relations, and visual content production.
- Proficiency in using design tools (e.g. Canva, Adobe Creative Suite) and CMS platforms (e.g. Drupal or similar).
- Knowledge of international displacement, humanitarian issues, or development policy is an asset.
- Excellent interpersonal skills, with a collaborative and proactive approach to team coordination and stakeholder engagement.
- Experience coordinating brand development or organisational rebranding, including working with external agencies or consultants, is an asset.
- Ability to plan and manage communications during organisational change, build agreement across teams, and translate strategic decisions into practical communication materials and guidance.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC offices in Geneva, Oslo, Brussels, Berlin, London, or any other country where NRC has an established office, provided the duty station is within ±3 hours of CET. The successful candidate must have the legal right to live and work in their chosen country of residence.
- Contract: 6 - 12 months.
- Travel: Up to 10%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s Resident salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Market Place.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you have any questions about this role, please email **ho.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Head of Recruitment
jobs.description:
## **Starting Date / Initial Contract Details**

1st March 2027. Full -time, open-ended

## **Role Summary**

The Head of Recruitment provides strategic leadership for Medair’s recruitment function, ensuring the sourcing, attraction and acquiring of the right talent for country programs and GSO to deliver on its mission and strategic priorities. The role drives timely, effective and proactive recruitment, anticipating future workforce needs and building strong talent pipelines. Through effective leadership and development of the recruitment team, the role ensures a high-performing function that delivers quality recruitment and an excellent candidate and stakeholder experience.

## **Project Overview**

Medair’s global HR function enables effective humanitarian programming by ensuring the organisation recruits and retains the right people. The team fosters a values-driven culture and supports staff through a people-focused model, contributing to both operational excellence and organisational well-being.

## **Workplace & Conditions**

Global Support Office (GSO) position based in Lausanne, Switzerland, Swiss or eligible EU citizens, or those with a valid work permit for Switzerland.

## **Responsibilities**

• **Deliver effective recruitment:** Ensure vacancies are filed with the right talent within agreed timelines, delivering high-quality candidate and stakeholder experience including owning the Relief & Recovery Orientation Course, related management of delegated activities and administrative process.

• **Anticipate Future Talent needs:** Partner with HR and leadership to forecast workforce needs, identify emerging talent risks, advise on talent availability and align recruitment priorities with Medair strategy

• **Build proactive recruitment capability:** Develop talent pipelines, strengthen alumni engagement, grow proactive sourcing capacity and reinforce Medair employer branding & visibility within target talent communities

• **Drive recruitment excellence:** Design, implement and continuously improve the recruitment model to increase effectiveness. Monitoring KPIs, data quality and reporting to drive consistency and accountability.

• **Lead a high performing team:** Develop, coach and empower a capable, accountable and collaborative recruitment team that delivers consistent results and works towards continuous learning and improvement.

## **Qualifications, Experience & Technical Competencies**

• Experience in developing and implementing recruitment strategies and workforce planning within complex international organisations.

• End to end recruitment expertise, understanding contemporary recruitment practices for specialist, leadership and hard-to-fill roles. Experience in proactive talent acquisition, including strategic sourcing and headhunting with proven ability to build pipelines of high-quality candidates.

• Experienced with application systems, HR information systems, data tracking and analysis

• Experience in developing teams and individuals, coaching, mentoring, delegation and support

• Previous recruitment experience within the NGO, humanitarian, international development, or not-for-profit sector desirable

## **Behavioural Skills**

• Ability to see the wider organisational picture, anticipate future needs and connect priorities to Medair’s mission, strategy and operating context

• Collaborative relationship builder, working across cultures and functions to achieve shared outcomes

• Takes ownership for high-quality outcomes and improvements

• Positive, adaptable and able to face challenges constructively

• Servant leader with integrity, humility and respect.

## Team Spiritual Life

Reflect the values of Medair with team members, local staff, people we serve, and external contacts. Work, live, and pray together in our Christian faith-based teams. Fully contribute to a rich spiritual team life, including team devotion, prayer, and words of encouragement.

jobs.title: Senior Research Officer - FSL for South Sudan, based in Juba
jobs.description:
## BACKGROUND ON IMPACT AND REACH

REACH was born in 2010 as a joint initiative of two International NGOs ([IMPACT Initiatives](http://www.impact-initiatives.org/) and [ACTED](http://www.acted.org/)) and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) Operational Satellite Applications Programme ([UNOSAT](http://www.unitar.org/unosat/)). REACH’s **purpose** is to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity for emergency, reconstruction and development contexts, supporting and working within the framework of the humanitarian reform process. REACH facilitates information management for aid actors through three complementary services: (a) need and situation assessments facilitated by REACH teams; (b) situation analysis using satellite imagery; (c) provision of related database and (web)-mapping facilities and expertise.

IMPACT Initiatives is a humanitarian NGO, based in Geneva, Switzerland. The organisation manages several initiatives, including the REACH Initiative. The IMPACT team comprises specialists in data collection, management and analysis, GIS and remote-sensing. IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarter is based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which allows particularly IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support on its fields of intervention.

### **We are currently looking for a REACH Senior Research Officer to support our team in South Sudan.**

**Supervisor:** REACH Research Manager

**Title**: REACH Food Security and Livelihoods Senior Research Officer

**Location:** Juba, South Sudan with minimum of 25% in field and deep field settings

**Contract duration:** 12 months

**Start Date:** January 2027.

## COUNTRY PROFILE

IMPACT, through REACH, has been implementing programming in South Sudan since 2012 supporting humanitarian decision-making with assessments and information management activities focusing on the needs of displaced, returnees, and conflict-affected populations. Today, data collected and disseminated by REACH aims to provide a baseline for ongoing response planning efforts across South Sudan as well as highlight areas of highest need and concern as crises emerge. Broadly, REACH South Sudan implements assessments across three core pillars:

*Monitoring of the humanitarian situation in South Sudan through Real Time Monitoring*, through frequent assessments covering over 2,000 settlements in South Sudan; tracking and analyzing large-scale population movement trends including returns and seasonal movements; market monitoring including Joint Market Monitoring.

*Informing Emergency Prioritization in the response through providing direct technical support to humanitarian clusters* through active engagement with coordination bodies, dedicated assessments and information products, and strategic engagement to promote evidence-based understanding and identification of emergency and catastrophic needs in South Sudan; engagement of Emergency Rapid Response Mechanism rapid assessments and tracking of Areas of Concern.

*Mainstreaming Accountability to Affected Populations and Conflict Sensitivity,* including through standalone assessments on community priorities relating to humanitarian needs and perceptions of assistance, contextual analysis of the impact of aid on community dynamics; as well as providing a critical AAP and CS lens to all REACH SSD research.

## POSITION PROFILE

Under the supervision of, and in close coordination with the Research Manager, Senior Research Manager, IMPACT Country Coordinator and IMPACT HQ in Geneva, the FSL Senior Research Officer (SRO) will be responsible for the management and implementation of food security data collection and analysis at the national level and in hot-spots identified by the REACH team and external analysis frameworks and coordination bodies (such as the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), the Needs Analysis Working Group (NAWG) and the Food Security & Livelihoods Cluster (FSLC). The FSL SRO will engage relevant stakeholders to ensure that research and analysis conducted by REACH is properly utilized, in order to maximize impact on the humanitarian response.

## SUMMARY

The primary tasks of the FSL SAO will include:

Conduct food security assessments – including assessment design, data collection and analysis, output drafting, and dissemination of findings – which focus on building FSL partner capacity to fill FSL information gaps, primarily those that factor into the IPC analysis.

Collaborate closely with Emergency Prioritization sector leads to carry out rapid assessments. Provide input on FSL mainstreaming into REACH workstreams, including EP, and Humanitarian Situation Monitoring and assist with FSL analysis across other REACH workstreams.

Serve as field team leader during FSL assessments. Communicate regularly with the senior management team in Juba and implement ACTED security protocols.

Advocate for the establishment of a community of practice around common methodologies, tools and analysis, both within REACH and within the South Sudan humanitarian community at-large, including by providing technical support and guidance in the development and adoption of such methodologies and processes.

Participate in regular FSL cluster meetings, as well as other relevant coordination or analysis bodies, such as the Needs Analysis Working Group and ICCG. Share information from these meetings on suspected “hot-spots” as well as information on response gaps with the REACH senior management team and other focal points in various sectors.

Engage and provide technical support during IPC workshops, including training, planning and preparing REACH teams for the workshop.

Provide technical backstop for other REACH assessment officers and workstreams regarding correct FSL terminology, methodology, and analysis.

Coordinate logistical aspects of assessments with partner organisations; manage and direct data collection teams in the field.

Ensure the writing of timely and accurate assessment reports and factsheets from collaborative assessments. Work to ensure the harmonisation of FSL-related indicators between the FSL Cluster common tool and other critical, nation-wide assessments.

Support the development/revision of assessment/programme strategies, reports or new proposals.

In coordination with the Country Representative, external representation of REACH with donors, partners and the wider humanitarian community through clusters and sectoral working groups.

### MANAGEMENT OF RESEARCH CYCLES AND COORDINATION

#### **Objective 1: Conduct rapid food security assessments (as requested by Donors, FSL cluster or NAWG)**

- The Senior Research Officer for Food Security and Livelihoods, in close collaboration with the Research Manager and other REACH team members, will conduct rapid assessments, as requested by donors, the FSL Cluster, NAWG, or following the identification of a high-risk area by REACH workstreams or secondary sources. The Senior Research Officer will be responsible for providing analysis on FSL hot-spots and high-risk areas, leading on assessment design, data collection, analysis, output production, and dissemination. Rapid assessments may be conducted independently, jointly with the Emergencies sub-unit, or jointly with external partners. The FSL SRO may serve as team lead and security focal point while conducting assessments in field and deep field locations, and in such cases will be responsible for carrying out security protocols. Moreover, the FSL Senior Research Officer will serve as a general FSL technical backstop for rapid assessments and outputs in coordination with the global FSL specialist at IMPACT HQ.

#### **Objective 2: Support at IPC workshops and capacity build REACH staff**

- The FSL SRO, in close coordination with Research Manager and IMPACT HQ, is responsible for regular attendance and participation in IPC analysis workshops, providing support for REACH participants in analysing South Sudan-wide food security, including REACH outputs, in order to support combined understanding of priority areas for FSL responses. The FSL SRO will also act as an inter-agency liaison with other food security analysis partners to maximize impact before and during the workshop. The SRO will provide capacity building opportunities for REACH staff to enhance their ability to provide technical input and analysis at the IPC workshop, and to better enable them to conduct FSL analysis in their respective workstreams.

#### **Objective 3: Streamline tools and methodologies for food security analysis**

- The Senior Research Officer will work closely with the FSL cluster and other FSL partners to streamline the modules and methodologies used in data collection and analysis, including but not limited to ad-hoc rapid assessments and Inter-agency Rapid Needs Assessments (IRNAs). Specifically, the FSL SRO will work with partners to better understand the tools and methodologies used across agencies to investigate and corroborate reports of extreme health outcomes, including hunger-related deaths.

***REACH REPORTING***

- The Senior Research Officer is responsible for consolidating all analyses and conclusions from assessments into IMPACT products such as factsheets, reports and briefs using standard formats. The Senior Research Officer is responsible for following the designated timeline of reports to be submitted to project partners and donors. They must ensure the writing of timely and accurate assessment reports and factsheets, ensuring the quality and accuracy of technical information provided as well as the confidentiality and protection of collected information. They will ensure that assessment reports contribute to aid coordination and planning and add to the general base of field knowledge in the country for all organisations working in the areas.
- They will also manage the drafting of narrative reports and contribute to the development of financial reports through regular budgetary follow-up.
- The Senior Research Officer will also store, organize and disseminate assessments, project documents and best practices among partners and potential partners. He/she will coordinate timely and accurate reporting to IMPACT.

***HR MANAGEMENT***

- The Senior Research Officer is responsible for day-to-day management of project and field staff both directly and remotely. He/she is expected to guide and direct IMPACT staff and prepare and follow up workplans with each staff member that directly reports to them. The Senior Research Officer will be required to take the lead in the recruitment of IMPACT assessment staff in coordination with the ACTED HR Officer. This will include the preparation of ToRs, observation of recruitment procedures by planning recruitment needs in advance, and undertaking interviews.
- The Senior Research Officer will ensure that all field teams are comprehensively briefed on the objective, expected outputs and that the overall implementation strategy of any given activity is clearly understood. He/she will ensure that project/field staff are given training and complete all the necessary documentation in line with program requirements set by IMPACT.

***EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT***

- The Senior Research Officer will be responsible for the representation of IMPACT in cluster and multi-sector meetings/technical working groups in-country and follow up on technical issues identified in cluster meetings in other parts of the country. This specifically will include liaising with external partners to identify potential for datasets to be integrated into existing databases and mapped to support the coordination of the broader humanitarian community.
- The Senior Research Officer will further represent IMPACT vis-a-vis current and potential donors and communicate relevant information to the IMPACT Country Representative. He/she will participate in inter-NGO meetings and those of UN agencies and any other relevant inter-governmental institutions at the national or provincial level.

***ACCOUNTABILITY TO COMMUNITIES AND BENEFICIARIES***

- The SRO is responsible for ensuring that all interactions with South Sudanese communities are conducted in a respectful and consultative manner. Due attention must be paid to ensuring that communities are adequately consulted and informed about IMPACT programme objectives, activities, beneficiary selection criteria, and methodologies. This is the responsibility of every IMPACT staff member.

***CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION***

- The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. He/she will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during his/her assignment with IMPACT.

## REQUIREMENTS

- Excellent academic qualifications, including a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline;
- Excellent analytical skills;
- At least 2 years’ experience working in humanitarian settings required;
- At least 6 months’ experience leading FSL-related assessments required;
- IPC – level 1 certification an asset
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting;
- Excellent team management skills;
- Ability to collect and interpret multi-sectoral datasets, both qualitative and quantitative.
- Familiarity with the aid system, and understanding of donor and governmental requirements;
- Familiarity with early warning systems / IPC or CH workshop, including participation in analysis workshops, is an asset;
- Fluency in English required;
- Ability to operate Microsoft Word, Excel and Project Management Software;
- Ability to operate R / GIS is an asset;
- High level of autonomy and willingness to spend time in deep-field locations;
- Prior knowledge of the South Sudan context an asset;
- Experience working and living in challenging environments, especially South Sudan, for extended periods of time an asset;
- Willingness to relocate to South Sudan and living in the organisation’s guesthouse.

## COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- For this position, salary between 2’820 CHF and 2’880 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- R&R after 3 months (flight ticket up to 500$ + 200$ of living allowance)
- Contribution to the transportation of luggage: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’ HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training.
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.title: Chief of Party - Food for Peace
jobs.description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Chief of Party – Food for Peace**, you will lead the overall management, implementation and representation of the FFP Program in Mozambique. You will build strong relationships with government, USDA, donors, local organisations and partners, promote adaptive management and gender, youth and social inclusion, and oversee staff development, programme delivery, and financial and donor reporting. The position will be based in Maputo, with 25% travel to targeted regions, and will report to the National Director of World Vision Mozambique. Appointment will be subject to funding and donor approval.

You will oversee grant implementation to ensure strategic objectives, programme quality and donor requirements are met. You will maintain stakeholder and consortium relationships, address implementation challenges, and facilitate learning events to document and share good practices. You will supervise senior international and national staff, build programme capacity, and manage grant staff and consultants. You will establish effective reporting, evaluation and communication systems, submit timely and accurate donor reports, and ensure budgets and expenses comply with approved spending levels and donor regulations. You will also promptly escalate and resolve grant management issues.

**Requirements include:**

- A master’s degree in international development, non-profit management, agriculture, natural resource management, economics, agribusiness, or related concentration from an accredited U.S. college or university, or international equivalent.
- Excellent communication skills and strong management and interpersonal skills.
- Field experience in low-resource environments.
- Professional licenses, as required in the field and by the donor.
- A minimum of 15 years of progressively increasing management responsibility in complex, multi-sectoral international projects, and at least five years of experience in fragile or post-conflict states such as Mozambique preferred.
- Demonstrated technical expertise in food security and livelihoods and experience in managing program implementation and financial reporting.
- Proven success serving in a leadership role for a project addressing issues related to resilience, agriculture, natural resource management, agribusiness, or similar is required, preferably in the Southern Africa region.
- Familiarity with Mozambique’s social, political, economic, and cultural landscape, and demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with host governments, donors, other donor-funded projects and stakeholders, local organizations, and partners preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in adaptive management and learning techniques highly encouraged.
- Experience with large Title II grants with USG food commodities, including Resilience Food Security Activity (RFSA), Development Food Security Activity (DFSA), and Development Food Assistance Programs (DFAP)s.
- Experience with market strengthening grants like Feed the Future (FtF) and Food for Progress (FFPr) preferred.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and managing alliances with the private sector is desirable.
- Familiarity with and commitment to addressing social inclusion in project sectors is required, as demonstrated by at least two years of senior-level experience working on projects that addressed such constraints.
- Proven leadership skills managing projects of a similar size and scope in developing countries facing complex, volatile, and uncertain contexts involving Title II commodities and/or cash transfer mechanisms.
- Fluency in oral and written English is required.
- Fluency in Portuguese is preferred.
- Mandatory travel to implementation sites and regional, global meetings as required.
- Travel to the United States World Vision Washington, DC Office to meet with donors and other stakeholders.
- Ability to sit for prolonged periods and use standard office equipment like computers and phones.
- Strong speaking and hearing ability for high-level meetings and liaison with government officials and stakeholders.

***Note: The Chief of Party (CoP) position is contingent upon funding and donor approval and will be based in Maputo, Mozambique, with approximately 25% travel to targeted regions across Mozambique.***

jobs.title: Survivors of Violence Mobile Implementation Referent (f/m/x) – Brussels, Abidjan or Nairobi – MSF Belgium
jobs.description:
## **CONTEXT**

The medical department of MSF Belgium (OCB - Operational Centre Brussels) plays a key strategic role by defining the modalities of implementation of MSF’s medical strategy so that both coherence and quality can be safeguarded. It also has an overarching normative role and provides technical and strategic support for project implementation and follow-up throughout the project cycle. It ensures knowledge transfer to the medical workforce and stimulates research and innovation by challenging current medical practices and scanning for new approaches.

It comprises multiple specialists across a network of units worldwide (Belgium, Brazil, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Luxembourg, and South Africa) and works in close collaboration with operations, other OCB departments and the MSF movement. It also provides specific partial support to the projects of MSF WACA and Ubuntu.
