**Activity rate:** **100%**

**Functional link:-Country Office Technical Advisor or Project Teams**

**Workplace-Position open in Burkina Faso, Kenya, or Senegal**

**Background:**

The Terre des hommes Foundation (Tdh), headquartered in Lausanne with offices in Zurich, is the largest Swiss organization defending children's rights with more than 2,000 collaborators worldwide. We stand by children to guarantee their rights, protect their lives, and improve their well-being. We achieve this through our innovative programs in health, migration, and access to justice, designed to have a positive and lasting impact.

**Context**:

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), the largest Swiss organization defending children's rights, is reorganizing its organizational model to get closer to children and young people in vulnerable situations in the thirty or so countries where it operates.

Regional offices play a central strategic role in Tdh's new organizational model. Their main mission is to strengthen the relevance, quality, and impact of child protection interventions as well as their role as representative and strategic partners at the regional level. In this context, Tdh is recruiting a regional protection advisor.

In sub-Saharan Africa, Tdh operates directly in 8 countries (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinea-Conakry, Kenya, Mali, Mauritania, Nigeria, and Senegal) and through partnerships in 6 other countries (Benin, Cameroon, Madagascar, Niger, Togo, and Uganda).

In the Africa region, Tdh addresses child protection issues both in emergency contexts and in stable development contexts. The cross-cutting child protection sector brings its expertise to TDH programs in migration, access to justice, and health in the areas of WSDS, case management, participation and empowerment of children and youth, child protection and rights, and business through a community-based approach and systems strengthening.

By addressing the unique challenges children face in these various contexts, Tdh provides comprehensive and integrated support. This approach not only meets immediate protection needs but also contributes to the resilience and long-term well-being of children and their families.

**Overarching responsibilities “Main goals”**

Under the supervision of the Africa Regional Protection Coordinator and in coordination with the global Protection team,

- She/he ensures the development of thematic approaches and methodologies specific to her/his area and adopted within the sector's strategy, as well as their adaptation, rollout, and monitoring at the regional level;
- She/he participates in programmatic steering by ensuring the establishment and monitoring of indicators relating to cross-cutting Protection themes in the region, and by validating the indicators and their analysis.
- She/he provides technical support and guidance to interventions/projects in the fields of Protection at the regional level.
- She/he manages and shares Protection expertise and knowledge with Tdh teams in the region (training, coaching), contributing, among other things, to the digitization of methods and procedures stemming from her/his activities.
- She/he ensures the quality and alignment of Protection interventions/approaches and projects at the regional level.
- She/he ensures technical support as well as quality control of programs in the region across all Protection thematic areas.
- She/he develops strategic partnerships in the fields of Protection at the regional level.
- She/he is responsible for structuring a Protection professional track/stream at the regional level.
- She/he is responsible and accountable to beneficiaries, staff members, and donors.
- Under the guidance and delegation of the Regional Protection Coordinator, she/he represents Tdh in her/his area of expertise by participating in external and internal conferences, forums, working groups, etc., and actively contributes to thematic advocacy related to her/his field in the region.

**Specific Responsibilities/Context of “tasks”**

More specifically, she/he assumes the following responsibilities:

Strategy and Steering:

- Contributes to the thematic analysis of issues and major trends in Protection thematic areas at the national and regional levels;
- Participates in defining the implementation of the organization’s global strategy in the fields of Protection at the regional level;
- Participates in and provides technical support to pilot/cross-cutting/thematic Protection projects at the regional level;
- In coordination with country representatives, ensures the collection and analysis of Protection programmatic indicators for programs in her/his region.

Principles, Standards, Methodologies:

- Acts as the regional Protection thematic focal point in coordination with the Regional Protection Coordinator;
- In this capacity, promotes, facilitates, and ensures the integration and implementation of child protection approaches, methodologies, and standards (including the Minimum Standards for Child Protection in Humanitarian Action) in collaboration with Tdh’s various programs and other cross-cutting areas of expertise (Children and Youth on the Move, Access to Justice, Health, WaSH, and ICT4D), and within Protection projects in the countries of the region, including Safeguarding components;
- Contributes to the rollout of Protection principles, approaches, methodologies, and standards at the regional level;
- Supports the deployment of our Protection programmatic priorities in the field across the Region;
- Leads the development of technical products in child protection areas of expertise integrated into regional projects and strategic country projects.

Innovation:

- Contributes to the development and implementation of innovations across the various fields of Protection for programs in her/his region;
- Utilizes the ecosystem created by the Disruptive Innovation Unit to generate, incubate, and accelerate innovations. Integrates this dimension into team training.

Funding:

- Identifies donors and funding opportunities favorable to Protection in the region;
- Contributes to securing funding (drafting communication documents, contributing to proposal writing led by country offices or the regional office).

Quality Assurance and Quality Control:

- Provides technical support to Protection-related programs in the region;
- Coordinates quality control of Protection interventions, particularly by promoting the use of Tdh’s Protection programmatic indicators;
- Leads, conducts, or facilitates child protection capacity needs assessments, capitalization reports, and related capacity-building activities in the region, notably through blended approaches combining face-to-face training and coaching, online learning and exchanges, etc.;
- Ensures that child protection interventions are grounded in Tdh frameworks, approaches, and methodologies.

Knowledge Management and Sharing:

- Ensures the strengthening of Protection technical skills and capacities (within the framework of Learning & Development for staff) at the regional level;
- Facilitates communities of practice / peer exchanges across all Protection themes for the region;
- Promotes knowledge management and capitalization.

Advocacy:

- Contributes to campaigns and advocacy initiatives related to Protection expertise in line with regional and global priorities.

Practices and Networks:

- Leads and consolidates strategic partnerships in the field of Protection at the regional level in close coordination with the Protection Coordinator and all PREXs;
- Shares Tdh’s knowledge, results, and experiences within professional networks in the field of Protection.

Organizational Structures:

- Participates in identifying needs and defining competencies within her/his specialty;
- Participates in the recruitment of experts in country offices;
- Works in a matrix structure with other sectors of the organization.

**Skills**

This role requires mastery of core **Personal, Social and Leadership Competencies (PSLC)**, **Technical and Methodological Competencies (TMC)**, and **Managerial and Strategic Competencies (MSC)**.

In particular:

- Welcomes and generates creative thinking and innovative initiatives;
- Ensures the production of knowledge, technical expertise, and implementation tools;
- Proven analytical, strategic thinking, and synthesis skills;
- Develops implementation strategies and policies;
- Enhances and strengthens the capacities of targeted actors (internal and external);
- Develops partnership leadership (internal and external);
- Exercises an advisory role within her/his area of specialization in a spirit of partnership.

**As well as the following specific "Job/Technical" competencies:**

- Proven experience in Technical Advisor or Coordinator positions in Protection thematic areas;
- Excellent interpersonal communication and high emotional intelligence (active listening and diplomatic skills);
- Flexibility, responsiveness, adaptability, and pragmatism;
- Rigor, organizational skills, and strong training/facilitation abilities;
- Excellent drafting and representation skills in both French and English;
- Proficiency in standard office software tools.

**Required conditions**

**Training/Qualifications**

1\. **Advanced university degree** (Master’s or equivalent) in a relevant field such as Child Protection, Social Work, Psychology, Social Sciences, or a related field, **or an equivalent combination of professional training and proven experience in the field of Protection.**

2\. **In-depth expertise required** *(technical reference role, recognized senior expertise, ability to analyze protection issues in complex contexts, formulate informed and contextualized strategic recommendations, and provide technical support at multiple levels – project, country, and regional – internally and to local and national partners)* **in at least one of the following areas**:

· **Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPHA)** and/or

· **Protection Systems Strengthening**, particularly in relation to case management systems

3\. **Solid cross-cutting proficiency required** *(contribution to project design / mainstreaming Protection into Programs, alignment of interventions with international Protection standards, continuous technical support to country teams)* **on the following themes and approaches:**

· Child Protection Case Management

· Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPHA)

· Community-Based Child Protection and Protection Systems Strengthening

· Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS)

· Safeguarding

All of these approaches integrate **child and youth participation and empowerment** as a cross-cutting priority.

**Experience**

· **At least 5 years of proven experience in Child Protection**, gained in humanitarian and development contexts, and within diverse cultural settings.

· **Solid professional experience in Child Protection**, including:

\- Regional and/or international technical support to country teams and partners,

\- Implementation, supervision, and analysis of Child Protection programs,

\- Working in humanitarian, fragile, and development contexts.

· **Proven experience in capacity building**, including:

\- Designing and facilitating Training of Trainers (ToT) and training sessions for frontline actors,

\- Coaching, supervision, and technical mentoring, including adapting content to different cultural and operational contexts.

· **Demonstrated experience in project design and management, including:**

\- Project design,

\- Proposal writing and development,

\- Technical dialogue with donors.

· **Experience in knowledge management and capitalization**, including developing, structuring, and sharing knowledge and best practices.

· **Prior experience in an international NGO** or an organization operating at a regional or international scale is an asset.

· **Excellent analytical and synthesis skills,** with the ability to translate complex analyses into operational recommendations.

· **Non-hierarchical leadership,** with the ability to influence, unite, and guide multidisciplinary teams.

· **Ability to arbitrate, prioritize, and provide direction** in complex and constrained environments.

· **High degree of autonomy and sense of responsibility,** with the ability to support and advise other professionals.

· **Ability to manage a heavy workload.**

· **Strong interpersonal skills,** including the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships at all levels of the organization and within external networks and partnerships.

· **Excellent communication skills,** enabling effective interaction with both technical and non-technical audiences.

· **Proven institutional representation skills** and contribution to coordination and advocacy spaces.

· **Good knowledge of the region** and experience working in multicultural and multidisciplinary environments.

**Languages-French (mandatory) and English** at a professional working level

\*\*IT Knowledge-\*\*Mastery and professional practice of Office tools (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, etc.).

**General Code of of Conduct and Tdh’s Risk Management Policies**

Commits to complying with the General Code of Conduct and systematically reports any breach of the Code through the Tdh warning procedure raises the awareness within the Foundation on violence and abuse and the rights that derive from them regarding children, community members and our own employees.

Commits to complying with the Risk Management Policies, including Safeguard policies (the policy of Safeguarding Children, the Policy of Protecting against Exploitation and Sexual Abuse, the Guideline on Abusive Behavior at Work), the Safety/Security Policy and Anti-Fraud/Corruption Policies and the Prevention of Funding Criminal Acivities.

Commits to reducing the risk of abuse by developing an open and informed culture of management within the organization and in our work with children and the communities where we work.

**Tdh’s organizational values**

Our organizational values guide us in our operational and strategic choices and are the foundation of all decisions made by us. Those five values are incorporated into each process connected to the staff. All collaborators are assessed according to the organization’s values.

**PARTICIPATION AND EMPOWERMENT**

- We promote and enhance participation and empowerment.
- We create the space for active participation and embrace inputs from others.
- We are sensitive about others’ needs to influence.
- We share and delegate power and responsibilities.

**PARTNERSHIP AND COLLABORATION**

- We trust the capacities of our key actors as primary responders and agents of change. We build on their strengths and on their needs.
- We champion co-creation and value complementary.
- We appreciate other points of view and seek collectively for pragmatic and innovative solutions.
- We manifest humility, respect, fairness and see others as equal partners.

**INNOVATION AND LEARNING**

- We promote a culture of innovation.
- We value curiosity, welcome new initiatives, and foster creativity.
- We embrace voluntary learning and are ready for trial and error.
- We foster knowledge sharing, learning and strive for sustainability.

**DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION**

- We celebrate Diversity and Inclusion of people.
- We genuinely commit to diversity and inclusion and see it as a wealth in all our activities.
- We understand the cultural contexts and value differences.
- We are truly committed to an equal treatment.

**LEADERSHIP AND EXCELLENCE**

- We thrive to offer our best, we think ahead, and are ready and willing to go the extra mile for the well-being of children.
- We provide quality programming and support. We are accountable and transparent. We use power responsibly.
- We position ourselves through our expertise and savoir-faire.
- We advocate for the rights of children whenever possible and seek actively opportunities to do so.

jobs.title: Regional Housing Ecosystem & Partnership Associate Director
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

PEO Worker

**Summary:**

The Regional Housing Ecosystem & Partnership Associate Director (focus: Ukraine) is a key technical and strategic position responsible for strengthening Habitat's role in the development of inclusive, resilient, and sustainable housing systems in Ukraine and across the Central and Eastern Europe (CEE) region. The role combines housing ecosystem development, partnership building, policy dialogue, and program design to support Habitat's strategic positioning and growth in a highly relevant and evolving housing and recovery context.

Approximately 60% of the role is dedicated to Ukraine, with a strong emphasis on building a robust pipeline of fundable opportunities and strategic partnerships that can translate Habitat's housing ecosystem approach into scalable programs. The Associate Director supports the identification, design, and advancement of donor-aligned concepts, fosters relationships with public, private, and institutional stakeholders, and helps position Habitat as a credible partner in housing recovery, basic services, and longer-term systems change.

The remaining 40% of the role contributes to the advancement of the CEE regional strategic program pillar focused on adaptive reuse and the "Empty Spaces to Homes" approach, ensuring strong linkages between Ukraine programming and broader regional affordable housing priorities. The role is expected to generate cross-regional synergies, support innovation in program design, and contribute to the development of partnership and funding pathways that reinforce Habitat's regional strategic objectives.

In addition, the position serves as the Europe and Middle East (EME) regional focal point for Habitability and Basic Services, providing thought leadership, technical input, and coordination support to strengthen program quality, regional learning, and strategic coherence.

**Key Responsibilities:**

1\. Strategic Planning and Program Support for HFHI's program in Ukraine and CEE region

UKRAINE FOCUS

• Support HFHI Ukraine and its partners in developing, implementing, and aligning national and subnational

housing strategies with HFHI’s vision for a strengthened housing ecosystem

• Lead analysis and integration of market systems, policy frameworks, and partnership opportunities

across the housing value chain

• Conduct research and provide technical recommendations on innovative, inclusive, and climate-resilient

housing solutions, including integration of energy systems, green construction practices, and circular

economy approaches relevant to Ukraine’s recovery context

CEE REGIONAL FOCUS

• Act as focal point for technical construction and spatial aspects of the regional ‘empty space to homes’

i.e. HFHI's "50 Cities strategy" development, implemention and drive project-level initiatives with cities across the CEE region;

• Liaise with demonstration project donors and partners in the NOs, CEE region and western/southern

Europe on promoting ‘empty space to homes’ initiatives, research and funding.

• Conduct contextual research and provide technical recommendations on appropriate, innovative, and

climate-resilient basic services solutions for housing projects.

2\. Support HFHI's Housing. Construction and adaptive reuse technical capabilities across the CEE region (Housing Systems Strengthening and Adaptive Reuse)

UKRAINE FOCUS

• Provide technical and strategic support to local partners, municipalities, and selected private-sector actors in Ukraine to integrate sustainable, inclusive, and resilient housing solutions into wider housing ecosystem development, local governance frameworks, and recovery planning.

• Support the design and delivery of targeted capacity-building initiatives, technical guidance, and knowledge products, including manuals, toolkits, policy briefs, and practical methodologies, to strengthen national and local capacities for housing systems development, partnership-based delivery, and scalable implementation in Ukraine.

• Provide ongoing technical assistance on project oversight, quality assurance, and performance monitoring for housing, neighborhood, and habitability interventions in Ukraine, ensuring alignment with national standards, sustainability objectives, donor expectations, and HFHI’s resilience, inclusion, and people-centered housing principles.

• Lead or support the documentation, synthesis, and dissemination of lessons learned, promising practices, and operational models emerging from Ukraine programming, with particular attention to housing ecosystem development, public-private collaboration, post-disaster and recovery settings, and the integration of energy-efficient and climate-resilient construction approaches.

CEE REGIONAL – Empty Spaces to Homes

• Provide technical and strategic advice to the regional program team and National Organizations engaged in Empty Spaces to Homes demonstration projects, including support on feasibility assessments, adaptive reuse options, life-cycle thinking, renovation pathways, and delivery models suited to local housing markets.

• Serve as a regional focal point for technical guidance and quality support to demonstration projects under the Empty Spaces to Homes agenda, helping ensure that practical pilots contribute to scalable models and evidence generation for Habitat’s 50 Cities by 2030 strategy.

• Support the development of tools, technical guidance, training modules, manuals, and reference materials that strengthen internal and partner capacities to design, implement, and scale adaptive reuse interventions under the Empty Spaces to Homes approach.

• Contribute to the strategic positioning of Empty Spaces to Homes within the wider CEE affordable housing agenda by helping connect demonstration projects to the 50 Cities by 2030 vision, city-level partnerships, municipal engagement, and broader housing ecosystem opportunities.

• Support the CEE program team and National Organizations in identifying and leveraging construction product donations, technical partnerships, and in-kind contributions that can strengthen the implementation, visibility, and replicability of Empty Spaces to Homes demonstration projects.

3\. Serve as Habitatibility and Basic Services contact point for EME regions

• Ensure regional housing programs incorporate habitability, accessibility, and safety standards in

alignment with HFHI housing quality frameworks.

• Provide guidance related to basic services provision in renovation projects (heating, ventilation,

WASH, fire safety, digital readiness).

• Capture and disseminate knowledge on habitability and service integration within HFHI.

4.Coordination, Representation, and Learning

UKRAINE FOCUS

• Actively engage in HFHI’s regional and global communities of practice and represent HFHI in Ukraine in

technical and policy forums

• Represent HFHI in Ukraine in national and international coordination platforms, working groups, and

forums related to housing, social infrastructure, and energy efficiency.

• Promote HFHI’s technical leadership and facilitate learning exchanges with donors, ministries, and

industry partners

• Provide a technical support to the Ukraine team in leading the development and nurturing of strategic

partnerships with government, financial institutions, private sector, and NGOs to advance affordable

housing, housing finance, and resilient urban development in Ukraine

CEE Regional Focus

• Represent the Area Office in regional and sub-regional technical forums, working groups, and

stakeholder engagements related to 'empty space to homes’ initiatives.

• Build partnerships with external organizations, donors, and networks engaged in housing technology,

climate change adaptation, and disaster risk reduction.

• Participate in relevant HFHI communities of practice, technical initiatives, and cross-departmental

coordination.

5.Supporting Fundraising

• Collaborate closely with Fundraising, Partnership, and Program team of Ukraine Program to position

Habitat’s housing ecosystem and partnership agenda to donors

• Contribute to proposal design, donor engagement, and project development processes, ensuring

technical quality, strategic alignment, and compliance with HFHI and donor standards

• Support in reviewing technical proposals, promoting donor compliance and the implementation of

technical standards in relation to ‘empty space to homes’ demonstration projects.

**Minimum Requirements**

• Master’s degree (or equivalent experience) in housing, architecture, urban development,

civil/environmental engineering, economics, or related field. Strong background in housing systems,

market-based approaches, and/or policy reform preferred.

• Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience in housing, shelter, urban development,

market systems, or development programming, including at least 5 years in partnership management or

ecosystem development

• Proven experience in affordable housing, incremental housing processes, or climate/disaster-resilient

housing solutions.

• Background in humanitarian assistance, development sector, shelter or energy related projects

• Familiarity with humanitarian and development sector trends, principles, standards (e.g., Sphere, Core

Humanitarian Standard, WHO guidelines), and country specific standards.

• Strong analytical, facilitation, and advisory/consultancy skills.

• Proficient in MS Office; familiarity with GIS software and construction management tools preferred.

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a matrix organization and multicultural

environments required.

• Active support of HFHI Values:

Humility - We are part of something bigger than ourselvses

Courage - We do what's right, even when it is difficult or unpopular

Accountability - We take personal responsibility for Habitat's mission

• Safeguarding

HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work. Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct.

This role requires 30% of international travel.

\#LI-DNI

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Responsable des initiatives gestion de déchets et achats responsables (volant) – Zone Afrique - HULO
jobs.description:
**Date de rédaction : 19/11/2026**

**Date de début de contrat : 01/02/2027**

**Type de contrat : CDD**

**Localisation : Tchad avec déplacements sur les pays de sa zone d'affectation**

**Conformément aux principes de fonctionnement propre à la Coopérative, ce poste est recruté et contractualisé par Solidarités International, pour le compte de la Coopérative hulo.**

**QUE FAISONS-NOUS…**

La Société Coopérative Européenne d’Intérêt Collectif « Humanitarian Logistics Cooperative », aussi connue sous l’appellation « hulo », est la première coopérative humanitaire fondée en juin 2021. Dirigée par des organisations humanitaires et intégrant de nouveaux membres régulièrement, hulo a pour objectif d'améliorer l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant la collaboration et la mise en place de projets communs dans ses pays d’intervention. Chez hulo nous sommes convaincus que le partage et la mise en commun de ressources et d’expertises entre organisations contribue à augmenter la performance de la logistique humanitaire et de la chaine d’approvisionnement

Notre action s’appuie sur une approche collaborative et participative, l’intelligence collective et l’animation d’une communauté de pratiques. Toutes nos activités sont structurées autour d’un objectif commun, impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes autonomes et interdépendantes, qui coopèrent de manière horizontale. Le pilotage y est distribué, fondée sur la concertation, la co-responsabilité et l’engagement volontaire.

Dans nos 7 pays d’intervention répartis dans 3 régions nous mettons en place des initiatives mutualisées dans les domaines des achats, des ressources humaines et des pratiques responsables. En support aux organisations humanitaires nous coordonnons des initiatives de transport international humanitaire mutualisées à destination des crises humanitaires les plus graves. Enfin nous développons constamment des solutions digitales au service de la communauté humanitaire.

Pour en savoir plus, vous pouvez consultez le rapport annuel 2026 en cliquant sur le lien [https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/](https://hulo.coop/january-2026-annual-impact-report/)

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis près de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans une vingtaine de pays environ, les équipes de SI - 2000 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de staffs nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

**DESCRIPTIF DU POSTE**

**Objectif général :**

Le/la Responsable des initiatives gestion de déchets et achats responsables (volant) soutient le réseau hulo sur le terrain : équipes locales hulo, organisations humanitaires membres et partenaires, opérateurs de gestion de déchets et fournisseurs. Il/elle les accompagne le déploiement opérationnel de (1) La gestion des déchets (Joint Waste Initiatives (JWI)) ; (2) Les achats responsables.

Il/elle joue un rôle clé dans le renforcement des capacités du réseau, ainsi que dans la mise en œuvre concrète et le suivi opérationnel des solutions identifiées. Il/elle apporte un appui opérationnel et un accompagnement pratique, en veillant à la qualité des initiatives mutualisées et au respect des normes, avec des solutions adaptées aux contextes locaux.

**Priorités sur les 2/3 premiers mois :**

1. Prendre connaissance de la stratégie locale hulo, des JWI et projets achats responsables en cours, et se coordonner avec le RP et les équipes locales
2. Réaliser les évaluations terrain des pratiques de gestion des déchets et des besoins des organisations dans le pays prioritaire
3. Analyser le cadre réglementaire national et rencontrer les autorités compétentes
4. Lancer ou finaliser les Appels à Manifestation d’Intérêt (AMI) pour cartographier les filières de valorisation/destruction
5. Se positionner dans les réunions de coordination, clusters et groupes de travail
6. Établir le planning des déplacements dans les autres pays prioritaires

**Principales missions :**

**1. Déployer les initiatives de gestion de déchets mutualisées sur le terrain**

- Réaliser des diagnostics des pratiques et besoins des organisations humanitaires en matière de gestion des déchets et identifier les opportunités de mutualisation.
- Identifier, évaluer et mobiliser les opérateurs et filières locales de collecte, de recyclage, de valorisation et de traitement des déchets.
- Concevoir et déployer des solutions mutualisées de gestion des déchets, en accompagnant les organisations dans leur mise en œuvre opérationnelle.
- Assurer le suivi de la qualité des services, mesurer les résultats et capitaliser les bonnes pratiques et les enseignements tirés des initiatives.

**2. Promouvoir et déployer les achats responsables**

- Identifier des alternatives responsables adaptées aux marchés locaux et contribuer à l'évolution des spécifications techniques des produits et services.
- Sensibiliser et accompagner les organisations humanitaires et les fournisseurs dans l'adoption de pratiques d'achats plus responsables.
- Animer des échanges avec les acteurs locaux et capitaliser les initiatives et leurs impacts.

**3. Renforcer les capacités et accompagner les acteurs sur le terrain**

- Concevoir et animer des formations, ateliers et actions de sensibilisation à destination des équipes hulo, des organisations membres, partenaires et fournisseurs.
- Accompagner les organisations dans l'évolution de leurs pratiques en tenant compte de leurs besoins et des spécificités locales.
- Contribuer à l'intégration des enjeux en lien avec la gestion des déchets et les achats responsables dans les outils et systèmes d'information de hulo, en lien avec les équipes concernées.
- Documenter les retours d'expérience et contribuer à l'amélioration continue de la stratégie de hulo.

**4. Développer la coordination inter-ONG, la représentation**

- Développer les collaborations avec les organisations humanitaires, les acteurs institutionnels, les fournisseurs et les partenaires locaux afin de favoriser les approches communes et les solutions mutualisées.
- Représenter hulo au sein des mécanismes de coordination, clusters et groupes de travail pertinents dans les pays d'intervention.
- Mobiliser les parties prenantes autour des initiatives mutualisées de hulo et contribuer aux dynamiques sectorielles\*\*.\*\*

**VOTRE PROFIL**

**Expériences /formation**

- Formation spécialisée en gestion de projet, idéalement complété avec une spécialisation en lien avec la thématique, gestion des déchets ou achats responsables, ou domaine similaire ;
- Une formation en logistique / chaîne d’approvisionnement associée à un intérêt marqué pour les enjeux en lien avec la gestion des déchets et les achats responsables, sera un atout.
- Expérience dans le secteur humanitaire : 3 ans minimum

**Compétences techniques**

- Expertise en gestion des déchets dangereux et non dangereux, connaissance des enjeux HSE et des filières locales de collecte, de recyclage et de valorisation.
- Connaissance des enjeux liés aux approvisionnements / achats responsables
- Maîtrise de la gestion de projets : définition des priorités, planification des activités, allocation des ressources et suivi des résultats.
- Expérience dans l'organisation et l'animation d'ateliers, de formations et de réunions multipartites.
- Maîtrise des outils bureautiques (Excel, Word, Outlook).
- Excellentes capacités rédactionnelles.
- Maîtrise courante du français et de l'arabe, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.

**Compétences transversales**

- Excellentes capacités de communication, de facilitation et de collaboration avec des interlocuteurs variés (autorités, ministères, ONG, acteurs du secteur privé et collecteurs informels).
- Capacité à travailler en réseau, à coordonner des acteurs multiples et à développer des partenariats.
- Aptitude à accompagner le changement et à renforcer les capacités des organisations et partenaires.
- Capacité d'analyse, sens de l'organisation et aptitude à gérer les priorités.
- Adaptabilité, réactivité, pragmatisme et capacité à résoudre des problèmes dans des environnements opérationnels complexes.
- Autonomie, sens de l'initiative et capacité à représenter une organisation et à développer un réseau professionnel.

**SI VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES**

- CDD de 8 mois basé à N’Djaména
- Salaire brut mensuel : à partir de 2365€ (2150+ 10% congés payés), en fonction de l’expérience du/de la candidat/e.
- Perdiem : selon la politique perdiem en vigueur
- Breaks : Pendant la mission, un système d’alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois. A ces périodes de pause, s’ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.
- Couverture sociale et médicale : Les expatriés bénéficient d’une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d’un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

jobs.title: Regional Safety and Security Advisor
jobs.description:
## **Background**

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), founded in 1960, is Switzerland’s largest organization dedicated to defending children’s rights. Tdh is committed to bringing about meaningful and lasting change in the lives of children and young people, particularly those most at risk. Tdh operates in some 30 countries, working in both humanitarian and development contexts.

In sub-Saharan Africa, Tdh operates directly in 8 countries (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinea-Conakry, Kenya, Mali, Mauritania, Nigeria, and Senegal) and through partnerships in 6 other countries (Benin, Cameroon, Madagascar, Niger, Togo, and Uganda).

As part of the decentralization of its organizational model, Tdh has opened a regional office in Dakar, Senegal, for which a position of Regional Safety and Security Advisor has been created.

## **Responsibilities**

- Monitors, analyzes, and reports on performance indicators related to risk management (security and safety) across the Africa region.
- Maintains contextual knowledge of all countries in the region and travels regularly to all countries in the region, including on very short notice if necessary.
- Promotes and ensures the implementation of global frameworks, standards, processes, and tools related to risk management (security and safety) in the Africa region.
- Ensures the implementation of risk prevention measures (security and safety) and provides methodological support in the management of critical incidents.
- Supports the various countries of operation in developing and maintaining crisis management capacity.
- Supports country offices in all matters related to risk management (security and safety).

## **Participation in governance bodies**

- Regional office managers’ meeting.
- Regional Managers’ Meeting.

## **Key Responsibilities**

Leadership

- As an authentic leader, he or she inspires the team through leadership, fosters collaboration and team cohesion, makes informed strategic decisions, and is committed to excellence and continuous innovation.
- Represents, encourages, and promotes the organization’s organizational and sociocultural values.
- Participates in mandatory governance bodies.

Management

- Where applicable, oversees the recruitment of field-level counterparts, working in coordination with the relevant departments in the regions and at headquarters; assists with their onboarding and provides them with ongoing support and training.

Safety and Security

- Supports managers in the region’s countries of operation in implementing the risk monitoring system, ensuring that security risks are identified, mitigated, and managed.
- For each country, reviews and analyzes security plans, SOPs, and contingency plans, and issues recommendations for improving risk monitoring.
- Supports country offices in implementing security incident management (reporting, handling, lessons learned, etc.).
- Builds the capacity of teams to address challenges related to risk management (security and safety) at the regional level, trains delegation teams, and supports the training of partners.
- Encourages and coordinates cross-country exchanges.
- Communicates regularly with counterparts in other regions and at headquarters to improve and harmonize risk monitoring in the region.
- Timely reports relevant information to headquarters to contribute to overall risk management (security and safety).
- Ensures, at the regional level, that the organization’s crisis management plan is in place and regularly trains the relevant personnel.
- Promptly informs headquarters of any crisis in the region based on established frameworks and protocols.

Regional Office Management

- Manages risks (security and safety) at the regional office in Dakar.

## **Skills**

This position requires fundamental personal, interpersonal, and leadership skills, as well as technical, methodological, managerial, and strategic skills. In particular:

Excellence in leadership

- Setting an example.
- Behavior aligned with core values.
- A strong spirit of collaboration and teamwork.

Management skills

- Skills in safety and security management, supported by a solid understanding of the principles of human resources management and project management.
- Ability to support and advise on organizational and operational transformation.

Interpersonal Skills

- Strong ability to establish and maintain positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Reliability and autonomy, with the ability to organize, make decisions, and manage conflicts at a basic level.
- Integrity, commitment, and compassion.

Specific Knowledge

- Strong analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to see the big picture, exercise sound judgment, and make decisions.
- Good practical knowledge of humanitarian access and security, and a commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Knowledge and experience in designing and implementing security-related training (risk analysis, humanitarian access, crisis management, etc.).
- Excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills, strong writing skills, and a keen sense of communication.

## **Requirements**

Education/Qualifications

- Degree: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in security management, international development, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

Experience

- At least five years of significant experience in operational safety and security management within an international humanitarian organization, with increasing responsibilities.
- Previous experience in Africa and a proven understanding of regional and national dynamics are strongly preferred.
- Experience in crisis management and the ability to train regional teams in this area are desirable.

Translation

- Required written and spoken languages: French and English.
- Preferred languages: Arabic, national languages of the countries where we operate.

Computer Skills

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office

## **Objectives**

Objectives for the coming period must be outlined on the performance review form in consultation with the line manager and in collaboration with the functional manager.

## **Tdh’s General Code of Conduct and Ethical Policies**

- Commits to promoting and adhering to the Global Code of Conduct, systematically reporting any violations of the Code through Tdh’s formal reporting mechanisms, and addressing any violations of procedures and processes appropriately.
- Raises awareness within the Foundation regarding the risks of non-compliance with policies, violence, and abuse, as well as the rights of children, community members, and our own employees.
- Commits to complying with key ethical policies and guidelines, including the safeguarding policy, the anti-fraud and anti-corruption policy, the conflict of interest policy, and other policies related to the prevention of terrorist financing and criminal activities, as well as workplace conduct.
- Commits to putting these values and principles into practice by demonstrating exemplary behavior, in full compliance with the Code of Conduct, and by always adhering to established procedures and processes.
- Commits to fostering a compliant and informed management culture within the organization and in our work with children and the communities in which we operate.

jobs.title: National Facilitator for Sustainability and Transition Strategy Development
jobs.description:
**About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is a non-profit, autonomous regional organization, international in status, established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes, with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction. Established in 1986 as an outreach center of the Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), ADPC has evolved into an organization dedicated to building disaster and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs across the 15 Priority Areas of Action of its Strategic Action Plan 2026–2030: Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. These Priority Areas of Action are complemented and underpinned by three cross-cutting enablers: gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation. Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**Department Introduction:**

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of ADPC focuses on enhancing the preparedness, climate action, and adaptation capacities of governments, response organizations, volunteers, non-governmental organizations, the private sector, communities, and other traditional and non-traditional actors within the Disaster Risk Management and Climate Resilience Ecosystem. It emphasizes the importance of locally-led adaptation strategies as a critical component of effective climate action while striving to strengthen the capacity of institutions and at-risk communities to achieve faster, more efficient, and climate-resilient disaster recovery. The department collaborates with these actors to ensure that regional, national, sub-national, and local disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and climate action frameworks and implementation plans are developed and implemented well before disaster strikes, prioritizing climate resilience and integrating strategies to reduce risks and build resilience against future climate-related hazards.

**Statement of Intent**

The Preparedness and Climate Action (PCA) Department of the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC), in partnership with the Ethiopian Disaster Risk Management Commission (EDRMC), is implementing the **E**nhancing **M**ulti-Hazard **P**reparedness for **O**ptimizing **W**arning and **Early Response** (EMPOWER) Program in Ethiopia, with technical and financial support from the Gates Foundation.

The EMPOWER Program aims to strengthen the organizational, institutional and leadership capacities of Ethiopia's disaster risk management institutions at national and subnational levels. It is anchored in the Multi-Hazard, Impact-Based Early Warning and Early Action System (MH-IB-EW-EAS) Roadmap, developed by EDRMC and endorsed by the Government of Ethiopia. Building on previous institutional capacity-building initiatives, EMPOWER seeks to strengthen institutional systems, human resources, technical capacities and coordination mechanisms that can be sustained beyond the program period. As part of these efforts, a Sustainability and Transition Strategy will be developed through an EDRMC-led, consultative and evidence-informed process, with technical support and inputs from ADPC. The process will review institutional capacities, systems and functions developed through successive capacity-building investments, including EMPOWER, to identify what has been sustained, remaining gaps and lessons learned. It will examine priority functions and capacities required to support EDRMC's evolving mandate, appropriate institutional arrangements, resource requirements and feasible sustainability and transition pathways. The findings will also inform EDRMC's longer-term institutional development priorities and potential future programming, with stronger government ownership and sustainability considerations embedded from the outset.

In this context, ADPC seeks to engage an experienced national facilitator to support the consultative process and development of the EMPOWER Sustainability and Transition Strategy during the period December 2026 to March 2027.

**Scope of Work**

The consultant will work closely with EDRMC leadership, relevant directorates and technical units, with overall coordination and technical support from the ADPC team, to facilitate an EDRMC-led process for developing the Sustainability and Transition Strategy. The consultant's role is to facilitate an objective, structured and participatory process, rather than to independently determine EDRMC's sustainability arrangements. The process will be guided by the principles of EDRMC leadership and ownership; function before financing; institutionalization rather than parallel arrangements; realism and feasibility; progressive transition; and future-oriented programming.

**1. Conduct desk review and prepare the consultation framework**

- Review the National Disaster Risk Management Policy (2024), the MH-IB-EW-EAS Roadmap, the EMPOWER program documents and progress reports, and relevant EDRMC policies, institutional strategies, organizational arrangements and capacity-development initiatives, including previous ADPC-supported programs, EMPOWER and other relevant partner-supported investments.
- Assess the institutional capacity-development journey, identifying key achievements, capacities and systems sustained over time, remaining gaps and lessons learned.
- Prepare a concise working paper outlining initial findings, institutional sustainability issues and strategic questions for consultation.
- Develop the consultation methodology, guiding questions and workplan in coordination with EDRMC and ADPC, and establish a common understanding with EDRMC leadership on the purpose, scope and expected results of the exercise.

**2. Facilitate Institutional Consultations, Sustainability Assessment and Strategic Planning**

- Facilitate consultations with EDRMC leadership, directorates and technical units to identify priority institutional functions, capacities and systems required to fulfil EDRMC's evolving mandate under the National DRM Policy (2024), including functional linkages with sector ministries and sub-national DRM structures.
- Assess institutional ownership, existing capacities, human resources and surge-capacity arrangements, operational and ICT systems and their recurrent costs (e.g., software licences, hardware, situation room and data-server infrastructure), resource requirements, partnerships and sustainability challenges, taking into account previous investments in institutional capacity building.
- Examine feasible institutionalization and sustainability arrangements, including integration into government structures, capacity transfer, recurrent financing and continued technical or partner support.
- Develop a sustainability and institutionalization mapping, presenting options for discussion rather than predetermined commitments, that captures priority functions, institutional responsibilities, resource requirements, sustainability options and lessons learned from previous capacity-building investments.
- Facilitate strategic consultations with EDRMC, ADPC and, as appropriate, the Gates Foundation to review assessment findings and identify feasible sustainability and transition pathways.
- Support discussions on institutional priorities, ownership, financing options, partnerships and progressive transition of technical support, with a focus on strengthening EDRMC's long-term institutional capacity for disaster risk reduction, resilience building and self-reliance, including its ability to coordinate, operate, maintain and improve the MH-IB-EW-EAS using its own structures, people, procedures and resources after EMPOWER ends.
- Identify institutional or policy matters requiring higher-level government decisions and propose appropriate engagement approaches to secure necessary institutional commitments and resources.
- Document agreed directions, outstanding issues and strategic considerations for potential future capacity-development programming.

**3. Develop and finalize the Sustainability and Transition Strategy**

- Prepare a draft EDRMC-led Sustainability and Transition Strategy and Action Plan, drawing on consultation findings, institutional priorities and agreed strategic directions.
- Develop a practical, phased action plan identifying priority actions, institutional responsibilities, indicative timelines, resource considerations and sustainability indicators, including actions that can begin during the remaining EMPOWER implementation period.
- Facilitate review of the draft and a validation discussion with EDRMC, ADPC and the Gates Foundation, as appropriate, to confirm the proposed sustainability pathways, institutional responsibilities and priority actions.
- Incorporate feedback and submit the final Strategy and Action Plan by **10 March 2027**.

**Expected Deliverables**

This is an output-based consultancy. Payment will be made upon acceptance of each deliverable by ADPC, in consultation with EDRMC, as follows:

- Deliverable 1 – \[20\]%;
- Deliverable 2 – \[40\]%;
- Deliverable 3 – \[40\]%.

The consultant is expected to deliver the following:

1. **Inception Report and Consultation Framework:** Outlining the methodology, workplan, initial mapping of programs’ supported functions, the working paper on emerging sustainability issues and strategic questions for consultation, preliminary review of EDRMC's institutional capacity-development journey, lessons from previous capacity-building investments, and proposed consultation approach.
2. **Institutional Sustainability Assessment and Consultation Report:** Consolidating findings from institutional and strategic consultations, including priority functions, existing capacities, institutional responsibilities, sustainability challenges, resource and financing requirements, and feasible institutionalization and transition options. The report will include the sustainability and institutionalization matrix and document key stakeholder discussions, agreed directions, outstanding issues and priority actions.
3. **Sustainability and Transition Strategy and Action Plan:** Developed in consultation with EDRMC and reflecting assessment findings and agreed sustainability priorities. The strategy will outline institutional responsibilities, phased actions, resource requirements, milestones, and indicators to strengthen long-term institutional capacity, disaster risk reduction, resilience building and self-reliance. It will include a priority action plan for the remaining EMPOWER implementation period and strategic considerations for potential future programming in Ethiopia. The final version will incorporate feedback from EDRMC, ADPC and the Gates Foundation, as appropriate.

**Deliverable 1:** Inception Report & Consultation Framework

**Timeline:** Dec 2026

**Deliverable 2:** Institutional Sustainability Assessment and Consultation Report

**Timeline:** Jan-Feb 2027

**Deliverable 3:** Sustainability Strategy

**Timeline:** Feb - Mar 2027

**Working Principles:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities above, the consultant will be supervised by the ADPC Program Manager based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, and work in close coordination with a designated EDRMC focal point, who will facilitate access to relevant directorates, personnel and information. ADPC will provide relevant documentations and evidence and will support the organization of consultation and validation meetings. All deliverables will be reviewed by EDRMC and ADPC prior to acceptance.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

The consultant should demonstrate the following:

- Postgraduate degree in Disaster Risk Management, Public Policy, Public Administration, Institutional Development, Development Studies, or a related field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in institutional capacity development, organizational strengthening, strategic planning, or sustainability and transition planning, preferably within government or public-sector institutions.
- Proven experience in facilitating institutional assessments, strategic consultations, and multi-stakeholder planning processes, particularly with government leadership and technical departments.
- Demonstrated experience in developing institutional sustainability strategies, transition plans, capacity development frameworks, or related strategic and operational plans, including practical implementation arrangements.
- Good understanding of disaster risk management, multi-hazard early warning systems, and institutional arrangements for disaster preparedness and response.
- Experience assessing institutional functions, human resource capacities, operational systems, financing requirements, and options for sustaining externally supported investments.
- Familiarity with government institutional structures, planning and budgeting processes, and coordination mechanisms in Ethiopia; prior experience with EDRMC or the national DRM system is an advantage.
- Strong analytical, stakeholder engagement, facilitation, and report-writing skills, with the ability to translate consultation findings into actionable recommendations, responsibilities, milestones, and resource considerations.
- Experience working with government institutions, development partners, and international organizations is highly desirable.
- Excellent proficiency in English and Amharic is required.

**Duty Station:** Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

**Duration:** December 2026 – March 2027

The consultancy is expected to require 30 working days, spread over a three and a half month period from December 2026 to March 2027. A detailed work schedule, including consultations and deliverable deadlines, will be mutually agreed upon at the commencement of the assignment, in coordination with EDRMC and ADPC. Indicatively, the level of effort is

- \[8\] days for Deliverable 1,
- \[12\] days for Deliverable 2 and
- \[10\] days for Deliverable 3.

The final Strategy is due by March 2027; the remaining period allows for any final review and contract close-out.

**Itinerary:**

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC financial policy. All travel must be pre-approved by ADPC and undertaken only upon written request and consent by the ADPC.

jobs.title: Donor & Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 1 year. Employment location will be Kabul, Afghanistan (AF).

Welthungerhilfe (WHH) has established offices in Afghanistan since 1992, supporting communities through humanitarian assistance and development programmes. Today, WHH operates in five provinces, reaching up to 700,000 people annually. With its Country Strategy 2025–2030, WHH Afghanistan aims to increasingly strengthen development-oriented programming while continuing to respond to humanitarian needs.

As Donor & Grants Coordinator, you will play a key role in supporting this strategic direction. Working closely with the Country Programme Team and the Director of Programmes, you will contribute to the development of project proposals for short-, medium-, and long-term humanitarian and development interventions. You will oversee the entire grants management cycle, ensuring compliance with WHH's Programme and Project Cycle Management (PCM) standards as well as internal and external quality requirements. Through your work, you will help strengthen WHH's strategic positioning, donor engagement, and long-term impact in Afghanistan, contributing to sustainable and meaningful change for the communities we serve.

## Your responsibilities

- Support donor and stakeholder mapping, identify new funding opportunities, and contribute to the development of innovative project ideas and proposals.
- Develop a strong understanding of donor strategies, priorities, and requirements, and support the implementation of projects in line with WHH's and donors' strategies, procedures, and standards.
- Identify potential co-financing opportunities to diversify WHH Afghanistan's funding sources and strengthen its financial sustainability.
- Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders and donors, and represent WHH in relevant coordination meetings and forums.
- Coordinate and oversee grants monitoring processes in close collaboration with relevant stakeholders across the Country Programme.
- Strengthen the quality of grants and project management by promoting best practices and supporting capacity-building initiatives for staff and partners.
- Provide programmatic and coordination support to the Country Office in implementing WHH Afghanistan's new strategic direction.
- Develop, regularly update, and share grants management guidelines, resources, and tools, including the Grants Follow-up Tracker.
- Ensure that WHH's programme management system (ProMIS) is regularly updated and its relevant functionalities are effectively used throughout the entire project cycle.
- Support the Director of Programmes in developing donor mapping and fundraising strategies for WHH Afghanistan, while proactively researching and identifying new funding opportunities.
- Manage and coordinate grants across the Country Programme, ensuring effective reporting, alignment, and synergies in programme design and implementation.
- Lead the development of high-quality project proposals and engage with existing and potential donors in close consultation with the Director of Programmes and other relevant stakeholders.

## Your profile

- A bachelor's degree or equivalent university qualification in International Development, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- At least three years of relevant, country-based experience in proposal development, reporting, and grants management within an NGO.
- Strong ability to structure complex information and present it in clear, concise, and visually appealing documents, reports, and proposals.
- Proven grants management, donor reporting, communication, and coordination skills, ideally gained in a humanitarian context.
- Experience working in fragile contexts, with an understanding of relevant socio-cultural factors. Previous experience in Afghanistan, the region, or high-risk field offices is an advantage.
- A proactive, self-motivated team player with strong interpersonal skills, a good sense of humour, and experience in mentoring colleagues.
- Willingness to work in an insecure environment, adhere to strict security procedures, collaborate respectfully in a multicultural team, and receive the necessary vaccinations.
- You recognize the growing value of data in your field and are eager to build your awareness and skills to incorporate data-informed approaches into your work.
- Excellent English writing and communication skills, with proven experience in developing compelling, high-quality funding proposals tailored to different audiences.

## What we offer

- Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
- Commitment to Well-Being: We attach great importance to our duty of care with a focus on safety, security & health.
- Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
- Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
- Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

In addition, Welthungerhilfe offers numerous other benefits, which you can find under [**Our benefits**](https://www.welthungerhilfe.org/benefits-for-expatriate-employees).

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

jobs.title: Délégué Administration et finance (M/F/D) Madagascar - CDD - 40h (7045)
jobs.description:
La **Croix-Rouge luxembourgeoise** recrute

**Délégué Administration et finance à Antananarivo (Madagascar) (M/F/D) - référence :**

pour la mission de l’Aide internationale de la Croix-Rouge luxembourgeoise A.S.B.L. (AICRL) à Madagascar en CDD de 12 mois renouvelable – Statut : non accompagné.

**Le poste est basé à Antananarivo.**

Les projets mis en œuvre consistent principalement en l’assistance aux populations vulnérables dans le domaine des abris/habitats et de l’assainissement. Ces projets sont actuellement mis en œuvre avec principalement des fonds du Ministère des Affaires étrangères et européennes luxembourgeois, des fonds propres et ECHO.

**Missions :**

Sous la responsabilité du Directeur Financier basé à Luxembourg et en collaboration étroite avec le chef de mission et la responsable Desk, le gestionnaire administration, finances contribue à la qualité du fonctionnement de la mission en garantissant la bonne gestion administrative et financière des projets et de la Mission CRL.

Principales responsabilités :

1. Comptabilité et gestion de la trésorerie
- Gestion de la comptabilité – superviser le cycle comptable pour la Mission
- Gestion de la trésorerie –assurer un contrôle et une gestion fluide de la trésorerie
2. Engagement des dépenses, contrôle du budget, & gestion financière
- Engagement des dépenses
- Suivi du budget des projets, contrôle des coûts de la Mission, audits internes et externes
3. Gestion du cycle financier du projet
- Elaboration les budgets des projets et les rapports financiers en respectant les procédures internes de la CRL, les procédures de la CR malgache et celles des bailleurs ainsi que les deadlines
4. Coordination avec la CR malgache en matière de finances
5. Accompagnement de la CR malgache d’une prise d’autonomie dans les fonctions financières et administratives
6. Garantie de la bonne gestion financière avec la CR malgache sur nos projets communs
7. Archivage
8. Ressources Humaines
- Appui à la Croix Rouge malgache dans le recrutement et la gestion des ressources humaines locales, surtout celles du Département Suppor
- Accompagnement de la Croix-Rouge malgache dans le renforcement de ses compétences ; Assurer la formation du personnel en matière de procédures administratives, finances et comptables
9. Management
- Suivi, coordination et accompagnement du personnel Support mis à disposition de la CRL et renforcement de ses capacités
- Coordination du personnel Support basé à Antananarivo et sous bases.
10. Inventaire
- Garantie d’avoir une mise à jour régulière de l’inventaire de la Mission
- Travailler en collaboration avec le délégué logistique
11. Sécurité
- Garantie de mettre en place des éléments garantissant la sécurité des Délégués tels que mentionnés dans le Plan de sécurité et ses annexes (malle sécurité, fonctionnement des Iridium, trousses de secours…), en collaboration avec le délégué logistique
- Respect du Plan de sécurité et ses annexes ainsi que les consignes du Chef de Mission/Desk en la matière

**Profil :**

- Formation supérieure dans le domaine de la finance
- Expérience professionnelle de 5 ans, dont minimum 3 en mission humanitaire
- Expérience en remote management (gestion à distance) est un atout
- Connaissance du logiciel SAGA constitue un sérieux atout
- Connaissance des bailleurs tels que MAEE Luxembourgeois et ECHO constituent de sérieux atouts
- Expérience professionnelle au sein du Mouvement Croix-Rouge constitue un atout
- Excellente maîtrise à l’oral et à l’écrit de la langue française. Connaissances de base de l’anglais.
- Maitrise du pack office (Word, Excel, Powerpoint)
- Permis de conduire voiture catégorie B

jobs.title: Operations Officer (part time) – National Position
jobs.description:
Malteser International (MI) is the international humanitarian relief agency of the Sovereign Order of Malta. For over 60 years we provide relief and recovery for people during and following conflicts and disasters around the world. Christian values and humanitarian principles form the foundations of our work. In over 30 countries in Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and the Middle East, we support people in need – regardless of their religion, origin or political convictions.

In the Middle East Region, MI is operating in the context of the humanitarian crisis in Syria since 2012 implementing emergency relief measures in Turkey, Syria, and Lebanon and since 2014 in Iraq. Malteser International’s programs cover needs mainly in the health sector and are mostly partner implemented. In Lebanon, Malteser International works in partnership with the “Order of Malta Lebanon (OML)” to implement a multi-annual program funded by the German Federal Foreign Office to strengthen health, social and agro- humanitarian services provided by OML across Lebanon.

**To support the implementation of its partner programme in Lebanon and to strengthen operational compliance, documentation and procurement processes, Malteser International is looking for an experienced Compliance Officer (part time).**

As Compliance Officer, you will support overall operations with a strong focus on operational compliance and partner coordination with the Order of Malta Lebanon (OML). You will help ensure that finance, procurement, administration, logistics and documentation processes follow MI and donor guidelines, support audits and project closures, and contribute to accurate filing, procurement tracking, asset management and payment processes.

## **Your responsibilities:**

- Ensure that partner expenditure reporting, supporting documents and voucher verification processes comply with MI and donor requirements
- Follow up with OML on compliance recommendations, corrective actions and agreed improvements in operational processes
- Document and maintain compliance-related communication, records and filing systems between MI and the implementing partner
- Conduct field compliance visits and support regular compliance monitoring of partner activities and operations
- Manage MI procurement processes, including purchase requests, purchase orders, procurement tracking and payment requests
- Support contract follow-up, deliverables monitoring, due payments and asset/inventory documentation in line with MI procedures
- Contribute to monthly financial closure, audit preparation and project closure processes by ensuring complete and accurate documentation
- Support administrative and logistics arrangements for the Country Office, including preparation of delegation visits and other operational needs

## **Your profile:**

- University degree or relevant professional qualification in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Logistics or a related field
- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in operations, compliance, finance administration, procurement or partner support, preferably in the humanitarian or development sector
- Good understanding of financial documentation, voucher verification, procurement processes and basic internal control requirements
- Experience in supporting partner coordination, compliance follow-up or documentation processes is an asset
- Familiarity with donor requirements and audit preparation, particularly for institutional donors such as GFFO, BMZ, ECHO, EU or UN agencies, is an advantage
- Strong organizational skills, attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records, trackers and filing systems
- Good communication and coordination skills, with reliability, integrity and a service-oriented working style
- Strong commitment to humanitarian principles, safeguarding and accountability
- Fluent in English, French and Arabic, additional languages (German) are an asset

## **What we offer:**

- Start date: ASAP
- Duty Station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Duration of contract: 1 year, part time (50 %)
- Salary according to qualification and experience, insurance package

## **Working for Malteser International**

Malteser is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all people, regardless of gender, confession or origin.

Malteser International is committed to safeguarding people within our programmes from exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment and has specific policies on this commitment (including a Code of Conduct) which outlines the expected behaviour and the responsibility of all staff, consultants and other organisational representatives. Malteser International conducts reference and background checks for all staff (including criminal records check for specific roles). Any candidate offered a job with Malteser International will be expected to sign MI’s Code of Conduct as an appendix to their contract of employment and agree to conduct themselves in accordance with the provisions of these documents.

Whether you work as a specialist on overseas service or in one of our regional offices - we offer you a challenging working environment in an experienced international team. More than 1,000 national and international staff are currently deployed in various crisis and disaster areas around the world as well as in our regional offices in Cologne and New York City. For more information please click [here](https://www.malteser-international.org/en/jobs.html).

jobs.title: Project Manager, Digital Delivery
jobs.description:
**Remote · Europe Contract · Full Time**

## **About Relief Applications**

Relief Applications is a humanitarian tech company headquartered in Toulouse, France. We build digital tools with and for NGOs, UN agencies and mission-driven organisations, bringing solutions to those changing the world.

We have more than 40 projects running at the same time, from ERPs and grants platforms to data tools and information management systems. Our team is remote and works across Europe, Africa and Latin America.

## **About the role**

From the first workshop to handover and support. You will be the client's main contact and keep developers, designers and sector experts working to one plan.

## **Key responsibilities**

### **Delivery**

- Plan each project in phases and sprints, with working versions the client can test
- Track scope, person-days, budget and milestones, and flag risks early
- Keep allocations, tickets and project records up to date in our tools

### **Clients**

- Run kick-offs, workshops, steering meetings and phase sign-offs
- Handle change requests openly and keep a record of decisions
- Tie delivery to the contract: deliverables, payment milestones, reporting

### **Team**

- Coordinate developers, designers and consultants across countries and time zones
- Agree priorities with tech leads when several projects need the same people
- Give the team clear, short briefs and feedback

### **Quality and handover**

- Organize user acceptance testing and training with client teams
- Make sure documentation, user guides and code handover are complete
- Close projects properly: lessons learned, client feedback, final report

### **Business development**

- Help the bids team with work plans, team set-up and budgets for new proposals
- Join client interviews for projects you would run

## **What's in it for you**

- A varied portfolio with UN agencies, international NGOs and donors
- Remote-first work in a small, international team
- Real ownership of your projects, from scoping to close
- Tools that serve humanitarian and development programs directly

## **Candidate profile**

### **Experience**

- 5+ years managing software or digital projects
- Running several projects in parallel for external clients
- Ideally with NGOs, UN agencies, donors or public bodies

### **Skills**

- Agile delivery: sprints, backlog, user stories, acceptance criteria
- Budgeting and tracking in person-days
- Enough technical knowledge to discuss APIs, hosting, data models and GDPR with engineers
- Jira or a similar tool, and clear written reporting

### **Language**

- Fluent English and French
- Spanish or Arabic is a plus

### **Soft skills**

- Organised, and calm when priorities collide
- Confident in front of a client's leadership
- Honest when something slips, and early about it

### **Additional assets**

- ERP, grants management or case management projects
- Knowledge of donor rules and grant cycles
- Field or HQ experience in a humanitarian organisation
- Scrum, PMP or PRINCE2 certification

jobs.title: Senior Programme officer - Macroeconomic Policy
jobs.description:
The African Economic Research Consortium (AERC) seeks an experienced and results-oriented macroeconomist to contribute to its macroeconomic policy fellowship and institutional capacity-development portfolio under the Department of Research and Capacity Development. The position combines substantive economic policy expertise with the design and delivery of demand-driven technical assistance and fellowship support to African governments which are beneficiary of the new, flagship and ambitious African Growth Fellowship (AGF) Program implemented in partnership with the African Capacity Building Foundation (ACBF).

The Senior Programme Officer will work with government counterparts, fellows, host institutions, technical experts and development partners to translate priority policy and institutional needs into practical assignments, high-quality analytical products and sustained institutional capability. The postholder will be expected to deliver technically credible advice, manage policy advisory activities effectively, track results of AGF and help ensure that skills, processes and knowledge are embedded within beneficiary institutions in a coordinated manner with regular follow up meetings.
