We uphold the highest standards of integrity and expect the same of those we work with.

Engagement with DT Global is subject to formal background screening, criminal record checks, employment verification, and periodic compliance checks. All DT Global staff receive safety, compliance, safeguarding and integrity training, and we expect our personnel and partners to always act in alignment with our company values.

jobs.title: Asistente Administrativo/a (National Position)
jobs.description:
? La Fundación AVSI es una organización internacional sin fines de lucro con sede en Italia que desarrolla proyectos de cooperación y desarrollo. Su presencia en Colombia se ha mantenido en los últimos años mediante iniciativas de adopciones internacionales. A partir de 2026 se prevé un fortalecimiento de esta presencia con la implementación directa de un proyecto de cooperación internacional, acompañado por el equipo regional con oficina en Brasil.

Juntos por la Vida es un proyecto financiado por la Comisión de Adopciones Internacionales (CAI), orientado a mejorar el bienestar integral y la protección de niñas, niños y adolescentes en situación de vulnerabilidad en Colombia y México. La intervención fortalece los sistemas públicos y comunitarios de protección, las oportunidades educativas, el apoyo psicosocial y las trayectorias de autonomía progresiva.

El proyecto desarrolla capacidades técnicas y metodológicas entre operadores de centros de protección, familias de acogida y adoptivas. En Colombia refuerza la integración de los servicios de salud y educación; en México, la colaboración con los sistemas DIF de Tabasco, Chiapas y Oaxaca. La implementación involucra a AVSI México A.C. y Fundación Monserrate ETS, con el apoyo técnico de los organismos autorizados para las adopciones internacionales SRAI y La Maloca.

Para su ejecución en Colombia, AVSI requiere un/a Asistente Administrativo/a con formación profesional y experiencia suficiente para gestionar procesos administrativos y financieros con autonomía, apoyar al equipo del proyecto y contribuir a consolidar la capacidad administrativa de AVSI en el país.

## Objeto de la contratación:

Incorporar un/a Asistente Administrativo/a del Proyecto Juntos por la Vida en Colombia, responsable de apoyar y gestionar sus procesos administrativos, financieros y contables, de acuerdo con los procedimientos de AVSI, los requerimientos del donante y la normativa local aplicable.

La persona deberá contar con capacidad para planificar, organizar y dar seguimiento a la gestión administrativa de una oficina o filial. En el marco de sus responsabilidades del proyecto, contribuirá al fortalecimiento de los procedimientos y controles de AVSI Colombia, bajo la orientación de la administración regional y en coordinación con la gerencia del proyecto y la representación legal.

? **Lugar de destino**: Bogota

? **Fecha de inicio**: 04.01.2027

⏳ **Duración**: 12 meses

**Idioma**: Español

**Reporta a**: El/la Asistente Administrativo/a reportará operativamente al/la Gerente del Proyecto Binacional y funcionalmente a la Gerencia Administrativa Regional, en coordinación con el equipo financiero de AVSI HQ.

La preparación y gestión de operaciones se realizará respetando la separación de funciones, las autorizaciones de gasto y las facultades de firma establecidas por AVSI.

## ? Tareas y responsabilidades principales:

### Gestión financiera y contable del proyecto

- Realizar, organizar y mantener actualizados los registros contables del proyecto, verificando la integridad de los soportes y registros y cierres que correspondan.
- Verificar la elegibilidad de los gastos y su correcta imputación presupuestaria, conforme a los requerimientos del donante y los procedimientos de AVSI.
- Elaborar y actualizar el seguimiento presupuestario, analizar desviaciones e informar oportunamente a la gerencia del proyecto proponiendo medidas correctivas.
- Preparar el flujo de caja y las solicitudes de fondos, anticipando las necesidades financieras de las actividades y los compromisos pendientes.
- Preparar y tramitar pagos a proveedores, contratistas y personal, previa verificación de soportes y autorizaciones; mantener actualizado el control de anticipos, cuentas por pagar y legalizaciones.
- Realizar las conciliaciones bancarias mensuales y el control de caja, identificar diferencias y dar seguimiento a su resolución.
- Preparar los reportes financieros periódicos y la documentación de rendición de cuentas, asegurando su consistencia con los registros contables y la ejecución técnica.
- Aplicar criterios documentados para la distribución de costos compartidos y verificar que los gastos imputados al proyecto correspondan a su ejecución y a las condiciones del donante.

### Gestión administrativa y soporte operativo

- Realizar la elaboración y actualización del plan de adquisiciones; gestionar cotizaciones y documentación de compras y contrataciones, respetando los procedimientos y niveles de aprobación.
- Mantener actualizados los expedientes de proveedores y contratos del proyecto, controlar vencimientos y dar seguimiento a entregas, servicios y compromisos.
- Gestionar la documentación administrativa del personal vinculado al proyecto y coordinar la información necesaria para nómina, honorarios y obligaciones asociadas con los responsables correspondientes.
- Organizar la logística administrativa de actividades, reuniones y desplazamientos, incluyendo anticipos, comprobantes y legalizaciones.
- Mantener el inventario y los registros de entrega, uso y custodia de los bienes adquiridos por el proyecto.

### Control interno y administrativo

- Organizar el archivo físico y digital del proyecto, asegurando trazabilidad, confidencialidad y disponibilidad de los documentos para revisiones y auditorías.
- Preparar la documentación requerida por auditorías internas y externas, y dar seguimiento a las observaciones y acciones correctivas.
- Mantener un calendario de cierres, reportes, vencimientos contractuales y obligaciones administrativas relacionadas con la ejecución del proyecto, coordinando con la contabilidad local y la administración regional.
- Realizar y dar el seguimiento de las obligaciones contables, tributarias y laborales aplicables a las operaciones del proyecto en Colombia.
- Organizar y documentar los procedimientos de pagos, compras, archivo, administración de personal y control de activos de AVSI Colombia que sustentan la ejecución del proyecto.
- Identificar debilidades operativas y riesgos administrativos o financieros, comunicar los hallazgos y proponer mejoras que fortalezcan la gestión de la oficina local.
- Consolidar la información administrativa y financiera de las operaciones vinculadas al proyecto que requieran la representación legal, la gerencia y la administración regional.

### Coordinación y acompañamiento al equipo

- Coordinar con la gerencia del proyecto binacional la programación de actividades, adquisiciones y pagos, alineando las necesidades operativas con la disponibilidad presupuestaria.
- Orientar al equipo técnico sobre requisitos documentales, elegibilidad de gastos, compras, anticipos y rendición de cuentas.
- Coordinar con la administración regional, AVSI HQ y la contabilidad local los cierres, reportes, consultas y mejoras de procesos.
- Informar oportunamente sobre retrasos, faltantes documentales y desviaciones, con propuestas concretas para su resolución.

## ? Requisitos esenciales

### Formación

Título profesional universitario en Contaduría Pública, Administración de Empresas, Finanzas o carreras afines. Se valorará formación complementaria en administración de organizaciones, gestión financiera de proyectos o control interno.

### Experiencia

- Mínimo cuatro años de experiencia en gestión administrativa, financiera o contable, con responsabilidades y capacidad demostrada para organizar procesos con autonomía.
- Al menos dos años de experiencia en ONG o proyectos de cooperación internacional, incluyendo seguimiento presupuestario, rendición de cuentas y aplicación de procedimientos de donantes.
- Experiencia comprobable en la administración de una oficina, organización o unidad operativa, incluyendo coordinación de compras, contratos, pagos y documentación de personal.
- Experiencia en preparación de cierres, conciliaciones bancarias, flujos de caja y documentación para auditorías. Se valorará haber participado en la organización o fortalecimiento de procesos administrativos.

### Conocimientos

- Gestión presupuestaria, tesorería, contabilidad de proyectos y control de costos; conocimientos de normativa contable, tributaria y laboral colombiana.
- Compras y contrataciones, gestión documental, administración de personal y control interno en organizaciones sin fines de lucro.

## ? Otras habilidades y experiencias requeridas:

- Excel avanzado y manejo de sistemas contables o de gestión financiera. Se valorará experiencia con Microsoft Dynamics NAV o Business Central.
- Requisitos documentales de donantes y auditorías, elaboración de reportes financieros y análisis de desviaciones.

? AVSI se reserva el derecho de solicitar información a empleadores anteriores sobre cualquier disputa, inquietud relacionada con la protección, investigación o medida disciplinaria, así como de requerir al candidato la presentación de antecedentes penales y civiles, con el fin de evaluar la idoneidad profesional para funciones que impliquen contacto con personas vulnerables, incluidos niños y adultos.

? AVSI aplica el principio de inclusión y no discriminación en su proceso de selección, garantizando la igualdad de oportunidades independientemente del sexo, la edad, el origen étnico, la nacionalidad, la orientación sexual, la identidad de género, el estado civil, las creencias religiosas, la discapacidad o la pertenencia a categorías protegidas.

jobs.title: Consultancy for ECW FER Drought Response Project Baseline & Endline Evaluation
jobs.description:
**TERMS OF REFERENCE**

Baseline and Endline Survey

## 1. Background and Project Context

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organization helping people forced to flee. We protect displaced people and support them as they build a new future. NRC has been operating in Somalia since 2004, providing critical aid for internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees. NRC works in the hard-to-reach areas – helping families get the food, water, shelter and support they urgently need1.

NRC is implementing the ECW-funded project “***Education in Emergencies for Flood-Affected Boys and Girls in Jubaland, Hirshabelle, Puntland, Northeastern and South-West States and Anticipatory Action Pilot Programme for Somalia.”***

The project responds to the compounding impacts of drought and flooding, which have severely disrupted access to education, contributed to school closures and increased dropout rates, weakened teacher retention, and heightened protection risks for children. Prolonged climate shocks have left many schools unable to operate effectively, resulting in widespread learning disruptions and reduced participation in education

The project builds on the achievements of Phase 1, which expanded access to education through the provision of temporary learning spaces, rehabilitation of education facilities, and support to teachers. The current phase will further strengthen access to safe, inclusive, and quality learning opportunities for crisis-affected children through learning materials, teacher support, psychosocial services, safeguarding measures, community engagement, cash assistance, and enhanced education preparedness.

NRC therefore seeks a qualified consultant or firm to undertake a baseline and endline survey. The two survey rounds will establish pre-intervention values, measure change over the implementation period, assess progress against the revised project results framework, and generate evidence for programme adaptation, accountability and final reporting.

The project will deliver a comprehensive package of interventions to achieve the following outcomes:

**Outcome 1**: Increased access to safe and equitable education

**Outcome 2:** Improved quality of teaching and learning

**Outcome 3:** Strengthened government and community capacity for education in emergencies

**Outcome 4:** Children and communities benefit from timely, well-coordinated, and effective responses to drought and emerging hazards, including floods, reducing disruption and enhancing resilience

## 2. Purpose, objectives and scope of the evaluation

**2.1 Purpose**

The purpose of the assignment is to design and implement comparable baseline and endline surveys for the project. The baseline will establish credible starting values for relevant outcome and output indicators and document the initial conditions of targeted learners, households, teachers, schools and education systems. The endline will repeat the core measurements using a consistent methodology to assess change, contribution and achievement against project targets.

## 2.2 Objectives

The overall objective of the baseline survey is to establish the initial conditions against which project performance will be measured, with particular emphasis on outcome-level changes. This survey will provide reference data for assessing the extent to which the project achieves its intended objectives. These include:

- Establish baseline values for all relevant indicators in the project results framework for which primary data are required.
- Assess education access, attendance, retention, participation and barriers to enrolment among targeted girls and boys, including internally displaced and host-community learners and children with disabilities.
- Assess learning-environment conditions, safety, WASH facilities, availability of teaching and learning materials, and school preparedness for drought, flood and displacement.
- Document the starting status of learner well-being, psychosocial support, safeguarding, referral awareness and community accountability mechanisms.
- Assess teacher capacity, motivation, well-being, training exposure and support needs.
- Assess household-level economic and protection barriers to education, including the relevance of cash support and flexible learning pathways.
- Provide disaggregated evidence to refine targeting, implementation priorities and monitoring arrangements.

### 3.2 Endline objectives

- Measure endline values for the same core indicators and assess changes from baseline.
- Assess the extent to which the project improved equitable access, participation, retention, learning continuity, safety and learner well-being.
- Examine the effectiveness and perceived relevance of project support, including learning spaces, materials, teacher support, psychosocial services, cash assistance, community engagement and preparedness actions.
- Assess differential results by sex, age, disability, displacement status, location and education pathway, where sample sizes permit.
- Identify unintended effects, remaining gaps, operational lessons and recommendations for future Education in Emergencies programming.
- Produce defensible evidence for ECW reporting, programme accountability and learning.

## 4. Scope of Work

The consultant or firm will be responsible for the full survey cycle for both rounds, from design through dissemination. The assignment will cover the following tasks:

- Review the ECW project document, revision request, results framework, indicator definitions, monitoring data, Phase 1 reports, safeguarding protocols and relevant assessment tools.
- Develop an inception report and detailed survey protocol, including an indicator measurement matrix, evaluation questions, sampling strategy, field plan, analysis plan, quality-assurance plan and risk-mitigation measures.
- Design or adapt quantitative and qualitative tools for learners, caregivers or households, teachers, head teachers, Community Education Committees, education authorities and relevant project stakeholders.
- Ensure that tools are age-appropriate, gender- and disability-sensitive, conflict-sensitive and suitable for formal and non-formal education settings.
- Translate tools into relevant local languages, back-check translations, program digital forms and conduct field testing and piloting.
- Recruit or support the selection of enumerators, deliver training, test enumerator competency and establish clear supervision and safeguarding arrangements.
- Undertake baseline and endline data collection using comparable tools, sampling procedures and quality controls.
- Clean, label and analyse quantitative and qualitative data; calculate indicator values; and compare baseline and endline findings.
- Facilitate validation sessions and produce concise, practical reports and presentations for NRC, implementing partners and relevant authorities.
- Submit all approved tools, anonymised datasets, syntax, codebooks, transcripts or structured notes, consent materials and supporting documentation.

## 5. Methodology

Applicants should propose a rigorous mixed-methods design suitable for measuring change between baseline and endline while remaining feasible in an operational humanitarian context. The final methodology will be agreed during inception and approved by NRC before data collection.

### 6.1 Quantitative component

- Use a probability-based sampling approach where feasible, with clear justification of the sampling frame, confidence level, margin of error, design effect, anticipated non-response and subgroup requirements.
- Develop a sample that adequately represents the agreed project locations and priority population groups. Stratification should consider location, sex, displacement status, disability and education pathway, as relevant.
- Where a panel design is proposed, include realistic tracking and attrition-management procedures. Where repeated cross-sectional samples are proposed, ensure comparability between survey rounds.
- Apply appropriate weighting and account for the complex sample design in analysis, where required.
- Use the same core indicators, questions, definitions, reference periods and scales at baseline and endline. Any necessary endline changes must be documented and their implications explained.

### 6.2 Qualitative and observational component

- Conduct key informant interviews and focus group discussions with relevant stakeholders, using safe and inclusive approaches.
- Include structured school or learning-space observations to verify infrastructure, WASH, accessibility, materials, safety and preparedness conditions.
- Use qualitative evidence to explain quantitative findings, explore implementation experience and identify unintended outcomes and contextual changes.

### 6.3 Learning assessment

If learning outcomes are included in the approved results framework, the consultant will propose an age- and grade-appropriate assessment approach aligned with the project’s learning objectives and languages of instruction. Administration conditions, scoring, assessor training and comparability across rounds must be standardised. The use of an existing validated tool is preferred where it is appropriate to the context and project indicators.

### 6.4 Data analysis

- Produce descriptive statistics and indicator estimates with appropriate measures of uncertainty.
- Compare baseline and endline results and test the statistical significance of observed differences where the design permits.
- Disaggregate findings by agreed population characteristics while protecting confidentiality and avoiding disclosure risks. Primarily Gender, Age, and Displacement status.
- Triangulate survey, qualitative, observation and available monitoring data.
- Clearly distinguish measured change from claims of attribution. Conclusions about project contribution must be supported by the design and evidence.

## 7. Data Quality, Ethics and Safeguarding

- Obtain informed consent from adult respondents and informed assent from children, together with caregiver consent where required. Participation must be voluntary.
- Apply NRC safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse, data-protection and referral requirements. All team members must sign and comply with relevant codes of conduct.
- Minimise data collection from children and collect only information necessary for the survey. Sensitive questions must be justified and administered by appropriately trained personnel.
- Establish procedures for safe disclosure management and referral. Enumerators must not investigate protection cases or promise services.
- Use secure, access-controlled digital data collection; remove direct identifiers from analysis files; and transfer data using approved channels.
- Build quality controls into programming and fieldwork, including skip logic, range checks, daily review, back-checks, spot checks, supervisor observation and a documented correction protocol.
- Maintain an auditable record of sampling, replacements, non-response, cleaning decisions, derived variables and analysis syntax.
- Obtain any required ethical or administrative approvals before fieldwork.

## 8. Main Deliverables and Timeline

The consultant is expected to be onboarded in November 2026, submit the inception at the end of November 2026, and conduct baseline data collection in December 2026. The draft baseline report is expected in the course of December, followed by a dissemination and validation workshop in early January 2027.

This timeline should be strictly followed. However, slight revisions can be accommodated considering the impact of post-El Niño flooding on accessibility, school operations, and field-level data collection. Final dates will be agreed upon during the development and approval of the inception report and detailed baseline survey workplan.

The consultant will deliver the key outputs specified below using relevant NRC and ECW FER project templates and formats. All deliverables shall be submitted in English, in editable Microsoft Word and PowerPoint formats, as applicable, as well as in final PDF format.

## 9. Suggested Report Structure

- Executive summary
- Project and survey background
- Purpose, objectives and survey questions
- Methodology, sampling and limitations
- Respondent and site profile
- Findings by outcome, indicator and measurement area
- Baseline-endline comparison and subgroup analysis, for the endline report
- Conclusions, lessons and actionable recommendations
- Annexes: evaluation matrix, tools, sampling details, indicator table, quality statement and other technical documentation

## 10. Management and Coordination

The assignment will be managed by NRC through the designated programme and MEAL focal points. NRC will provide available project documents and monitoring information, facilitate coordination with implementing partners and education authorities, review deliverables and consolidate feedback. The consultant will remain responsible for methodological quality, field-team management, logistics included in the agreed financial proposal, data quality, safeguarding compliance, analysis and timely delivery.

Key methodological decisions, tools, sample changes and fieldwork deviations require prior written approval from NRC. The consultant will provide brief progress updates during design and fieldwork and will immediately escalate any safeguarding concern, serious incident, access constraint or data-quality risk through the agreed channels.

## 11. Required Qualifications and Experience

### Essential

- Advanced degree in education, statistics, evaluation, social sciences, development studies, public health or another relevant field.
- At least seven years of relevant experience in evaluations, baseline and endline surveys or large-scale assessments, including in humanitarian or fragile settings.
- Demonstrated expertise in mixed-methods research, probability sampling, digital data collection, statistical analysis and qualitative analysis.
- Strong experience measuring Education in Emergencies outcomes, including access, attendance, retention, inclusion, learning environments, protection or psychosocial well-being.
- Demonstrated experience conducting ethical research involving children and applying safeguarding and data-protection standards.
- Ability to analyse and report disaggregated data and communicate technical findings clearly to programme and non-technical audiences.
- Strong written and spoken English and access to team members with relevant Somali language capacity.

### Desirable

- Previous experience in Somalia or the Horn of Africa.
- Familiarity with ECW-funded programmes, Education Cluster coordination, Anticipatory Action, FLER or cash assistance linked to education.
- Experience with disability-inclusive data collection and child-friendly research methods.
- Experience assessing teacher well-being, MHPSS, safeguarding and education preparedness.

## 12. Application Requirements

- A technical proposal of no more than 10 pages, excluding annexes, describing the applicant’s understanding of the assignment, proposed design, sampling approach, analysis plan, quality controls, safeguarding measures, team structure and workplan for both rounds.
- A financial proposal showing professional fees and all anticipated costs for baseline and endline activities, with assumptions clearly stated.
- CVs of the lead consultant and key team members, identifying their proposed roles.
- Two examples of comparable baseline, endline or evaluation reports and contact details for two professional references.
- A brief statement on availability for both survey rounds and capacity to mobilise in the target locations.
- Disclosure of any actual or potential conflict of interest.

## 14. Duration

The assignment comprises two linked survey rounds. The baseline will be completed by January 2027, and the endline will be completed by end of July 2027 to allow time for validation and integration into the final reporting. Applicants should propose the number of working days required for each round and identify any remote and in-country inputs. The assignment may be home-based with travel to project locations, subject to access, security and NRC approval.

## 15. Confidentiality, Data Ownership and Use

All tools, raw and processed data, analysis files, reports, presentations and other products prepared under this assignment will remain the property of NRC and the project. The consultant must maintain confidentiality, comply with NRC data-protection and safeguarding requirements, and obtain written approval before sharing, publishing or reusing any assignment-related material. No identifiable respondent information may be included in reports or handed over through unsecured channels.

jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Hygiene Promoter is responsible for implementing hygiene promotion and community awareness-raising activities to improve hygiene practices and reduce the risk of waterborne and sanitation-related diseases among targeted individuals, households, and communities. The position aims to promote positive hygiene behaviours, improve community knowledge of disease prevention, and encourage the safe use, handling, storage, and conservation of water, as well as appropriate sanitation and personal hygiene practices.

The Hygiene Promoter will conduct structured hygiene awareness sessions using approved hygiene promotion materials, methodologies, and key messages. Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

1. **Distribution Preparation and Implementation 30%**

- Hygiene Promotion Activities
- Conduct hygiene awareness sessions for community members.
- Promote handwashing, safe water handling, sanitation, and personal hygiene.
- Share key hygiene messages with households and community groups.

1. **Community Engagement and Participation 25%**

- Engage with community members and encourage participation in hygiene activities.
- Identify hygiene needs and challenges within the community.
- Encourage women, children, older people, and persons with disabilities to participate.

1. **Monitoring and Reporting 20%**

- Record attendance at awareness sessions and community activities.
- Collect basic information on hygiene needs and practices.
- Prepare simple activity reports and share them with the supervisor.

1. **Compliance, Safety and Safeguarding 10%**

- Follow organizational policies, safeguarding, and PSEA requirements.
- Treat all community members with respect and without discrimination.
- Report complaints, protection concerns, and safety issues to the supervisor.
- Participate in relevant briefings, training sessions, and coordination meetings as requested.

1. **Distribution and Demonstrations 15%**

- Support the distribution of hygiene kits and other hygiene materials when required.
- Demonstrate proper handwashing and safe water storage practices.
- Explain how to use hygiene items correctly.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**
- Previous experience in hygiene promotion, community mobilization, or humanitarian projects is desirable.
- Experience conducting awareness sessions or working directly with community members is an advantage.
- Experience working with vulnerable communities affected by conflict or displacement is desirable.
- Ability to communicate effectively with community members and work as part of a team.
2. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- A minimum of secondary education (high school diploma) is required.
- Training in hygiene promotion, public health, WASH, or community mobilization is an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Basic knowledge of personal hygiene, handwashing, safe water handling, and sanitation.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to conduct awareness sessions and encourage community participation.
- Basic skills in recording attendance and preparing activity reports.
- Understanding of safeguarding, PSEA, confidentiality, and Do No Harm principles.
- Ability to work in the field and follow instructions from the supervisor.

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

- Arabic

jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Water Quality Assistant supports the implementation, monitoring, and documentation of water-quality activities within the project, ensuring that water-quality monitoring is conducted in accordance with approved workplans, established technical procedures, and relevant water-quality standards. The position assists with routine water sampling, field testing, monitoring of water sources and supply facilities, recording and reporting test results, and identifying and promptly communicating potential water-quality risks. The Water Quality Assistant works closely with the WASH Officer, relevant technical staff, partner teams, and community representatives to support access to safe water and contribute to the effective monitoring of water quality across project locations.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Water-Quality Testing and Monitoring 35%**

- Conduct routine water-quality monitoring at designated water sources, water supply stations, distribution points, and other project locations, according to the approved monitoring schedule.
- Collect water samples and conduct basic field tests in accordance with established procedures and technical instructions.
- Conduct residual chlorine testing and other assigned water-quality checks using approved equipment and testing methods.
- Ensure that water samples are collected, handled, labeled, stored, transported, and tested appropriately, following applicable procedures.
- Record test results accurately using approved monitoring forms and tools.
- Follow the testing frequency, sampling locations, and procedures established by the WASH Officer or designated technical staff.
- Report any abnormal results, suspected contamination, or potential water-quality risks immediately to the supervisor.

**Field Visits and Water-System Follow-up 25%**

- Conduct regular field visits to assigned water supply facilities, water points, and distribution locations to support water-quality monitoring.
- Observe water-system conditions and report visible concerns that may affect water quality, including damaged infrastructure, unsafe storage, potential contamination sources, or inadequate chlorination where relevant.
- Support the WASH Officer in following up on identified water-quality issues and monitoring the status of corrective actions.
- Assist with monitoring water-treatment and disinfection processes, as assigned and in accordance with technical guidance.
- Verify that water-quality testing equipment and supplies are available, functional, and appropriately maintained.
- Report equipment malfunctions, shortages of testing materials, and any constraints affecting monitoring activities.
- Follow organizational safety and security procedures during field visits.

**Equipment, Supplies and Quality-Control Support 15%**

- Maintain and organize water-quality testing equipment, sample containers, reagents, consumables, and other assigned materials.
- Check the condition, expiry dates, storage requirements, and availability of testing materials in accordance with manufacturer instructions and established procedures.
- Support routine equipment checks, cleaning, calibration, and maintenance where trained and authorized to do so.
- Maintain records of equipment use, stock levels, consumption, and replenishment needs.
- Follow appropriate procedures for handling, storing, transporting, and disposing of testing materials and waste.
- Inform the supervisor of damaged equipment, expired reagents, stock shortages, or quality-control concerns.
- Support quality-assurance procedures and participate in technical briefings or training as required

**Data Management, Reporting and Coordination 15%**

- Maintain complete and accurate records of water samples, sampling locations, dates, test methods, results, and observations.
- Submit water-quality monitoring forms and field updates to the WASH Officer within agreed deadlines.
- Support the compilation and review of water-quality monitoring data to identify unusual results, recurring concerns, and trends requiring technical follow-up.
- Immediately communicate results that fall outside applicable limits or indicate potential contamination through established reporting channels.
- Coordinate with relevant WASH staff, partner teams, and facility personnel to arrange sampling and monitoring visits.
- Support the preparation of routine monitoring summaries and contribute information for project reports as required.
- Maintain the confidentiality and integrity of records and ensure that data is stored and shared in accordance with organizational procedures

**Compliance, Safety and Community Engagement 10%**

- Follow approved water-quality monitoring procedures, relevant technical guidance, and applicable organizational requirements.
- Use appropriate personal protective equipment and comply with safety procedures during sampling, testing, and field visits.
- Communicate with facility staff and community representatives regarding sampling arrangements and access to monitoring locations, as assigned.
- Report potential sources of contamination, community concerns regarding water quality, and suspected waterborne disease risks to the supervisor through established channels.
- Support awareness activities on safe water handling and storage when requested and within the scope of the position.
- Apply safeguarding, accountability, inclusion, and Do No Harm principles in all field activities.
- Promptly escalate safeguarding, PSEA, security, or other serious concerns through established organizational procedures.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**
- At least 1–2 years of relevant experience in water-quality monitoring, WASH programming, water sampling, laboratory support, environmental health, or a related field.
- Experience conducting basic water-quality tests and maintaining accurate monitoring records is desirable.
- Experience working in humanitarian or development projects, particularly in communities affected by conflict or displacement, is an advantage.
- Experience handling field-testing equipment, water samples, or monitoring supplies is desirable.
- Experience working with community representatives, water-system operators, or partner organizations is an advantage.
2. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**
- Bachelor's degree or in Water and Sanitation, Environmental Health, Public Health, Civil or Environmental Engineering, Environmental Sciences, Agri engineering or another relevant field.
- Training in water-quality testing, water sampling, chlorination, laboratory safety, or WASH standards is an advantage.
3. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**
- Basic knowledge of water-quality parameters, sampling procedures, and field-testing methods.
- Familiarity with residual chlorine testing and other relevant water-quality monitoring procedures.
- Understanding of safe water handling, water contamination risks, and basic water-treatment principles.
- Ability to operate and care for water-quality testing equipment in accordance with training and manufacturer instructions.
- Good data recording, documentation, and reporting skills.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to identify and report abnormal results.
- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Ability to work independently on assigned routine tasks while following technical instructions and escalating issues appropriately.
- Basic computer skills and familiarity with Microsoft Office or digital data collection tools are desirable.
4. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

- Fluent in Arabic and good understanding in English terms related to WASH

## **General Information**

**Position Title**

Civil Engineer

**Job Category**

Engineering & Infrastructure

## **Job Highlight**

Drive high-quality infrastructure delivery by providing technical expertise, supervising work, and ensuring compliance with design and safety standards.

## **About the Region**

The Asia Pacific Regional Office, based in Bangkok, Thailand, provides strategic leadership and oversight for UNOPS operations across 17 countries, ensuring high performance, operational excellence, and alignment with organizational goals. Operations currently span Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, Nepal, Papua New Guinea, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Pacific Islands. Across these countries, we work closely with key stakeholders to strengthen partnerships and maximize impact through five main operating units: Afghanistan (AFCO), Myanmar (MMCO), South Asia Multi-Country Office (SAMCO), East Asia and Pacific Multi-Country Office (EAPMCO), and the Asia Regional Health Cluster (ARHC). Through these entities, we provide agile, client-focused service delivery across diverse sectors - including infrastructure, health, procurement, and project management - supporting the implementation of sustainable development solutions across the region.

## **About the Country/Multi-Country Office**

The East Asia and Pacific Multi-Country Office (EAPMCO), headquartered in Bangkok, supports UNOPS operations across 24 countries in Southeast Asia, Northeast Asia, and the Pacific. Established in January 2023, EAPMCO provides strategic direction, operational support, and quality assurance to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of projects across its portfolio. EAPMCO implements initiatives in priority areas such as energy transition, climate change, and sustainable development, drawing on UNOPS' core expertise in human resources, procurement, infrastructure, fund management, and programme management.

## **About the Project Office**

Established in 2018, the Pacific Operations Cluster supports the delivery of infrastructure, capacity building, programme management, and procurement services across 12 Pacific Small Island Developing States (PSIDS). UNOPS partners with governments and development agencies to deliver tailored solutions aligned with national development priorities. Drawing on its core expertise in infrastructure, procurement, and project and programme management, UNOPS helps PSIDS address the challenges of small population size, geographic isolation, and heightened vulnerability to climate change. UNOPS projects in the Pacific contribute to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by strengthening health systems, promoting sustainable consumption and production, enhancing climate resilience and coastal protection, and supporting institutional development and local governance.

## **About the Group**

In June 2023, the Government of Australia, represented by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), and the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS), executed a grant agreement, the Australia Kiribati Climate Security Initiative (AKSI), to address the need for practical and sustainable solutions to enhance coastal resilience in Kiribati. The objective is to implement high-quality, inclusive, and resilient coastal protection solutions, across three sites in Tarawa, to improve the resilience of Kiribati to the impacts of climate change. The project seeks to engage a Civil Engineer based in Tarawa to support the implementation of the project as detailed below.

## **Job Specific Context**

In June 2023, the Government of Australia, represented by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), and the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS), executed a grant agreement, the Australia Kiribati Climate Security Initiative (AKSI), to address the need for practical and sustainable solutions to enhance coastal resilience in Kiribati. The objective is to implement high-quality, inclusive, and resilient coastal protection solutions, across three sites in Tarawa, to improve the resilience of Kiribati to the impacts of climate change. The project seeks to engage a Civil Engineer based in Tarawa to support the implementation of the project as detailed below.

This vacancy is for a parental cover (temporary assignment.)

## **Role Purpose**

The Civil Engineer plays a vital role in the day-to-day operations and successful delivery of infrastructure projects within defined time, cost, quality, scope, risk and benefit parameters.

Working closely with the Project Manager and project teams, the Civil Engineer performs a broad range of tasks, including assisting in project assessments, preparing bills of quantity (BoQS) and bid documents, supervising works on-site, and conducting technical evaluations to ensure compliance with design standards, quality assurance, occupational health and safety, and environmental management requirements.

The incumbent provides technical expertise, promoting best practices in construction management and ensuring high standards of consistency and quality in project outputs. Through these responsibilities, the Civil Engineer contributes to the achievement of organizational performance goals and overall project success.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

**Project Planning and Implementation**

- Support the preparation of project implementation plans, BoQs, cost estimates and schedules.
- Provide technical input during feasibility studies, needs assessments, and design development.
- Assist in the preparation of tender documents, bid evaluations, and contract award documentation.
- Ensure compliance with technical specifications, contractual provisions, and organizational standards throughout project execution.

**Construction and Supervision and Quality Assurance**

- Supervise day-to-day construction activities to ensure timely, cost-effective and high-quality delivery.
- Verify material quantities, monitor site activities, and ensure health, safety, social and environmental (HSSE) compliance on all work sites.
- Oversee contractor performance, including site safety, environmental standards, and quality control.
- Liaise with contractors, consultants and engineering teams to resolve technical issues and support effective construction management.

**Monitoring, Reporting and Compliance**

- Monitor progress against key performance indicators (KPIs) and project success criteria. Contribute data and analysis for reporting.
- Prepare and submit progress reports, site monitoring documentation, and handover/close-out reports.
- Ensure compliance with organizational systems, reporting requirements, and accountability standards.
- Identify risks and issues, recommend corrective actions, and track remedial measures to maintain delivery within scope, budget and schedule.

**Stakeholder Coordination**

- Collaborate with project managers, procurement teams, and other stakeholders to facilitate smooth project implementation.
- Represent UNOPS in field activities, stakeholder meetings, and technical fora as directed/authorized.
- Support engagement with local authorities, contractors, and beneficiaries to strengthen coordination and project ownership.

**Knowledge Building and Sharing**

- Support the organization, facilitation and delivery of training and learning sessions on civil engineering project topics.
- Participate in knowledge-sharing initiatives and Communities of Practice (CoPs), contributing insights and lessons learned.
- Conduct research on civil engineering project-related topics and contribute to the drafting of reports, summaries and briefing notes.

## **Skills**

Civil Engineering, Project Engineering, Project Implementation, Project Resource Management, Project Team Management

## **Competencies**

Treats all individuals with respect; responds sensitively to differences and encourages others to do the same. Upholds organisational and ethical norms. Maintains high standards of trustworthiness. Role model for diversity and inclusion.

Acts as a positive role model contributing to the team spirit. Collaborates and supports the development of others. **For people managers only:** Acts as positive leadership role model, motivates, directs and inspires others to succeed, utilizing appropriate leadership styles.

Demonstrates understanding of the impact of own role on all partners and always puts the end beneficiary first. Builds and maintains strong external relationships and is a competent partner for others (if relevant to the role).

Efficiently establishes an appropriate course of action for self and/or others to accomplish a goal. Actions lead to total task accomplishment through concern for quality in all areas. Sees opportunities and takes the initiative to act on them. Understands that responsible use of resources maximizes our impact on our beneficiaries.

Open to change and flexible in a fast paced environment. Effectively adapts own approach to suit changing circumstances or requirements. Reflects on experiences and modifies own behavior. Performance is consistent, even under pressure. Always pursues continuous improvements.

Evaluates data and courses of action to reach logical, pragmatic decisions. Takes an unbiased, rational approach with calculated risks. Applies innovation and creativity to problem-solving.

Expresses ideas or facts in a clear, concise and open manner. Communication indicates a consideration for the feelings and needs of others. Actively listens and proactively shares knowledge. Handles conflict effectively, by overcoming differences of opinion and finding common ground.

## **Education Requirements**

**Required**

- Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Structural Engineering or related fields with 4 years of relevant experience OR
- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in any of the above or related fields with 2 years of relevant experience is required.

**Desired**

- A recognized professional certification or membership in a civil engineering association, at the national or international level, is desirable.

## **Experience Requirements**

**Required**

- Relevant experience is work in civil engineering, structural works, construction technology, construction supervision and monitoring, or related areas.

**Desired**

- Experience of working in multicultural environments or UN system organizations in a developing country is desired.
- Experience in development or humanitarian contexts is desired.

English Fluent Required

We strive to sustain and strengthen this diversity, fostering an inclusive working environment where all personnel are treated with respect and have equal access to opportunities.

We are committed to a fair and transparent selection process and welcome diverse perspectives, including those of women, indigenous and racialized communities, individuals of diverse gender identities and sexual orientations, and persons with disabilities.

To uphold these standards, background checks are conducted for all final candidates to help ensure that individuals with a history of such conduct are not hired. By applying for a position with UNOPS, candidates acknowledge and consent to these verification processes.

jobs.title: Protection Assistant - 1 Tal Abyad, 1 Ras Al-Ayn
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Protection Assistant supports the day-to-day implementation of protection activities within the project, ensuring that interventions are delivered in a safe, inclusive, dignified, and conflict-sensitive manner and in accordance with approved project objectives, workplans, protection standards, and organizational policies.

The position assists with activity preparation and implementation, community engagement, protection awareness sessions, monitoring, data collection, referrals, and reporting. The Protection Assistant works closely with the Protection Officer, Project Coordinator, protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and other relevant project staff to identify protection concerns, support access to available services, and ensure that children, adults, and vulnerable groups can participate safely and meaningfully in project activities.

The position is also responsible for maintaining accurate activity records, sharing field observations and emerging concerns with the relevant supervisor, and adhering to organizational requirements related to safeguarding, confidentiality, informed consent, accountability, and the protection of sensitive information.

Activities will address relevant hygiene priorities, including handwashing with soap at critical times, safe drinking water handling and storage, household cleanliness, environmental hygiene, sanitation practices, menstrual hygiene management where relevant and appropriate, and prevention of waterborne diseases. The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Protection Programme Implementation and Field Support**

- Support the implementation of protection activities in line with approved project plans, the DIP, performance framework, protection standards, and humanitarian principles.
- Assist protection facilitators, volunteers, and community structures in organizing and delivering protection activities.
- Support the identification of protection needs, risks, vulnerabilities, and barriers to accessing services among targeted communities.
- Assist in adapting activities to the local context and the specific needs of children, women, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable groups.
- Promote safe, inclusive, gender-sensitive, child-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive approaches during activity implementation.
- Ensure that protection activities are conducted in accordance with Do No Harm, confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, participation, and non-discrimination principles.
- Report implementation challenges, emerging needs, and any protection concerns to the Protection Officer/Project Coordinator in a timely manner.

**Protection Monitoring, Risk Identification and Referrals:**

- Support the identification and documentation of protection risks, concerns, trends, and barriers affecting children, adults, and vulnerable groups.
- Assist in conducting protection assessments, community consultations, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and other data collection activities.
- Identify individuals who may require additional or specialized protection support and report concerns through established internal procedures.
- Support safe referrals to relevant service providers through established referral pathways, with informed consent and in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
- Maintain and regularly update information on available protection services and referral mechanisms.
- Follow up on referrals within the scope of the position and in coordination with the Protection Officer, while respecting confidentiality and data protection requirements.
- Immediately communicate urgent protection concerns and emerging risks to the Protection Officer/Project Coordinator.
- Support community awareness activities on available protection services, rights, and referral mechanisms.

**Activity Monitoring, Quality Assurance and Capacity Building Support**

- Support the preparation and implementation of protection activity plans, schedules, and field implementation arrangements.
- Monitor activity participation, coverage, and progress against agreed protection indicators and targets.
- Conduct regular field visits to follow up on activity implementation and identify operational challenges.
- Support the collection, verification, and organization of protection-related data and ensure that records are accurate and submitted on time.
- Report implementation gaps, quality concerns, and emerging needs to the Protection Officer and support the implementation of agreed corrective actions.
- Assist in identifying capacity-building needs among protection facilitators, volunteers, partners, and community structures.
- Support the organization and delivery of training, coaching, awareness sessions, and community-based activities on relevant protection topics, including protection principles, safeguarding, PSEA, referral mechanisms, and safe programming.
- Apply technical guidance and feedback received from the Protection Officer to improve the quality of field implementation.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement:**

- Coordinate with relevant Protection Sector/Sub-Sector actors, authorities, partners, community representatives, service providers, and other stakeholders as required.
- Participate in relevant protection coordination meetings, working groups, technical discussions, and inter-agency coordination mechanisms.
- Engage with communities to understand protection concerns, priorities, barriers, and feedback and ensure that programme responses are appropriate and context-sensitive.
- Support community-based protection mechanisms and promote meaningful participation of women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, and other potentially marginalized groups.
- Coordinate with other project sectors to ensure protection is appropriately mainstreamed across programme interventions, including Education, WASH, FSL, PSS, and other relevant sectors.
- Promote safe, dignified, accessible, and inclusive programme approaches and support teams to identify and mitigate protection risks.
- Support the identification and strengthening of referral pathways and linkages with specialized services

**Reporting, Documentation and Learning:**

- Prepare regular protection activity updates and contribute to project reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other programme documentation.
- Maintain comprehensive and secure records of protection activities, including attendance, training, monitoring, assessments, community consultations, referrals, and field visits, in accordance with data protection requirements.
- Document protection trends, challenges, achievements, good practices, lessons learned, and success stories while ensuring confidentiality and protection of sensitive information.
- Support the implementation of community feedback and response mechanisms and ensure relevant protection-related feedback is appropriately followed up.
- Support the preparation and review of protection-related proposals, budgets, activity plans, indicators, and project documents as required.
- Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality, monitoring, accountability, and learning processes.
- Ensure protection documentation is maintained in accordance with organizational, donor, safeguarding, and data protection requirements.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Professional Experience**

- At least 1–2 years of relevant experience in protection, humanitarian, development, or community-based programming, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Experience implementing or monitoring protection, child protection, community-based protection, protection monitoring, awareness-raising, or referral activities is desirable.
- Experience working with children, families, displaced populations, vulnerable groups, and communities affected by conflict or displacement.
- Experience providing technical support, coaching, mentoring, or capacity building to staff, volunteers, community structures, or partner organizations.
- Experience working with Protection Sector/Sub-Sector coordination mechanisms, referral networks, local authorities, service providers, or other humanitarian actors is an advantage.

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, Law, International Development, Social Sciences, or another relevant field.
- Additional qualifications or training in Protection, Child Protection, GBV, PSEA, Safeguarding, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related areas are an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications**

- Good knowledge of Protection programming principles and approaches relevant to humanitarian and/or development contexts.
- Understanding of barriers to protection access and participation, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized children.
- Knowledge of child safeguarding, child participation, inclusion, gender, and conflict-sensitive programming.
- Good monitoring, data collection, analysis, and reporting skills.
- Strong communication, facilitation, interpersonal, and coordination skills.
- Ability to work effectively with partners, community representatives, education

1. **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

Non

1. **Physical Requirements**

Non

1. **Language Requirements**

Arabic and basic English is desirable

jobs.title: Project Officer (Health) - Hasaka
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Job purpose:**

The Health Officer is responsible for the technical follow-up, coordination, monitoring, and quality assurance of health and nutrition activities implemented through partner organizations under the project, ensuring that services are delivered effectively, safely, inclusively, and in line with approved project objectives, workplans, relevant health and nutrition standards, and donor requirements. The position supports the implementation of primary healthcare services through two fixed health facilities in Ras Al Ain and Tell Abiad, with a focus on outpatient consultations, reproductive health, maternal and child health, preventive and therapeutic nutrition services, and community health and nutrition education.

The Health Officer works closely with the Project Coordinator, implementing partners, relevant health and nutrition technical teams, MEAL colleagues, and other stakeholders to monitor partner performance, identify implementation gaps, strengthen service quality, and ensure that health and nutrition activities respond to the needs of vulnerable communities. The position also supports capacity building for project and partner staff on relevant health topics, including infection prevention and control (IPC), reproductive health (RH), antimicrobial resistance (AMR), non-communicable diseases (NCDs), community management of acute malnutrition (CMAM), and infant and young child feeding (IYCF). The Health Officer contributes to accurate reporting, accountability, coordination, and evidence-based programme improvement while ensuring that clinical services and technical decisions remain the responsibility of qualified and authorized health professionals within the implementing partner facilities.

The Hygiene Promoter will adapt communication approaches according to age, gender, disability, literacy level, cultural context, and the specific needs of the target population.

The Hygiene Promoter will work closely with the WASH team, community mobilizers, local authorities, community leaders, health actors, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that hygiene promotion activities are inclusive, safe, culturally appropriate, and aligned with approved project objectives and technical guidance. The position will also support the identification of hygiene-related concerns and barriers within communities and communicate relevant findings to the supervisor for appropriate follow-up

**Major Responsibilities:**

1. **Health Programme Implementation and Partner Coordination 30%**

- Health Programme Implementation and Partner Coordination
- Support the planning, coordination, and follow-up of health and nutrition activities implemented by partner organizations in the two fixed health facilities in Ras Al Ain and Tell Abiad.
- Maintain regular communication with implementing partners to follow up on approved workplans, activity schedules, service delivery, staffing, operational challenges, and progress against agreed targets.
- Conduct regular monitoring visits to partner-supported health facilities and community activity locations to assess operational status, service availability, implementation progress, and compliance with agreed programme requirements.
- Review partner implementation plans and identify potential delays, gaps in service delivery, and resource or operational constraints requiring follow-up.
- Support partners in addressing implementation challenges and coordinate with the Project Coordinator and relevant technical focal points to facilitate timely solutions.
- Monitor the availability and continuity of planned primary healthcare, maternal and child health, and nutrition services through partner facilities, escalating service interruptions and significant gaps.
- Ensure that health and nutrition activities are implemented in accordance with the approved project design, Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP), performance framework, budget, and donor requirements.
- Promote equitable and non-discriminatory access to services for women, men, girls, boys, persons with disabilities, displaced populations, and other vulnerable groups.

1. **Primary Healthcare and Maternal and Child Health Service Quality Monitoring 20%**

- Monitor the delivery of outpatient primary healthcare consultations through the two partner-supported fixed health facilities, ensuring progress against agreed service delivery targets.
- Follow up with partners on the availability and continuity of planned primary healthcare services, including maternal and child health and reproductive health services, within the scope of the approved project.
- Review service utilization data, disaggregated by sex, age, and disability where applicable, to identify access barriers, underserved groups, service utilization trends, and potential gaps in coverage.
- Monitor partner compliance with agreed health service standards, relevant clinical protocols, patient safety requirements, and organizational and donor expectations through observation, documentation review, and coordination with qualified health professionals.
- Follow up on partner staff capacity-building activities related to IPC, RH, AMR, NCDs, and other relevant health topics, as identified in the project workplan.
- Support partners in identifying service quality gaps and developing appropriate follow-up actions, referring clinical or specialized technical matters to qualified health professionals and designated technical focal points.
- Monitor the documentation of consultations through the relevant health information systems, including the SAMS Health Information System (HIS), and follow up on missing, inconsistent, or incomplete records.
- Escalate significant service interruptions, patient safety concerns, or other issues that may compromise access to or the quality of healthcare services.

1. **Nutrition Programme Monitoring and Technical Follow-Up 20%**

- Monitor the implementation of preventive and therapeutic nutrition activities delivered through implementing partners at facility and community levels.
- Follow up on partner delivery of CMAM services, including screening, identification, admission, referral, treatment, and follow-up of children with moderate and severe acute malnutrition (MAM and SAM), in accordance with approved protocols.
- Monitor the implementation and quality of IYCF counselling, including counselling for caregivers on appropriate infant and young child feeding practices, within the scope of the project.
- Track the implementation of nutrition screening activities using mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) for children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), as applicable to the approved programme.
- Review partner nutrition activity data, including screening records, admission registers, IYCF registration records, CMAM databases, and relevant reports, to monitor progress against targets and identify inconsistencies or service delivery gaps.
- Follow up on partner capacity-building activities on CMAM, IYCF, and other relevant nutrition topics, ensuring that training activities and supporting documentation are maintained.
- Monitor health and nutrition education sessions delivered by trained community health workers (CHWs), including session coverage, participation, documentation, and relevance to identified community needs.
- Coordinate with partner nutrition focal points and relevant technical specialists to address identified gaps and ensure that cases requiring specialized support are managed through established clinical and referral pathways.
- Ensure that nutrition-related data is reviewed and reported accurately, with appropriate disaggregation and confidentiality safeguards

1. **Capacity Building and Technical Support to Partners 20%**

- Support the identification of training and capacity-building needs among implementing partner health and nutrition staff and relevant project personnel.
- Coordinate with qualified technical specialists and partners to facilitate training on relevant health topics, including IPC, RH, AMR, NCDs, CMAM, IYCF, and other agreed topics.
- Follow up on training plans, participant attendance, completion records, training reports, and certificates, where applicable.
- Monitor the application of relevant training content through partner follow-up discussions, field monitoring, documentation review, and feedback from technical focal points.
- Support knowledge sharing and the dissemination of approved technical guidance, tools, and reference materials to relevant partner and project staff.
- Identify additional capacity gaps and communicate recommendations to the Project Coordinator and relevant technical teams.
- Support partners in strengthening documentation, reporting, and monitoring practices related to health and nutrition service delivery.

1. **Monitoring, Data Quality, Reporting, and Documentation 10%**

- Monitor progress against agreed health and nutrition indicators, targets, workplans, and milestones, maintaining an updated overview of implementation progress.
- Collect, review, verify, and consolidate health and nutrition data and supporting documentation submitted by implementing partners.
- Follow up on key programme indicators, including outpatient consultations, staff trained on health topics, nutrition staff trained, IYCF counselling sessions, MAM and SAM admissions, MUAC screenings, and health and nutrition education activities.
- Review relevant sources of verification, including partner workplans, health facility operationality trackers, digital patient records through the SAMS HIS, monthly verification reports (MVRs), attendance sheets, training reports, CMAM databases, IYCF records, and activity reports.
- Coordinate with MEAL colleagues to support data quality assurance, verification, indicator tracking, monitoring visits, and other relevant monitoring processes.
- Prepare regular health and nutrition activity updates and contribute to project progress reports, donor reports, situation updates, and other required programme documentation.
- Document achievements, implementation challenges, lessons learned, good practices, and recommendations for programme improvement.
- Ensure that partner reports and supporting evidence are submitted accurately and on time, and promptly follow up on missing or inconsistent information.
- Maintain appropriate confidentiality and ensure that personal and sensitive patient information is handled in accordance with applicable data protection and health information management requirements

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

1. **Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Health Sciences, Nursing, Medicine, Nutrition, Midwifery, or another relevant health-related field.
- Additional training or certification in public health, primary healthcare, reproductive health, maternal and child health, nutrition, CMAM, IYCF, IPC, or health programme management is an advantage.

1. **Preferred Knowledge, experience and skills**

- At least 2–3 years of relevant experience in health, public health, nutrition, humanitarian response, or health programme coordination, preferably with an NGO or humanitarian organization.
- Good understanding of primary health and nutrition services delivery and programme implementation in humanitarian and early recovery contexts.
- Experience in monitoring and coordinating primary health and nutrition projects including maternal and child health, reproductive health, community health, and nutrition activities.
- High coordination skills for health projects including coordinating with health authorities, health service providers, local partners, or relevant humanitarian coordination mechanisms is desirable.
- Experience in following up on activity implementation, workplans, service delivery, reporting, and agreed programme targets.
- Understanding of nutrition programming, including CMAM, MAM and SAM management, IYCF counselling, MUAC screening, and community-level nutrition interventions.
- Experience supporting training, capacity building, or technical follow-up for health and nutrition staff is an advantage.
- Experience in managing medical stocks at primary health settings including pharmaceuticals and other medical supplies.
- Good knowledge of health data collection and analysis including the use of health information systems and relevant programme databases.
- Experience reviewing health and nutrition data, maintaining programme documentation, and contributing to donor or project reports.
- Strong communication, interpersonal, coordination, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams
- Good computer skills, particularly Microsoft Word and Excel; familiarity with mobile data collection and reporting tools is an advantage.

Non

Non
