***Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP / MBBR / ABR) Implementation:***

- Finalize and validate the complete technical engineering design for the hospital wastewater treatment system.
- Oversee technical contractors and suppliers during construction, supervising civil works (reinforced concrete slabs) and the installation and commissioning of the MBBR (Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor) unit.
- Lead the design, tendering, and construction of the site-wide wastewater network, including Anaerobic Baffled Reactors (ABRs), lifting pump stations, grease traps, septic tanks, and soak-away systems.

***Water Desalination & Potabilization System Project:***

- Lead the complete design, tendering, and contracting process for the site desalination and water potabilization plant (water softening + reverse osmosis / RO).
- Ensure that maintenance access, availability of critical spare parts, electrical power quality, and long-term operational sustainability are fully integrated into the design from the initial engineering phase.
- Prepare complete tender documentation, lead technical evaluations of supplier bids, and support final contract awards and vendor management.

***WATSAN Design for New Buildings & Extensions:***

- Develop, review, and validate comprehensive WATSAN engineering designs, plumbing schematics, and layout plans for the Labor Room, Newborn Ward, Laundry Facility, and other new infrastructure projects.
- Rethink and upgrade the stormwater/runoff drainage system across the hospital compound.
- Lead technical discussions with medical, Infection Prevention Control, and construction teams to ensure alignment with clinical protocols, hygiene constraints, and operational needs.

***Handover, Maintenance Strategy & System Exploitation Transfer:***

- Handover Dossiers & As-Built Plans: Establish complete handover documentation, As-Built drawings, pipe/valve schematics, and operating manuals for all newly built WATSAN infrastructure.
- Maintenance & Operations Plan: Develop preventative and corrective maintenance protocols, maintenance schedules, buffer stock lists (spare parts, chemical reagents, filters, pump replacement kits), and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
- Staff Capacity Building: Formulate and execute a structured training and mentoring program for national Watsan staff, logistics technicians, and hospital maintenance teams covering daily operation, monitoring, and safety measures.
- Commissioning & Transition: Oversee step-by-step testing and commissioning phases prior to final user takeover to ensure a smooth, safe, and fully documented transfer of ownership.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- Academic background in civil engineering, Sanitary/Environmental engineering or an equivalent relevant training
- Previous experience in technical aspects of water and sanitation works like hospital plumbing, wastewater treatment plant/desalination and construction
- Hands on experience in an emergency project humanitarian or international development setting with a minimum of 6-months
- Desirable experience in or familiar with implementing and promoting the use of two or more of the following activities (water supply, excreta disposal, waste and wastewater management, vector control, and dead bodies management) in two or more different contexts (conflicts, natural disasters, refugee/Internal Displaced People camps, etc.)
- Desirable experience or background in public health
- Fluency in written and spoken French and Englisch (B2 – C1)
- Computer literacy
- Ability to work in a team, cultural sensitivity, excellent organizational and improvisational skills, and a high level of mental and physical resilience
- Willingness to work in accordance with Médecins Sans Frontières humanitarian principles, charter and mission statement

***What do we offer***

- Expected starting date: 01 February 2027
- Location: Port-au-Prince, Haiti
- Contract type and duration: Fixed term contract – Full time, 6 months
- Salary according to MSF mobile salary grid
- Round-trip transportation to and from assignment and room & board during assignment
- A comprehensive insurance package, including health and emergency evacuation insurance
- Holiday leave (depending on project)
- No family position

The major part of our projects are taking place in acute or chronic crisis areas and instable contexts. Learn more about security management within our organization [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SI7MsR-helE) and about working in acute conflict [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oNXdGhxYDeM). The living conditions in the project can be challenging due to isolation, rough climate, security and set up of the living quarters. Learn more about working and living in the projects [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mc-njOPX-K4).

jobs.title: Collective Portfolio Manager
jobs.description:
**Location:** Any MSF office\*

**Contract:** Permanent contract at 100%

**Starting date:** 01st of February 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 03rd of December 2026 - We reserve the right to close this position once suitable candidates have been identified.

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.*

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**Context**

MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF movement and implements international projects and initiatives as requested. In 2026, MSF began a new six-year strategic cycle — the Strategic Planning and Resource Cycle (SPARC) — which replaces the previous Resources-Sharing Agreement (RSA4). SPARC brings together movement-wide priorities, coordinated decision-making, shared accountability and collective investment stewardship across the MSF movement.

Within this framework, the Collective Portfolio is a core mechanism for translating SPARC ambitions into coherent, prioritised and monitorable movement-level investments. It brings together the Common Strategic Priorities Portfolio and other collective portfolio components, enabling the movement to assess strategic fit, sequencing, interdependencies, absorptive capacity, risk and value across a complex set of initiatives. The SPARC Interoperability priority in particular cuts across all other priorities and provides an enabling approach that shapes portfolio implementation and coherence.

The Collective Portfolio Manager is the senior role responsible for holding together the diverse components of the Collective Portfolio during SPARC implementation. The role enables collective ownership, strengthens evidence-based steering, and reinforces accountability for results, resource choices and delivery against SPARC Goals and Principles. It operates across MSF’s decentralised governance and executive environment, working closely with the International Office, Executive Committees, the SPARC Steering Committee, the Portfolio Committee, finance stakeholders, content owners and senior leaders across the movement.

As a member of the International Office management environment, the role also contributes to institutional coherence, organisational learning and SPARC-related change leadership.

**Purpose of the job**

The main purpose is to provide strategic leadership for SPARC’s Collective Portfolio to strengthen movement-wide accountability, prioritisation, effectiveness and alignment across collective investments.

The role ensures that the Collective Portfolio has robust decision-making and accountability mechanisms. This includes ensuring that portfolio composition, investment choices, delivery performance, risk monitoring and resource visibility are integrated into cross-cutting analysis and timely executive decision-making.

The role also leads management of the portfolio of work for the Common Strategic Priorities and advances portfolio, project and change management practice across the International Office and relevant executive platforms. This work involves paying particular attention to interoperability, absorption capacity, sequencing, implementation quality and organisational coherence.

Finally, this position also supports the functioning of the SPARC Steering Committee. It provides coordination, analysis and synthesis needed for the Committee to fulfil its oversight role on behalf of the Full ExCom. The role helps translate information emerging from the Collective Portfolio, SPARC Coordinating Mechanisms and related reporting processes into coherent cross-cutting insight on progress, risks, resource implications, interdependencies and emerging tensions.

**Accountabilities**

**1. Manage the Collective Portfolio, enabling effective collective governance.**

**Expected result: The Portfolio Committee, relevant executive platforms and the Full ExCom have timely, relevant and decision-ready information on portfolio performance, integration, resourcing and risk.**

- Integrate and coordinate across the components and content owners of the Collective Portfolio, in line with the SPARC MoU and related governance arrangements;
- Translate portfolio design into practical governance and decision-making processes that strengthen collective ownership and disciplined portfolio stewardship;
- Oversee and report on portfolio composition, results, dependencies, risks and strategic fit, preparing analysis for decision-making in the Portfolio Committee and/or further escalation;
- Oversee and report on portfolio health, planning, and resourcing in close collaboration with the IO finance team, the FinDir and portfolio content owners, ensuring integration with the movement’s annual resource planning and budget cycle;
- Ensure that strategic, operational, organisational and implementation risks across the Collective Portfolio are identified, monitored and escalated appropriately, and facilitate the development of mitigation strategies with relevant stakeholders;
- Convene, prepare and facilitate the work of the Portfolio Committee in line with its terms of reference, ensuring focused discussion, sound documentation, clear follow-up and accountability for agreed actions;
- Develop approaches to gather learning and insight from portfolio implementation and contribute to the ongoing refinement, adaptation, and maturation of the Collective Portfolio model throughout the SPARC cycle.

**2. Lead management of the portfolio of work in the Common Strategic Priorities, strengthening investment steering.**

**Expected result: Initiatives and projects within the portfolio of work for the Common Strategic Priorities are strategically aligned, appropriately prioritised and collectively steered to optimise their contribution to SPARC goals and principles.**

- Coordinate and align stakeholders in the Common Strategic Priorities, bringing coherence with approved Movement-level goals, principles, and agreed outcomes;
- Build and continuously improve the portfolio pipeline management process, ensuring transparency, consistency, usability and institutional learning;
- Drive analysis required for investment steering, including strategic relevance, interdependencies, timing, delivery feasibility, absorption capacity, opportunity costs, and portfolio balance;
- Cultivate reflection on emerging priorities, initiatives, or opportunities for better effectiveness or efficiency among Priorities;
- Broker shared understanding across stakeholders where priorities compete, perspectives diverge or conditions evolve, enabling collective choices in a decentralised environment without direct hierarchical authority;
- Promote equitable participation and enable the surfacing of diverse perspectives from across the movement in portfolio dialogue and prioritisation processes while maintaining focus on strategic coherence and delivery discipline;
- Track portfolio decisions, commitments and follow-up actions to strengthen visibility, continuity, and accountability.

**3. Cultivate organisational learning, advancing portfolio-wide accountability for delivery results.**

**Expected result: Collective portfolio oversight decisions are supported by evidence, implementation follow-through is tangible, and the movement has stronger accountability for the results of collective investments.**

- Shape and maintain fit-for-purpose portfolio monitoring, reporting and review mechanisms to support executive decision-making and accountability for results;
- Consolidate portfolio information into clear, decision-ready reporting for governance and executive stakeholders, including progress, bottlenecks, deviations, unintended outcomes, risks, resource implications and emerging strategic choices.
- Follow up on regular reporting and related steering decisions, translating learning into actionable change, in particular with regards to gaps, delays, unresolved dependencies or accountability concerns.
- Drive the development of relevant review processes, evaluation exercises and reflection on Portfolio effectiveness, organisational learning and value generation.

**4. Lead project, change and interoperability management practices across the International Office and executive Platforms.**

**Expected result: The International Office and relevant executive platforms apply stronger portfolio, project and change management practices, enabling more coherent delivery, organisational learning and implementation effectiveness.**

- Drive the improvement of portfolio, project and change management standards, practices and governance approaches across the International Office and relevant executive Platforms;
- Guide and promote disciplined approaches to planning, implementation, benefits realisation and organisational change;
- Advise stakeholders on ways to assess absorption capacity, implementation feasibility and unintended organisational effects when shaping or adjusting initiative processes, timelines, or scopes;
- Promote coordinated use of resources across projects, portfolios, and change initiatives, seeking efficiencies and facilitating cross-functional learning in the International Office and executive Platforms;
- Engage and align stakeholders around the SPARC Interoperability priority, facilitating shared accountability and progress against the Interoperability Ambitions to 2031 and related roadmap;
- Convene and facilitate relevant project and portfolio management communities or working groups in the Movement to strengthen knowledge-sharing, consistency, effectiveness and institutional learning;

**5. Advise and support process design and facilitation for strategic initiatives or organisational transformation processes as requested by the ISG/DSG5. Support the SPARC Steering Committee in fulfilling its oversight, coordination and escalation role by providing timely portfolio analysis, cross-cutting insight, and decision-support across SPARC implementation**

**Expected result: the Steering Committee is equipped with clear, integrated and decision-ready information that strengthens its ability to monitor SPARC implementation, identify and address cross-cutting challenges, and provide well-grounded advice and recommendations to the Full ExCom.**

- Consolidate relevant inputs from the Collective Portfolio, SPARC Coordinating Mechanisms, monitoring and evaluation processes, and other reporting streams;
- Surface risks, interdependencies, resource implications, tensions and emerging issues;
- Support the preparation of coherent recommendations and documentation for Steering Committee review and onward escalation to the Full ExCom.

Autonomy, complexity

**Autonomy to deliver results**

Operates with a high degree of autonomy within the mandate of the role. Determines portfolio management approaches, governance rhythms, prioritisation processes, analytical frameworks and facilitation strategies required to strengthen collective investment steering, accountability and executive decision-making. Exercises independent judgement on complex organisational, strategic and implementation issues with movement-wide implications, while escalating matters requiring broader executive or governance authority.

**Complexity of the environment**

The role operates in a highly complex and decentralised international environment involving multiple governance and executive bodies, operational directorates, sections, finance stakeholders and strategic initiatives with intersecting priorities, timelines and resource implications. The role requires navigating ambiguity, influencing without formal authority, balancing strategic and operational considerations, and enabling collective choices where perspectives, incentives and institutional interests may differ. The position must synthesise diverse streams of information into coherent portfolio insight while supporting implementation discipline across a dynamic and evolving strategic cycle.

**SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse, including those detailed in the MSF Typologies of Abuse. When an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it, without investigating it, to protect others.

- Ensure respectful management and communication at all levels.
- Ensure that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities regarding expected behaviour and reporting abuse while working for MSF.
- Welcome complainants, guide colleagues towards the appropriate channels without investigating, and promote a working environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour.
- Ensure that staff know how to raise concerns and are kept informed of reporting mechanisms.

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Master’s degree or equivalent professional competence in portfolio management, organisational strategy or public administration
- Advanced qualifications or certifications in portfolio, programme or change management are desirable.

**Experience**

- Significant MSF experience is mandatory.
- experience in complex international and multi-stakeholder environments;
- experience leading or coordinating strategic portfolios, organisational transformation initiatives or cross-functional governance processes;
- proven track record of designing and facilitating senior-level consultation, prioritisation and decision-making processes, including with executive committees or governance bodies;
- strong experience influencing senior stakeholders and driving alignment across decentralised structures without direct hierarchical authority.

**Knowledge**

- Understanding of portfolio, programme and change management approaches, governance models, organisational strategy and investment stewardship;
- understanding of complex organisational systems, prioritisation processes, accountability mechanisms and resource planning; familiarity with MSF’s movement dynamics, governance and executive environment, including the interaction between operational, strategic, financial and associative dimensions;
- demonstrated understanding of organisational interoperability, implementation risk, and cross-functional coordination in decentralised environments.

**Languages**

- C2 or excellent English level.
- French, Spanish or Arabic are assets.

**Other**

- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to MSF offices and operational contexts.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures.**

jobs.title: Coordinateur.trice Projet - Sud Est - Haïti - H/F
jobs.description:
## **ALIMA sur la base Sud Est Haïti**

ALIMA intervient en Haïti depuis février 2024 dans un contexte de crise politico sécuritaire majeure privant une grande partie de la population d’accès aux soins, en raison de déplacements forcés, de précarité économique ou de la fermeture/dysfonctionnement des structures de santé. ALIMA a déployé 4 cliniques mobiles couvrant 32 sites dans la zone métropolitaine de Port-au-Prince (communes de Delmas, Port-au-Prince, Cité Soleil, Pétion ville et Croix-de-bouquets) et appuie la réouverture progressive et la pleine fonctionnalité des structures sanitaires publiques (Chancerelles, CHAPI, Thomassin 25, Santo 17 et Corail Cesselesse et la maternité de Croix-de-bouquets), en partenariat avec le Ministère de la Santé Publique et de la Population. Cette approche a permis de faciliter l’accès à un paquet intégré santé primaire/santé sexuelle et reproductive y compris la prise en charge de survivantes de violence sexuelle/santé mentale/Nutrition aux populations déplacées ou vulnérables. ALIMA poursuit et développe une approche communautaire à travers un soutien aux agents de santé communautaires polyvalents sur les sites cliniques mobiles et dans les structures sanitaires soutenues visant à assurer la promotion de la santé et à améliorer la demande des services de santé.

En 2025, face aux difficultés d’accès aux soins pour les femmes enceintes/allaitantes et enfants de moins de 5 ans ainsi que la déportation massive de populations haïtiennes à travers la porte d’entrée d’Anse-à-pitres dans le département du Sud-Est Haïti, ALIMA a étendu sa présence en Haiti en appuyant les centres de santé de Belle-Anse et Mapou (commune de Belle-Anse), les centres de santé de Jéricho, Platon-cèdre et le Centre hospitalier d’Anse-à-pitre (commune d’Anse-à-Pitres). L’objectif est de réduire la morbidité et la mortalité parmi les populations déplacées, déportées et hôtes, à travers trois axes d’intervention prioritaires :

- Amélioration de l’accès aux soins
- Prévention et traitement de la malnutrition
- Réponse rapide aux urgences

Priorités du projet:

Dans le contexte d’insécurité et d’instabilité des populations, donner accès aux soins de santé primaire, secondaire, préventifs, aux populations demande de la ﬂexibilité opérationnelle.

Le principal risque pris en compte est la violence armée, basé sur l’expérience des chocs antérieurs qu’a connu la région. Les principaux facteurs de crise du Sud-Est sont :

- Une forte pression migratoire, en raison des retours forcés de migrants haïtiens déportés de la République dominicaine et des déplacements internes dus m l’insécurité;
- Un système de santé souffrant d’une insuffisance critique des services de santé et d’un accès limité aux soins;
- La survenue des catastrophes naturelles (ouragan, inondations, tremblements de terre), les épidémies et la crise alimentaire).

## MISSION ET ACTIVITES PRINCIPALES

Sous la supervision du Chef de Mission, vous êtes responsable des interventions opérationnelles d’ALIMA dans le cadre du projet. En étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de la capitale, vous définissez les priorités et objectifs du projet et établit un plan pour atteindre ces derniers.

Pour y parvenir, vous examinez les données relatives à la santé de la population et aux besoins humanitaires, analysez le contexte, les questions humanitaires en jeu, ainsi que les risques et contraintes associées au contexte ; par la suite, vous évaluez les besoins en matière de ressources humaines et financières. De plus, vous coordonnez l'exécution du projet, en étroite collaboration avec le coordinateur médical et le chef de mission adjoint, afin d'assurer la réalisation effective des objectifs et aussi afin d'améliorer l'état de santé de la population ciblée ainsi que la situation humanitaire. Enfin, vous veillez au respect des procédures d’engagement des dépenses de ALIMA et du bailleur.

Vous êtes l’interface entre l’équipe de coordination et l’équipe de terrain que vous encadrez et représentez ALIMA auprès des interlocuteurs locaux. Vous êtes le garant sur le terrain des principes opérationnels d’Alima. Au travers des activités, vous les défendez, les appliquez et les diffusez. Vous supervisez et animez l'équipe de terrain et facilitez sa participation à la dynamique du projet.

Vos principales activités :

1. Analyse et gestion de la sécurité
2. Mise en œuvre des programmes
3. 1. Gestion et suivi du projet
2. Diagnostic et conception des projets
3. Mise en œuvre et suivi opérationnel
4. Analyse des données et reporting
5. Gestion des Ressources Humaines du projet
6. Représenter ALIMA sur sa zone d'intervention
7. Prévention contre les abus

## LIEU DU POSTE

Poste basé à Anse à Pitres (avec déplacements fréquent dans le département du Sud Est et possiblement sur tout le territoire haitien)

## LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

- Sous la responsabilité du Chef de mission ALIMA, vous encadrez l’équipe du projet
- Votre équipe projet est composée d’un.e référent.e médical, d’un.e administrateur.trice, d’un.e Logisticien.ne projet, et d’un.e responsable de la qualité des soins Infirmiers (RSI).

## PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ

- Niveau 3: Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

## EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES

- Vous avez une expérience réussie au sein d'une ONGI médicale dans la gestion de projets et la supervision d'une équipe multiculturelle. Vous faites preuve d'une grande capacité de négociation et êtes capable de développer et d'entretenir un réseau efficace. Vous savez évoluer dans des contextes sécuritaires dégradés et/ou d’urgence (gestion des épidémies).
- Une connaissance approfondie des bailleurs de fonds humanitaires est un atout. Vous êtes à l'aise avec les outils informatiques (word, excel et internet). Vous encouragez le travail d’équipe, vous êtes orienté vers la résolution de problèmes et communiquez facilement.

LANGUES

- Bonne maîtrise du français (lu, écrit, parlé) indispensable
- La maîtrise de l’anglais , de l’espagnol ou du creole haitien est un atout

CONDITIONS

- Durée et type de contrat : CDD de droit français de 6 mois renouvelable.
- Prise de poste : ASAP
- Salaire : Selon grille salariale ALIMA + valorisation de l’expérience + Perdiem
- ALIMA prend en charge:
- Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission
- Les frais d’hébergement
- La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droits
- L’évacuation pour l’employé et ses ayants droits

jobs.title: Programme Development Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Programme Development Officer

**Department:** Programme Support

**Division:** Programmes

**Duty Station:** Juba, South Sudan, with some travel within South Sudan and occasionally internationally

**Administrative Line Manager:** Programme Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-Time

**Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP)** envisions a worldwide culture of peace where conflicts within and between communities and nations are managed through nonviolent means. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through unarmed civilian protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**JOB PURPOSE:**

The Programme Development Officer works with the entire country program team to support all stages of the project cycle to ensure compliance with donor regulations (including offering support to sub grantees to ensure their awareness of donor requirements), design projects and write proposals & reports, and represent NP in external engagements when needed.

**COMMITMENT TO NP PRINCIPLES**
All staff are expected to embody and actively work towards NP’s core principles in all aspects of their work:

1. **Nonviolence** in our approach, language, and actions.
2. **Direct Action** when engaging meaningfully with mandate goals.
3. **Radical Connection** through fostering safe, respectful, and inclusive relationships with communities, partners, and colleagues.
4. **Process-oriented** by abiding by NP's values, policies, and the Global Employee Handbook.
5. **Independence** by maintaining integrity in judgment and conduct.
6. **Nonpartisanship** by acting without bias or partisan influence.
7. **Redemption and Healing** by contributing to environments where accountability and growth are possible.
8. **Pluriversality** by embracing and protecting the diversity of all people NP works with and for.

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**
**I. Project Cycle Management:**

**a. Project Technical Design and Development**
• Support the South Sudan country team in identifying opportunities for project funding by tracking upcoming opportunities and those in the pipeline with an online, living document.
• Participate in context and other briefings led by the project and advocacy staff to help identify opportunities for programming which align with community needs/feedback, as well as NP’s strategic framework globally and in-country. Overlay with upcoming funding opportunities to support the team to prioritize where to place time and efforts and code switch between NP’s internal language and the language of donors.
• Lead the project design process in collaboration with project staff, holding ideation workshops when needed, and then synthesizing and articulating colleagues’ input into strong donor materials.
• Proposal development: Establish internal timelines and responsibilities for proposal development, taking the lead in drafting and reviewing, and liaising with other departments (such as Finance for budget development and Global Programme Development for technical support and overall quality assurance).

**b. Compliance**
• Hold ownership of official donor agreements in-country by reading through prior to signature, fully familiarizing with donor requirements, including reporting timeframes and templates, visibility requirements, disbursement schedules, audit and baseline/endline evaluation commitments, and other specific donor commitments. Collaborate across departments (finance, project, and global-based support colleagues) to raise concerns and identify solutions throughout the project cycle.
• Represent NP South Sudan in grants management meetings, taking the lead in preparing for inception meetings and in preparation for grants midterm and other grants related meetings.
• Participate in internal Budget vs Actual meetings to stay abreast of project developments and support colleagues to flag any concerns
related to compliance (ie related to budget category variance, identifying needs for NCEs, etc).

**c. External Facing Engagements**
• Work with the country management team to establish and maintain positive relationships with donors and potential donors, including acting as the focal point for donor relations in-country. Attend donor meetings alongside country management staff and contribute to project and context updates (in writing and in person) which reflect donor language, interests, and NP’s approach and strategic direction.
• Liaise with Program Manager in the cultivation of relationships with partners, whether civil society or international actors. Identify opportunities for formal and informal collaboration, including positioning NP as a subgrantee or consortium member.
• Represent NP South Sudan in partner meetings.

**d. Grants Management & Reporting**
• Maintain a timeline for reporting, identifying upcoming deadlines, and communicating with the relevant team members regarding their responsibilities and timeframes.
• Liaise with MEAL colleagues throughout the project cycle to ensure that the necessary data is being collected in line with donor commitments and NP’s Global MEAL Strategy, pre-emptively identifying and addressing any concerns with the relevant colleagues prior to any reporting deadline.
• Compile input into the correct templates, identify any technical inconsistencies or concerns, and to the extent possible address all concerns prior to sharing with Global Programme Development for review.
• Lead in drafting narrative donor reports and coordinating with the finance department to ensure that financial reports are submitted on time, in adherence with financial reporting requirements, and that they correspond to the narrative reports.
• Contribute to team-wide communications and knowledge management and participate in organization-wide events and discussions on related topics/projects.

**e. Other**
• Travel to field sites in order to enhance understanding of the context and programming for the purposes of developing proposals and reporting to/liaising with donors.
• Support programmatic input into relevant advocacy efforts, whether in-country or at a global level

**QUALIFICATIONS:**
**Required Qualifications**
**Experience**
• At least three (3) to five (5) years of project and grants management experience with a variety of bilateral donors
• Proven experience in grant management, including proposal development for institutional donors
• Experience in institutional donor compliance and familiarity with basic rules and regulations
• Track record of developing successful proposal packages, including narrative, log frames, and budgets
• Significant experience developing narrative donor reports under minimal supervision
• Experience tracking donor trends and opportunities.
• Knowledge of, or demonstrable interest in unarmed civilian protection, human security, violence reduction and/or peacebuilding (preference to candidates with strong familiarity of UCP and ability to differentiate UCP from broader protection and humanitarian language and framing).

**Context-specific**
• Experience implementing programmes in the field, ideally in humanitarian emergencies, and experience in South Sudan or the wider region a plus.

**Education**
• Relevant university degree in social sciences, international development, or related area of studies

**Skills:**
• Self-starter who can take the lead without prompting while also knowing when others need to be looped in/consulted.
• Ability to solve problems, analyse data, and prioritize a high workload with a flexible approach to changing environments.
• Ability to meet strict deadlines
• Attention to detail
• Creativity and innovation in generating new ideas and undertaking research
• Enthusiasm for learning and applying new skills
• Ability to work under pressure and in difficult conditions

**Interpersonal:**
• Ability to work effectively and diplomatically in a multi-cultural environment
• Ability to be a collaborative team player, willing to proactively help colleagues

**Languages and communication:**
• Fluency in written and spoken English, with excellent writing skills which do not require AI for formulation or editing.
• Knowledge of French is a plus.

**Information Technology:**
• Advanced skills in Microsoft Office applications.
• Experience with Salesforce is a plus.

jobs.title: Financial Controller - Haiti
jobs.description:
**About Us**
GOAL has responded to the world’s major humanitarian crises since its founding in 1977, working with vulnerable communities in 13 countries across the globe with a dedicated team of personnel. In Vanuatu, CARE focuses on gender equality, disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation and inclusive governance to support communities, especially women, to lead, decide and thrive.

We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced Senior Manager, Programs to lead CARE Vanuatu’s development and humanitarian portfolio, with accountability for program strategy, business development, program quality and partnership integration.

- **Lead and manage designated staff**, setting clear objectives, providing regular supervision and performance reviews, and addressing performance concerns.

- **Oversee program and partnership risks**, ensuring appropriate mitigation, clear decision thresholds and escalation to the Country Director, with risks held by those best placed to manage them.

jobs.title: Endline Consultant
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference for a Consolidated Endline Evaluation Report of:**

***“Foundations: Strengthening Adolescent Girls’ Sexual and Reproductive Health in Mali, Niger and Sierra Leone”***

1. Project Summary

**Type of assignment** - Consolidated Endline Evaluation Report

**Project start and end** - 26/07/2021- 30/06/2027

**Project duration** - 6 years

**Donor** - Global Affairs Canada (GAC)

**Thematic Areas** - Adolescent Sexual and Reproductive Health (ASRH), Gender Equality

**Project location** - Mali (Sikasso and Koutiala), Niger (Maradi and Diffa), Sierra Leone (Kailahun)

**Estimated reach** - 429,226 direct beneficiaries (259,218 girls, 96,553 boys, 52,131 women, and 30,153 men)

**International Partners** - International Rescue Committee (IRC), Equipop, SickKids Hospital, Overseas Development Institute (ODI)

**National Partners** - Mali (ACOD/3AG); Niger (SongES); Sierra Leone (PPASL, Ndomakeh Federation)

**Overall objectives of the project** - Enhance the empowerment of adolescent girls, particularly the most marginalized and vulnerable, to exercise their ASRH rights in Mali, Niger, and Sierra Leone

2\. Project Description

*Strengthening Adolescent Girls’ Sexual & Reproductive Health* (FOUNDATIONS) is a 6-year (July 27th, 2021 – June 30, 2027) multi-country, gender-transformative project, funded by Global Affairs Canada. The project aims to enhance the empowerment of adolescent girls, particularly the most marginalized and vulnerable, to exercise their ASRH rights in Mali, Niger, and Sierra Leone. To achieve this ultimate outcome, three key intermediate outcomes are realized:

- 1100: Increased decision-making by in-school and out-of-school adolescent girls on adolescent sexual and reproductive health (ASRH) issues and the use of ASRH services.
- 1200: Improved provision of gender-responsive, adolescent-friendly and quality ASRH services for adolescent girls.
- 1300: Improved effectiveness of key stakeholders, particularly women & girls’ rights organizations and government decisionmakers, to advocate for evidence-based, accountable and equitable ASRH policies, legal frameworks and services.

The project is grounded in a rights-based and gender-transformative approach that places women and girls at the centre. In alignment with GAC requirements and its Feminist International Assistance Policy (FIAP), the project promotes gender equality and girls’ empowerment by using a socio-ecological approach that recognizes the multiple and interdependent spheres of influence shaping adolescent behaviours and norms. By engaging parents, other adult caregivers, teachers, community leaders, health providers, civil society organizations (CSOs) including women’s rights organizations (WROs), and government decisionmakers, the project addresses these spheres simultaneously to generate sustainable and meaningful change.

Save the Children implements the FOUNDATIONS project in three countries (Mali, Niger, and Sierra Leone) and in partnership with multiple international partners, including the International Rescue Committee (IRC), Equipop, ODI (formerly Overseas Development Institute) and the Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids).

3\. Endline Evaluation Background

Three baseline reports (i.e. one per country) were produced at the start of the project using a common methodology developed by Save the Children Canada (SCC). Each baseline measured around 20 outcomes indicators, which are common to all three countries. The common methodology used the same data collection tools, sampling method and data analysis plans to measure each indicator consistently. Independent consultants were hired in each country to carry out data collection using the tools developed by SCC. Consultants then handed over clean datasets to SCC along with the results from all questions disaggregated by type of respondent, age and gender. Then, SCC calculated each indicator and drafted three baseline reports using a similar structure.

A similar process will be used with the endline evaluation, but instead of SCC drafting each individual report, an independent consultant will be hired to do this work. As with the baseline, the same outcome indicators will be measured and analysed, using the same tools, sampling method and data analysis plans, to ensure consistency and comparability of results between the baseline and the endline.

4\. Endline Evaluation Purposes and Uses

The purpose of this evaluation is three-fold. First, conducting an endline evaluation meets an accountability requirement of SCC towards GAC (and more broadly to Canadian taxpayers). The endline evaluation will determine the extent to which the project has met the results it set out to achieve, whether the project was relevant to the target population and efficient, and whether it produced meaningful changes in the lives of participants, and to what extent observed results are sustainable.

Second, considering the size, complexity and duration of this project, the endline evaluation will identify lessons learned, good practices and unintended outcomes (whether positive or negative) to inform future design and implementation of similar projects. The evaluation will identify and explore key factors that may have contributed to the achievement of results, or lack thereof.

Third, SCC will use the main findings of the evaluation for dissemination purposes, including with GAC and other donors, to showcase the achievements of the project. Therefore, the consolidated endline evaluation report will highlight the project's main findings and lessons learned for dissemination purposes.

5\. Scope of the Assignment

The selected consultant will produce **three endline reports** (one per country) and **one consolidated report** using the data provided by SCC, including the values from the following outcome indicators (please refer to the Roles and Responsibilities sections for more details):

***Ultimate Outcome Indicators:***

- 1000.1: % of VYA and OA girls who report they are empowered as it relates to SRH decision-making
- 1000.2: % of adolescents (15-19 and 20-24 years) who are currently (within last three months) using a modern method of contraception
- 1000.3: Age-specific fertility rate of girls aged 15-19 years

***Intermediate Outcome Indicators:***

- 1100.1: % of VYA and OA girls (and boys) who report using ASRH information and services in health facilities covering puberty and fertility, family planning, STDs, HIV/AIDS, abortion and post-abortion care, SGBV prevention and treatment
- 1100.2: % of VYA and OA girls (and boys) who report they are able to make decisions related to their SRH
- 1100.3: % of parents/caregivers (m/f) who support (emotional, physical, financial) their daughter’s decision-making power around SRH issues
- 1200.1: Extent to which health facilities have achieved quality of care standards in providing ASRH services
- 1200.2: Extent to which health facilities have achieved gender-responsive standards in providing ASRH services
- 1200.3: Extent to which health facilities have achieved adolescent-friendly standards in providing ASRH services
- 1300.1: No. of actions (e.g. national plans, policy statements, action plans, public declarations, budget allocations, etc.) taken by the government decisionmakers to promote equitable ASRH services for adolescent girls in the past five years
- 1300.2: No. of actions taken by women and girls’ rights organizations in advocating for evidence-based, accountable and equitable ASRH policies, legal frameworks and services in the past five years

***Immediate Outcome Indicators:***

- 1110.1 % of VYA and OA girls and boys who demonstrate knowledge of ASRH topics and life skills
- 1110.2: % of VYA and OA girls and boys who hold positive attitudes towards ASRH rights and gender equality
- 1110.3: % of VYA and OA girls and boys who perceive negative social norms in their community around ASRH rights and gender equality for adolescent girls and boys
- 1120.1: % of parents/caregivers (m/f) who hold positive attitudes towards ASRH rights and gender equality for adolescent girls and boys
- 1120.2: % of parents/caregivers (m/f) who perceive negative social norms in their community around ASRH rights and gender equality for adolescent girls and boys
- 1130.1: % of male religious and traditional leaders, community leaders, partners/husbands of adolescent girls (13-18 years) and adolescent fathers (15-18 years) who hold positive attitudes towards ASRH rights, gender equality and reducing SGBV for women and adolescent girls
- 1130.2: % of male religious and traditional leaders, community leaders, partners/husbands of adolescent girls (15-18 years) and adolescent fathers (15-18 years) who perceive negative social norms in their community around ASRH rights, gender equality and reducing SGBV for women and adolescent girls
- 1220.1: % of targeted health facilities that deliver ASRH and SGBV services including puberty and fertility, family planning, STDs, HIV/AIDS, abortion and post-abortion care, SGBV prevention and treatment
- 1220.2: # of visits reported by health facilities of adolescent girls (and boys) seeking sexual health services, including family planning (on a monthly basis)
- 1220.3: # of visits reported by health facilities of adolescent girls (and boys) seeking SGBV health services (on a monthly basis)
- 1330.1: # of government officials able to identify at least two gender-based barriers to ASRH services for adolescent girls

In addition to these indicators, and considering that this is a final evaluation, a series of questions have been incorporated to the questionnaires to measure OECD-DAC criteria (relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability). It is expected that the country reports and the consolidated report will incorporate a section analysing the results against the OECD-DAC criteria.

To complement the analysis and meet the learning purpose of the assignment, the selected consultant will review and incorporate the following available secondary sources into the reports:

- Baseline reports from Mali, Niger and Sierra Leone
- Annual reports and workplans
- Qualitative data from each country, in the form of interviews, focus group discussions, stories of change, etc.
- Other assessments and research pieces prepared by SCC, Country Offices and partners throughout the project, including from SickKids (quantitative research), ODI (qualitative research) and IRC (baseline and endline of project components under their responsibility)

6\. Deliverables

This assignment has five main deliverables, as follows:

- Inception Report (an updated workplan, timeline, roles and responsibilities, etc.)
- Endline Evaluation report of Mali (in French)
- Endline Evaluation report of Niger (in French)
- Endline Evaluation report of Sierra Leone (in English)
- Consolidated Evaluation Report (in English and French)

The structure of the individual endline reports will follow the structure of the baseline reports, with the addition of a section on OECD-DAC criteria:

1. Executive Summary
2. Introduction
3. Methodology
4. Results (OECD-DAC criteria and outcome indicators)
5. Lessons Learned
6. Recommendations

As reference, each baseline report was about 200 pages long, including 80 tables and 30 figures and graphs. A copy of one report is annexed to these TORs.

The Consolidated Evaluation Report should be succinct (e.g. 20-30 pages), and focus on key findings, lessons learned and recommendations synthesized from the combined individual reports and other relevant sources. The final structure will be discussed and agreed upon with the selected consultant during the Inception Phase.

7\. Timeline

It is expected that this assignment will run over a period of six months, e.g. March to August 2027. At the time of preparing these TORs, the process to recruit independent consultants in each country is underway and should be completed by November-December 2026. It is then expected that in-country data collection will be completed between January and February 2027.

The selected consultant will review secondary data in March and draft individual reports on a rolling basis between April and July, and a prepare a Consolidated Report by August. Below is a provisional timeline for this assignment.

**Periods**

**Key milestones**

November-December 2026 - Request for proposals launched

January-February 2027 - Consultant selected and hired

March 2027 - Inception phase: desk review and short inception note

April-June 2027 - Drafting of individual reports (rolling basis)

June-July 2027 - Finalisation of Individual reports and Drafting of Consolidated report

August 2027 - Finalization of Consolidated report

8\. Payment Schedule

Payment to the consultant shall be done in accordance with normal procedures of Save the Children Canada. The consultant is expected to pay all taxes for which they are responsible.

Payments terms are net 30 and are scheduled as follows:

- 40%: after submission of the 1st draft of all three individual endline reports
- 30%: upon finalization of all three individual endline reports
- 30%: upon finalization of consolidated report

9\. Role and Responsibilities of the Consultant

This consultancy is essentially desk-based and can be conducted remotely as it doesn't require primary data collection or any travel. The selected consultant will be responsible for the following:

- Review project documents, including but not limited to: Project Implementation Plan, Logic Model, Performance Measurement Framework, Baseline reports, Annual Reports, Work Plans, annual budgets and expenditures, data collection tools, endline data analysis plan, SickKids and ODI research products, etc.
- Review the quantitative data and qualitative transcripts for FGDs and KIIs received from the three countries.
- Analyze data against the baseline and targets, and draft separate endline evaluation reports for Mali, Niger and Sierra Leone using OECD-DAC criteria.
- Incorporate other sources of data into the analysis, including qualitative data and other research pieces from partners.
- Draft a consolidated report with high-level findings, lessons learned and recommendations for wider dissemination (policy, advocacy, etc.).

10\. Role and Responsibilities of Save the Children

SCC will share with the selected consultant all data sources needed to complete the assignment in a timely manner, including indicators values, baselines, reports, assessments and all quantitative and qualitative data available, specifically:

- Clean data sets in SPSS and Excel
- Validated indicator calculations
- Analysis tables for all surveys (Sierra Leone in English; Mali and Niger in French)
- Analysis Plan for calculation of project indicators (for reference)
- FGDs and KII transcripts (Sierra Leone in English; Mali and Niger in French)
- All available secondary data (research reports, baselines, annual reports, workplans, etc.)

SCC will coordinate with Country Offices to ensure that in-country consultancies move as planned. SCC will be responsible for the calculation and verification of outcome indicators. SCC will review the endline reports on a rolling basis and will limit the turnaround time as much as possible.

The selected consultant will report directly to the SCC MEAL Team who will be responsible for overseeing and coordinating the entire process. SCC will set up a schedule of weekly check-in calls with the consultant to address any issues or concerns regarding analyzing and drafting the endline evaluation reports.

11\. Consultants Qualifications

The expected minimum qualifications of the Consultant for this assignment are as follows:

- A postgraduate degree in Social Sciences (e.g. public health, sociology, human rights, education, etc.);
- Deep familiarity with project thematic areas (sexual and reproductive health, gender equality, child and adolescent rights), including in West Africa;
- Demonstrated experience in analysing qualitative and quantitative data, using appropriate software;
- Demonstrated experience writing robust baseline and/or endline reports, including using OECD-DAC criteria, for NGOs and/or institutional donors;
- Demonstrated experience synthesizing and translating large amounts of data into high-level, succinct, jargon-free reports for dissemination purposes (e.g. decision-making, policy, advocacy, fundraising...)
- Ability to work and produce high-quality reports in both English and French

Annexes:

- Logic Model
- Performance Measurement Framework
- Baseline report from Sierra Leone

12\. Application Process

Applications for the consultancy must include the following:

1. Detailed **technical proposal** (70% of the total score) including the following:

- Presentation of the Consultant (individual, team or firm)
- Demonstrate previous experience in carrying out similar assignments, particularly endline reports of SRH projects in West Africa
- Understanding of the assignment objectives, scope, and deliverables
- Proposed approach, methodology and workplan to execute the assignment
- Proposed team structure, roles and responsibilities, and level of effort of each team member
- Detailed CVs and biographies of the proposed team, outlining relevant experience
- Names and contact information of three references who can be contacted regarding relevant experience of the proposed lead consultant.
- A copy of a previous report of a similar nature undertaken on a) baseline study; or b) endline evaluation.

2\. A **financial proposal** (30% of the total score) with a detailed breakdown of all costs including consultancy fees/costs.

**Open Request for Proposal**

**Individual Consultant**

**Subject Matter Expert - Future readiness & employability**

**Girl Effect India**

**Issue Date: 17th November 2026**

## **Procurement Summary**

## **Item**

## **Details**

## Procurement method

## Open competitive tender

## Consultant type

## Individual consultant only

## Assignment

## Future Readiness and Employability Subject Matter Expert

## Location

## India; primarily remote

## Duration

## Approximately 4–6 weeks from contract signature

## Proposal deadline

## **26 November 2026**

## Proposal currency

## Indian Rupees (INR)

## Submission email

## **suppliers@girleffect.org**

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. We use youth-centred storytelling, behaviour-change science and digital engagement to help adolescent girls make informed choices about their health, education, relationships and futures.

In India, our initiatives include Chhaa Jaa and Teeka Talk. These programmes provide trusted information and support on health, relationships, empowerment and HPV vaccination through social media, digital content, chatbots and community engagement.

More information is available at[ www.girleffect.org](https://www.girleffect.org).

## **Background and Objective**

Adolescent girls and young women in India face interconnected barriers to education, skilling, livelihoods and economic participation. These barriers are shaped not only by limited information and access, but also by restrictive gender norms, limited decision-making power, mobility and safety concerns, unequal digital access, family expectations and a lack of exposure to viable pathways.

Girl Effect India is supporting the development of a large-scale programme for girls and young women aged 14–20 in select geographies of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. The programme seeks to build participants’ life skills, digital and financial literacy, confidence, agency and ability to navigate gender norms through a facilitator-led, phygital learning model.

The programme will engage the following three audience segments:

1. In-school girls aged 14–17 through classroom-based sessions and multimedia content.
2. Out-of-school girls aged 14–17 through community platforms, including Kishori groups and Anganwadi-linked systems.
3. Young women aged 18–20 through Self-Help Group and livelihood-linked networks, supported by multimedia and digital engagement.

Beyond foundational capability-building, the programme includes a dedicated Future-Ready Pathways component to help girls and young women move from awareness and aspiration to real education, skilling, livelihood, enterprise and employment opportunities.

The pathways will be differentiated according to age, schooling status, aspirations, readiness, mobility, family support and local context. They may include higher education, open schooling, vocational and technical training, scholarships, mentorship, entrepreneurship, livelihoods, certification and placement-linked opportunities.

## **What You will do**

The Subject Matter Expert will build on Girl Effect India’s existing landscape mapping to develop an actionable Future Readiness and Employability Strategy for girls aged 14–17 years and young women aged 18–20 years in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. The assignment will combine studying the existing landscape developed by Girl Effect and strategic pathway development to identify opportunities to strengthen girls’ preparedness for education, skilling, livelihoods, and economic participation.

The assignment will be organised around three core outputs:

1. Practical future-readiness pathways: Identify realistic education, skilling, employment and entrepreneurship opportunities that girls and young women can access in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, differentiated for in-school girls aged 14–17, out-of-school girls aged 14–17, and young women aged 18–20.
2. Technical content and how-to guides: Define what each cohort should learn and develop ready-to-adapt, how-to-guides that help girls navigate these opportunities, using verified MP- and Maharashtra-specific examples.
3. Actionable ecosystem linkages: Identify which institutions, schemes and programmes the programme could connect girls to, and set out how those linkages would work in practice, including eligibility, referral steps, roles, safeguarding and follow-up.

### 1. Develop practical, cohort-specific future-readiness pathways

- Identify realistic education, skilling, employment and entrepreneurship opportunities that girls and young women can access in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, differentiated for the programme's three cohorts: (i) in-school girls aged 14–17, (ii) out-of-school girls aged 14–17 and (iii) young women aged 18–20.
- For girls aged 14–17, focus on career awareness, aspiration-building, education continuation or re-entry, exposure to vocational opportunities and preparation for future transitions. For young women aged 18–20, identify more actionable pathways towards skilling, certification, employment, self-employment and entrepreneurship.
- Identify the key steps, capabilities, enabling conditions and support mechanisms required to help girls navigate these pathways, taking into account their aspirations, mobility, family support, socio-economic circumstances and local opportunities.
- Develop a practical, age-differentiated pathways framework that illustrates how girls can progress from awareness and aspiration-building to accessing relevant opportunities, including critical transition points and potential barriers.
- Ensure that the proposed pathways reflect the specific contexts of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, including differences across rural, urban and tribal settings, and are feasible within the programme's existing implementation model.

### 3. Identify actionable ecosystem linkages and opportunities for convergence

- Building on Girl Effect's existing landscape mapping of Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, identify and prioritise credible education, skilling, livelihood, employment and entrepreneurship institutions, schemes and programmes in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra that could provide relevant opportunities for the programme's target cohorts.
- Undertake targeted validation of shortlisted opportunities, considering eligibility, accessibility, affordability, geographical coverage, credibility, safeguarding, gender responsiveness and suitability for the intended age groups.
- Identify practical opportunities for linkages with government departments and schemes, vocational and technical training institutions, Self-Help Group networks, livelihood missions, entrepreneurship support organisations, employers and other relevant ecosystem actors.
- Recommend how implementation partners could facilitate access to these opportunities through information-sharing, career exposure, referrals, institutional coordination or other feasible mechanisms.
- Develop a prioritised opportunity and partnership matrix outlining relevant institutions and programmes, target cohorts, geographical availability, eligibility requirements, potential collaboration models, referral processes and recommended next steps.
- Provide practical recommendations for operationalising these linkages within the programme's existing delivery model, including the roles of facilitators, implementation partners and relevant institutions, safeguarding considerations and mechanisms for follow-up.

The consultant will work closely with Girl Effect India's programme, curriculum, content, and safeguarding teams to ensure that all proposed pathways, learning resources and institutional linkages are technically sound, contextually relevant, age-appropriate and feasible within the programme's implementation model.

## **Deliverables**

The Subject Matter Expert will deliver the following outputs over the proposed 4–6-week assignment. The work will build on Girl Effect India’s completed landscape mapping, with targeted consultations and a focus on actionable programme strategy rather than duplicating existing research.

Deliverable

Description

Indicative timeline

1\. Inception Note and Workplan

An inception note setting out the consultant’s understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, analytical framework, information requirements, targeted stakeholder consultation plan, work plan, and timelines.

This deliverable will also be complemented by a document detailing an in-depth understanding of the landscape and formative reports developed by Girl Effect. This will aid the consultant towards developing a focused assessment of accessible, safe, gender-responsive, and realistic opportunities in light of girls’ aspirations, capabilities, mobility, household norms and socio-economic circumstances, and highlight gaps, barriers and opportunities for convergence across existing schemes and programmes.

Week 1

2\. Age- Differentiated Future Readiness and Employability Strategy/ framework

An actionable strategy outlining differentiated pathways for (i) girls aged 14–17 years who are in-school, (ii) girls aged 14–17 years who are out-of-school and (iii) young women aged 18–20 years.

For the 14-17 years age group, the focus should include aspiration-building, education continuation or re-entry, scholarship access, career exposure, mentoring, and awareness of vocational pathways. For young women aged 18–20, the focus should include workforce readiness, certification, skilling, financial inclusion, entrepreneurship, market linkages, livelihoods and employment opportunities. The strategy should identify critical transition points, enabling conditions, relevant support systems and convergence opportunities.

The strategy should also be translated into a clear, visually engaging and easy-to-navigate framework that illustrates the differentiated pathways, key transition points, enabling factors and support systems for each age cohort. This may be developed using collaborative visualisation tools such as Miro, Mural, FigJam, Lucidchart, Canva, Google Slides, or another suitable platform. The visual framework should clearly demonstrate how different pathways and opportunities connect, stakeholder engagement, and future implementation. The final visualisation should be shared in an editable format.

The consultant will present the proposed framework to the Girl Effect India team for review and validation, incorporating feedback and recommendations into the next iteration.

Weeks 2-3

3\. Partner and Opportunity Vetting Framework

A practical, standardised framework and checklist for assessing prospective partner organisations, institutions, employers, programmes, mentors and digital platforms. Criteria should include relevance to target cohorts, accessibility, safeguarding, gender responsiveness, quality, feasibility and potential for sustained engagement. The consultant will have to work with Girl Effect’s Safeguarding team to develop this framework.

Week 4

4\. Prioritised Ecosystem Partner Database

A curated database of approximately 15–25 high-potential partners and opportunities across the two states, drawing on existing mapping, desk research, and targeted consultations. Entries may include public programmes, educational institutions, skilling and certification providers, employers, industry-linked initiatives, SHG and community networks, mentorship providers, and digital platforms. For each entry, indicate geographic presence, target cohorts, relevance to proposed pathways, potential collaboration and recommended next steps. Inclusion does not imply a confirmed partnership or commitment to collaborate.

Week 4

5\. Strategic Recommendations and Technical Inputs for Programme Design

A consolidated set of prioritised, actionable recommendations covering institutional convergence, partnership opportunities, implementation considerations, and indicative next steps.

Include technical recommendations for integrating future readiness, career awareness, and employability concepts into programme curriculum and content, identifying suggested learning objectives, thematic areas and age-appropriate approaches.

Week 5

6\. Final Presentation and Validation

A presentation of key findings, proposed pathways, priority programme opportunities, potential partners and strategic recommendations to Girl Effect India. Incorporate consolidated feedback into the final outputs.

Week 6

The deliverables will be developed iteratively, with the landscape synthesis and sector opportunity analysis informing the strategy, partner assessment, and programme recommendations. Deliverables 2 and 3 constitute the core analytical and strategic outputs; Deliverables 4–6 translate the findings into practical programme design and opportunities.

All deliverables should be submitted in English in editable formats. The final work plan and deadlines will be agreed during inception, and the consultant will incorporate consolidated feedback from Girl Effect India into the final outputs.

A deliverable will be accepted only when it is:

- Complete.
- Accurate.
- Supported by verifiable and dated sources.
- Responsive to the approved brief.
- Submitted in the agreed editable format.
- Free from unresolved material errors.
- Approved in writing by Girl Effect.

Corrections required to meet the agreed requirements will be completed within the fixed professional fee and will not constitute additional scope.

## **Management and Working Arrangements**

- The consultant will report to Girl Effect India’s Programme and Content team.
- The consultant will work closely with curriculum, safeguarding, and other nominated Girl Effect colleagues.
- The assignment will primarily be delivered remotely.
- The consultant must be available for regular virtual coordination, review and validation meetings.
- Girl Effect will provide existing research and programme materials and facilitate agreed internal introductions.
- Girl Effect will provide consolidated feedback through its nominated project lead.
- The consultant must maintain:
- A work plan and timesheet, as required.
- Consultation record.
- Risk and dependency log.
- Feedback and revision log.
- Any travel must be requested and approved in writing before bookings are made or costs are incurred.
- No representation may be made to external stakeholders on behalf of Girl Effect without prior written approval.

## **Who You Are**

You are an experienced future-readiness, education, skilling, livelihoods or workforce-development specialist with a strong understanding of the barriers affecting adolescent girls and young women in India. You will have:

- Demonstrated experience (minimum 6 years) mapping education, scholarship, skilling, livelihood, enterprise or employment opportunities.
- Strong knowledge of government, community and private-sector opportunity ecosystems in India.
- Experience designing employability, career-readiness, transition or economic-empowerment strategies.
- The ability to assess labour-market trends and identify realistic growth sectors and pathways.
- Experience reviewing or vetting education institutions, skilling providers, employers, mentors or referral partners.
- A strong understanding of gender, safeguarding, workplace safety and the risks faced by adolescent girls and young women.
- The ability to translate technical evidence and ecosystem findings into practical programme recommendations and accessible curriculum inputs.
- Strong research, analysis, writing, facilitation and stakeholder-engagement skills.
- Strong data visualisation skills.
- A commitment to ensuring that opportunities are safe, inclusive, accessible and relevant to girls’ realities.
- Passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of young women and girls.
- Understanding of gender-responsive and gender-transformative programming, safeguarding and safe-work principles.
- Strong analytical, research, writing and stakeholder-management skills.
- Ability to provide clear and practical inputs into youth-facing curriculum and programme content.
- Familiarity with Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra is preferred.
- Ability and willingness to travel within India, if and when required.
- Commitment to Girl Effect’s mission, values and safeguarding standards.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 17th November 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: **26th November 2026**

## **Proposal Submission**

Your proposal, should you be interested, should cover (Max 7 pages):

Technical Proposal

- Your understanding of the brief and why you feel you are well placed to advise us on this
- Credentials/CV
- Please showcase any previous relevant work experience with links to previous works.
- Provide 3 contactable references
- Estimated level of effort and availability.
- Draft work plan showing activities, deliverables. and proposed timelines.

Financial Proposal

- A breakdown of the financial proposal in **INR**.
- A fixed, all-inclusive professional fee for the complete assignment.
- A breakdown of the professional fee by deliverable.

- Daily rate used to calculate the fixed fee.
- Applicable taxes shown separately.
- Anticipated travel or other reimbursable costs shown separately.
- Travel and other reimbursable expenses will only be payable where approved in writing before the cost is incurred.

## **Evaluation Criteria**

The criteria against which the application will be evaluated are listed below.

Technical Evaluation

- Experience and qualification as outlined in your CV/credentials/profile – 20%
- Showcases relevant experience in having done previous similar work with relevant agencies or organizations - 30 %
- Geographical Experience in the given states - 5%
- Interpretation and understanding of this TOR - 10%
- Evidence of a minimum of three contactable references - 5%

Financial Evaluation

- Value for money/proposed budget breakdown - 30%

Girl Effect may request clarifications, creative presentations, interviews, reference checks, due diligence or best-and-final offers.

The lowest-priced proposal will not necessarily be selected.

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Individual engagement:** The contract will be awarded to an individual consultant. Substitution or subcontracting requires Girl Effect’s prior written approval.
- **Contract and payment:** The selected consultant will sign Girl Effect’s standard consultancy agreement. Payments will be linked to satisfactory completion and written acceptance of agreed deliverables.
- **Fixed fee and changes**: The approved fee will remain fixed for the agreed scope. No additional cost or timeline extension will apply without prior written approval.
- **Taxes:** Applicants must show applicable taxes separately. Girl Effect will deduct or account for statutory taxes where required.
- **Travel and expenses:** Only expenses approved in writing before they are incurred will be reimbursable. Approved travel will be arranged or reimbursed in accordance with Girl Effect’s travel requirements.
- **Confidentiality and data protection:** The consultant must protect Girl Effect’s confidential information, programme materials and personal data and use secure transfer and storage methods.
- **Safeguarding:** Appointment and continued engagement will be subject to Girl Effect’s safeguarding requirements and any required checks.
- **Evidence and accuracy:** All information and recommendations must be properly sourced and verifiable. Unconfirmed opportunities or organisations must not be presented as confirmed partners or guaranteed benefits.

- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may clarify, negotiate, amend or cancel the process; reject any or all proposals; award part of the scope; or make no award. Proposal preparation costs will not be reimbursed.
