jobs.title: Protection Specialist
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview**

Reporting to the Deputy Director of Programmes (DDP) in Chad, the Protection Specialist will be responsible for the strategic vision, planning and design of programmes, as well as for co-coordinating the protection cluster and liaising with key stakeholders in the sector. This is a strategic role for the country programme, aimed at strengthening the IRC’s position as a key player in the field of protection. He or she will be based in N’Djamena and will make frequent visits to field sites.

The role of Protection Specialist will also involve building technical capacity in the areas of humanitarian coordination, strategy and the development of funding proposals. In line with IRC Chad’s focus on integrated programming, the Protection Specialist will work closely with the Senior Manager for Protection and Women’s Empowerment (WPE), and the technical coordinators of other sectors, notably nutrition, health, and economic recovery and development. In their role as co-lead of the protection cluster, this person will work closely with the cluster lead, UNHCR, at national and local levels, as well as with cluster members, international actors and local organisations.

The Protection Specialist will be supported remotely by technical protection advisers to ensure that their approach is relevant and aligned with IRC’s global commitments and positioning on protection, particularly child protection, the protection and empowerment of women, and protection and access to justice.

**Main responsibilities**
Co-coordination of the Protection Cluster

- Working closely with UNHCR and Chadian authorities in supporting the Protection Cluster lead in Chad with coordination, advocacy, information management, and capacity-building for cluster members to ensure an effective and integrated humanitarian response.
- Co-chair meetings and follow up on actions arising from regular sectoral coordination meetings of the Protection Cluster.
- Support the implementation and review of the Cluster’s transition strategy, action plans and the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP).
- Provide support to assess the Cluster’s performance, identify gaps and document lessons learnt.
- Actively identify, liaise with, and offer technical and operational support to new and existing protection partners, including large and small local organisations.
- Provide leadership and strategic guidance, reflecting in particular the perspective of NGOs, within the Cluster’s core processes, including those relating to the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) and the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP).
- Support coordination in order to enable coherent and rapid responses to protection and humanitarian needs.
- Participate in inter-cluster missions and surveys in targeted areas.
- Contribute to the development of periodic and ad hoc protection analyses to inform strategy development, as well as operational responses and advocacy. These analyses should be based on the Protection Analysis Framework (PAF) and highlight risks (threats), vulnerabilities and response capacities.
- Develop response and needs analyses to further help identify gaps in the response relative to identified needs.
- In collaboration with the Cluster’s Information Management Officer, support the Cluster’s data collection efforts, in particular by assisting Chadian partners in submitting accurate and consistent data; in turn, provide an analysis to the Cluster and other inter-agency bodies.
- Support other Clusters and their members in initiatives to mainstream protection, and promote the analysis and integration of protection risks into their strategies and associated responses.
- Lead and facilitate capacity-building sessions on protection for key stakeholders, in line with the Cluster’s agreed priorities.
- Support the Cluster’s representation in inter-agency forums; furthermore, support the mainstreaming of protection through inter-agency engagement and direct support to protection and non-protection actors.
- Work with protection and non-protection partners to promote understanding of and respect for humanitarian and protection principles and standards in accordance with international legal frameworks.

Strategic positioning and programme development

- Strengthen the design and development of project proposals by aligning them with IRC’s country, regional and global strategies, particularly in the area of protection, as well as with donors’ requirements.
- Provide the Protection programme with strategic direction and leadership that is needs-based, context-specific, responsive, coherent, integrated and operationally feasible.
- Contribute to the achievement of the outcomes of the Safety Outcome Strategy (IRC’s Protection Strategy) and its action plan in the country;
- Proactively identify funding opportunities and develop concept notes and project proposals for donors, with a view to expanding the Protection Programme’s portfolio and strengthening IRC’s positioning, particularly in relation to the protection and empowerment of women (including the prevention of and response to gender-based violence) and child protection;
- Regularly lead contextual protection needs assessments and data analysis to inform programme development and advocacy work, in close collaboration with the Senior Protection Manager;
- In close collaboration with the Senior Protection Manager, identify, monitor and report on unmet needs, and explore the IRC’s potential to address these needs within the parameters of the Protection Strategy and sectoral priorities;
- Ensure alignment and consistency with the IRC’s relevant national, regional and global strategies.

Representation, coordination and advocacy

- Actively develop and maintain effective working relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, government actors, United Nations agencies, international and local NGOs, and other relevant actors.
- Attend inter-actor coordination meetings on a regular basis.
- Ensure that protection concerns and challenges are raised with the relevant bodies in order to advocate for standards and procedures that systematise the way in which protection programming is implemented and coordinated in the field.
- Identify and nurture advocacy opportunities in consultation with the DDP and the Senior Protection Manager, drawing on information from the field.
- Support the DDP in positioning itself with donors and in fundraising, relationship-building and trust-building by providing technical insight and knowledge of the country programme.
- Together with the DDP, contribute to the advocacy efforts of IRC Chad and the West and Central Africa Region through analysis of the policy environment and trends, in close collaboration with the Senior Protection Manager.
- Working closely with the Senior Protection Manager, support greater sharing and use of research and learning across IRC’s programme sectors, notably by contributing to programme development and design, to ensure that interventions meet needs and are based on a sound understanding of the protection environment in Chad.
- At the request of the management team, and in close collaboration with the Senior Protection Manager, support the organisation and facilitation of field visits for partners, donors and other stakeholders interested in the IRC’s protection programmes in Chad.

**Key working relationships**

- The post is supervised by the DDP.

**Key stakeholders:**

- **Internal:** Other sector coordinators, the regional protection technical team, the grants manager and the monitoring and evaluation coordinator.
- **External:** UNHCR, inter-clusters, OCHA, members of the protection cluster, donors, authorities.

**Job requirements**

- A Master’s degree in humanitarian assistance, humanitarian work, human rights, international law, social and/or political sciences, or a related field.
- At least 5 years’ proven experience in protection issues in humanitarian contexts, including the provision of technical advice to field teams; excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency situations and in-depth knowledge of humanitarian principles, guidelines and laws.
- Proven experience in managing clusters and working groups.
- Proven strong skills in leadership, management, coordination, planning and analysis, with the ability to mobilise others around the integration of protection across sectors and units.
- Proven experience in policy, advocacy and negotiation.
- Proven experience in developing protection strategies, projects and programmes that have been successfully approved by donors, in similar protection contexts.
- Knowledge of and experience in the humanitarian context in Chad, particularly in the area of protection, is a major asset.
- Knowledge of the landscape of technical and financial partners in the field of protection in Chad or in West and Central Africa.
- Practical professional experience in implementing programmes in the field of protection, particularly programmes addressing and preventing gender-based violence, and child protection in conflict-affected areas.
- Knowledge of protection programming in the broadest sense, particularly access to justice, is an asset.
- Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to represent the organisation effectively and collaborate with external stakeholders.
- Ability to integrate easily and work well in a team, comfortable in a multicultural environment, flexible and capable of managing pressure effectively and productively.
- Excellent written and spoken French and English.

**Gender Equality:** IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRCconsiders all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability.

**French Version:**

**Contexte**

Le Comité international de secours (IRC) répond aux crises humanitaires les plus graves au monde, contribuant à restaurer la santé, la sécurité, l’éducation, le bien-être économique et l’autonomie des communautés dévastées par les conflits et les catastrophes. Fondé en 1933 à la demande d’Albert Einstein, l’IRC est l’une des plus grandes organisations non gouvernementales internationales (ONGI) au monde. Il intervient dans plus de 40 pays et 29 villes américaines, où il aide les populations à survivre, à reprendre le contrôle de leur avenir et à renforcer leurs communautés. Véritable force au service de l’humanité, le personnel de l’IRC a un impact durable en restaurant la sécurité, la dignité et l’espoir de millions de personnes. Si vous êtes une personne passionnée, orientée vers les solutions et porteuse de changement, rejoignez-nous pour avoir un impact positif sur la vie de millions de personnes à travers le monde et leur offrir un avenir meilleur.

**Aperçu du poste**

Sous la supervision du/de la Directeur/trice adjoint(e) des Programmes (DDP) au Tchad, le/la Spécialiste de la Protection sera responsable de la vision stratégique, de la planification et de la conception des programmes, ainsi que de la co-coordination du cluster protection et de la liaison avec les principales parties prenantes du secteur. Il s’agit d’un rôle stratégique pour le programme pays, visant à renforcer la position de l’IRC en tant qu’acteur clé dans le domaine de la protection. Il ou elle sera basé(e) à N’Djamena et effectuera de fréquentes visites sur le terrain.

Le rôle du/de la Spécialiste de la Protection consistera également à renforcer les capacités techniques dans les domaines de la coordination humanitaire, de la stratégie et de l’élaboration de propositions de financement. Conformément à l’accent mis par l’IRC Tchad sur la programmation intégrée, le/la Spécialiste de la Protection travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le/la Manager Senior Protection et Autonomisation des Femmes (PAF), ainsi qu’avec les coordinateurs techniques des autres secteurs, notamment la nutrition, la santé et le relèvement et le développement économiques. En tant que co-chef de file du cluster protection, cette personne travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le chef de file du cluster, le HCR, aux niveaux national et local, ainsi qu’avec les membres du cluster, les acteurs internationaux et les organisations locales.

Le/la Spécialiste de la Protection sera soutenu(e) à distance par des conseillers techniques en protection afin de garantir que son approche soit pertinente et alignée sur les engagements et le positionnement mondiaux de l’IRC en matière de protection, notamment la protection de l’enfance, la protection et l’autonomisation des femmes, ainsi que la protection et l’accès à la justice.

**Principales responsabilités**

Co-coordination du Cluster Protection

- En étroite collaboration avec le HCR et les autorités tchadiennes, appuyer le chef de file du Cluster Protection au Tchad en matière de coordination, de plaidoyer, de gestion de l’information et de renforcement des capacités des membres du cluster afin d’assurer une réponse humanitaire efficace et intégrée
- Co-présider les réunions et assurer le suivi des actions issues des réunions de coordination sectorielle régulières du Cluster Protection.
- Appuyer la mise en œuvre et la révision de la stratégie de transition du Cluster, des plans d’action et du Plan de Réponse Humanitaire (HRP).
- Fournir un appui pour évaluer la performance du Cluster, identifier les lacunes et documenter les enseignements tirés.
- Identifier activement les partenaires de protection nouveaux et existants, établir des liens avec eux et leur offrir un appui technique et opérationnel, y compris aux grandes et petites organisations locales.
- Assurer un leadership et une orientation stratégique, reflétant en particulier le point de vue des ONG, au sein des processus centraux du Cluster, y compris ceux relatifs à l’Aperçu des Besoins Humanitaires (HNO) et au Plan de Réponse Humanitaire (HRP).
- Appuyer la coordination afin de permettre des réponses cohérentes et rapides aux besoins de protection et humanitaires.
- Participer aux missions et enquêtes inter-clusters dans les zones ciblées.
- Contribuer à l’élaboration d’analyses de protection périodiques et ponctuelles pour éclairer le développement de la stratégie, ainsi que les réponses opérationnelles et le plaidoyer. Ces analyses doivent s’appuyer sur le Cadre d’Analyse de la Protection et mettre en évidence les risques (menaces), les vulnérabilités et les capacités de réponse.
- Élaborer des analyses de réponse et de besoins pour aider davantage à identifier les lacunes de la réponse par rapport aux besoins identifiés.
- En collaboration avec le/la Responsable de la Gestion de l’Information du Cluster, appuyer les efforts de collecte de données du Cluster, notamment en aidant les partenaires tchadiens à soumettre des données précises et cohérentes ; en retour, fournir une analyse au Cluster et aux autres instances interagences.
- Appuyer les autres Clusters et leurs membres dans les initiatives visant à intégrer la protection, et promouvoir l’analyse et l’intégration des risques de protection dans leurs stratégies et réponses associées.
- Diriger et faciliter des sessions de renforcement des capacités sur la protection pour les principales parties prenantes, conformément aux priorités convenues par le Cluster.
- Appuyer la représentation du Cluster dans les forums interagences ; en outre, appuyer l’intégration de la protection par le biais de l’engagement interagences et de l’appui direct aux acteurs de la protection et non liés à la protection.
- Travailler avec les partenaires de protection et non liés à la protection pour promouvoir la compréhension et le respect des principes et normes humanitaires et de protection conformément aux cadres juridiques internationaux.

Positionnement stratégique et développement de programme

- Renforcer la conception et le développement des propositions de projets en les alignant sur les stratégies pays, régionales et mondiales de l’IRC, notamment dans le domaine de la protection, ainsi que sur les exigences des bailleurs de fonds.
- Fournir au programme Protection une orientation et un leadership stratégiques fondés sur les besoins, adaptés au contexte, réactifs, cohérents, intégrés et opérationnellement réalisables.
- Contribuer à la réalisation des résultats de la Stratégie de Résultats (Stratégie de Protection de l’IRC) et de son plan d’action dans le pays ;
- Identifier de manière proactive les opportunités de financement et élaborer des notes conceptuelles et des propositions de projets pour les bailleurs de fonds, en vue d’élargir le portefeuille du Programme Protection et de renforcer le positionnement de l’IRC, notamment en ce qui concerne la protection et l’autonomisation des femmes (y compris la prévention de la violence basée sur le genre et la réponse à celle-ci) et la protection de l’enfance ;
- Diriger régulièrement des évaluations contextuelles des besoins de protection et des analyses de données pour éclairer le développement des programmes et le travail de plaidoyer, en étroite collaboration avec le/la Manager Senior Protection ;
- En étroite collaboration avec le/la Manager Senior Protection, identifier, suivre et rendre compte des besoins non satisfaits, et explorer le potentiel de l’IRC pour répondre à ces besoins en suivant la Stratégie de Protection et des priorités sectorielles ;
- Assurer l’alignement et la cohérence avec les stratégies nationales, régionales et mondiales pertinentes de l’IRC.

Représentation, coordination et plaidoyer

- Développer et entretenir activement des relations de travail efficaces avec les principales parties prenantes, y compris les bailleurs de fonds, les acteurs gouvernementaux, les agences des Nations Unies, les ONG internationales et locales, ainsi que d’autres acteurs pertinents.
- Assister régulièrement aux réunions de coordination inter-acteurs.
- Veiller à ce que les préoccupations et défis en matière de protection soient soulevés auprès des instances compétentes afin de plaider en faveur de normes et de procédures qui systématisent la manière dont la programmation de la protection est mise en œuvre et coordonnée sur le terrain.
- Identifier et cultiver des opportunités de plaidoyer en concertation avec le/la DDP et le/la Manager Senior Protection, en s’appuyant sur les informations du terrain.
- Appuyer le/la DDP dans son positionnement auprès des bailleurs de fonds et dans la collecte de fonds, l’établissement de relations et de confiance, en apportant un éclairage technique et une connaissance du programme pays.
- Avec le/la DDP, contribuer aux efforts de plaidoyer de l’IRC Tchad et de la région Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre par l’analyse de l’environnement politique et des tendances, en étroite collaboration avec le/la Manager Senior Protection.
- En étroite collaboration avec le/la Manager Senior Protection, appuyer un meilleur partage et une meilleure utilisation de la recherche et des enseignements tirés dans l’ensemble des secteurs de programme de l’IRC, notamment en contribuant au développement et à la conception des programmes, afin de garantir que les interventions répondent aux besoins et reposent sur une bonne compréhension de l’environnement de protection au Tchad.
- À la demande de l’équipe de direction, et en étroite collaboration avec le/la Manager Senior Protection, appuyer l’organisation et la facilitation de visites de terrain pour les partenaires, les bailleurs de fonds et autres parties prenantes intéressés par les programmes de protection de l’IRC au Tchad.

**Relations de travail clés**

- Le poste est supervisé par le/la Directeur/trice adjoint(e) des Programmes.

**Parties prenantes clés :**

- **Interne :** Les autres coordinateurs sectoriels, l’équipe technique régionale de protection, le/la responsable des subventions et le/la coordinateur/trice du suivi et de l’évaluation.
- **Externe** : HCR, inter-clusters, OCHA, membres du cluster protection, bailleurs de fonds, autorités.

**Exigences du poste**

- Un master en aide humanitaire, action humanitaire, droits humains, droit international, sciences sociales et/ou politiques, ou un domaine connexe.
- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience avérée sur les questions de protection dans des contextes humanitaires, y compris la fourniture de conseils techniques aux équipes de terrain ; excellente compréhension des enjeux de protection dans les situations d’urgence et connaissance approfondie des principes humanitaires, des directives et du droit humanitaire.
- Expérience avérée dans la gestion de clusters et de groupes de travail.
- Solides compétences avérées en leadership, gestion, coordination, planification et analyse, avec la capacité de mobiliser d’autres personnes autour de l’intégration de la protection dans l’ensemble des secteurs et unités.
- Expérience avérée en matière de politique, de plaidoyer et de négociation.
- Expérience avérée dans l’élaboration de stratégies, projets et programmes de protection ayant été approuvés avec succès par des bailleurs de fonds, dans des contextes de protection similaires.
- La connaissance et l’expérience du contexte humanitaire au Tchad, en particulier dans le domaine de la protection, constituent un atout majeur.
- Connaissance du paysage des partenaires techniques et financiers dans le domaine de la protection au Tchad ou en Afrique de l’Ouest et du Centre.
- Expérience professionnelle pratique dans la mise en œuvre de programmes dans le domaine de la protection, en particulier des programmes de prévention de la violence basée sur le genre et de réponse à celle-ci, ainsi que de protection de l’enfance dans les zones touchées par les conflits.
- La connaissance de la programmation de la protection au sens large, en particulier l’accès à la justice, est un atout.
- Solides compétences en communication écrite et orale, avec la capacité de représenter efficacement l’organisation et de collaborer avec les parties prenantes externes.
- Capacité à s’intégrer facilement et à bien travailler en équipe, à l’aise dans un environnement multiculturel, flexible et capable de gérer la pression de manière efficace et productive.
- Excellentes compétences en français et en anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral.

**Égalité des genres** : L’IRC s’engage à réduire l’écart entre les genres aux postes de direction. Nous offrons des avantages qui favorisent un environnement propice à la participation des femmes à nos équipes, notamment le congé parental, des protocoles de sécurité sensibles au genre et d’autres avantages et allocations de soutien.

L’IRC est un employeur garantissant l’égalité des chances. L’IRC examine toutes les candidatures sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur, d’origine nationale, de religion, d’orientation sexuelle, d’âge, de situation matrimoniale, ou de handicap.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Protection Coordinator-Damascus
jobs.description:
## Background/Context

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs across the country, with geographic priorities reviewed regularly as the context evolves. The IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery.

Our longstanding experience in the country provides a strong foundation for the IRC to further adapt and expand its programming across Syria, in order to respond to the new realities, with a greater focus on resilience, recovery, and local systems strengthening, while retaining the capacity to respond to emergencies. Alongside this, the IRC plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and actively engaging in advocacy efforts.

### Integrated protection

The IRC has been delivering protection programs in the northwest since 2013 and in the northeast of Syria since 2014, focusing on Protection/Rule of Law (PRoL), Women’s Protection and Empowerment (WPE), and Child Protection (CP). These efforts include specialized case management, PSS, community-based protection and prevention activities, protection monitoring, information and services, and advocacy. Collaborating with partners, the IRC improves access to protection services, raises community awareness, and strengthens referral pathways. Protection capacity building, community outreach, and rapid response through mobile protection teams have also been provided since 2017. As a lead protection actor, the IRC hosts the Protection Co-Coordination Cluster in Syria.

## Job overview

The Protection Coordinator (PC) is the lead protection role for IRC Syria, holding the strategic vision for, and overall accountability for the quality, results, and compliance of, the integrated protection portfolio (CP, WPE, PRoL) across Syria. The role covers all of Syria and requires nationwide movement, with geographic priorities set through the Strategy Action Plan (SAP) and the Protection Risk Analysis (PRA) as the context evolves.

The PC is a highly experienced, dynamic individual with a strong technical background and team and program management experience. The PC leads the design, development, and management of a robust violence prevention and response program able to meet the safety and protection needs of conflict-affected people, reducing risk and responding to cases of violence, coercion, and deprivation, as well as mainstreaming protection throughout the IRC’s and partners’ response in Syria.

The PC leads development and implementation of the integrated protection strategy for Syria, grounded in the IRC Safety Outcome Strategy and the SAP (with attention to donor and UN/cluster relations), drives new proposal design, and oversees quality implementation of ongoing grants, including spending plans, workplans, and budget management. Strong capacities and adaptive, evidence-based approaches in protection are integral to the delivery of the IRC Syria country strategy through both dedicated and integrated programming toward improving outcomes for target populations.

The PC plays a critical role in building staff technical and program management capacities, driving forward implementation and coordination with other actors, ensuring quality data is produced and analyzed effectively, and leading IRC’s protection voice in multi-agency advocacy efforts.

### Working in an evolving context

Syria’s operating context is fragile and changing, with shifts in security, access, governance, displacement and return, and funding. The PC is expected to lead with agility: reviewing priorities, geography, and delivery modalities regularly against the SAP scenarios and PRA findings, pivoting between emergency response and early recovery or systems strengthening as conditions require, and maintaining the capacity to scale up or down. Priorities and responsibilities may be adjusted as the country structure and strategy evolve.

## Responsibilities

### Program management, technical quality, and strategy

- Provide strategic vision and leadership for IRC Syria’s integrated protection portfolio, and be accountable for its technical quality, results against SAP indicators, and donor compliance.
- Lead contextualization and delivery of the Safety Outcome Strategy (FY26–28) in Syria through the SAP, across targeted individual assistance, violence prevention, and crisis-responsive social work systems.
- Serve as technical lead in quality program design, concept note and proposal development to further fund and develop IRC Syria protection programming, both targeted and integrated.
- Lead development and implementation of the integrated protection strategy for Syria, in line with SAP outcomes for safety, in collaboration with the DDP, the Regional Protection Lead, VPRU Technical Advisors, and protection staff, with an appropriate balance of system strengthening, partnerships, and direct implementation.
- Regularly review the strategy and workplans against the SAP scenarios, PRA findings, and changes in access, security, funding, and governance, and adapt priorities, geographic focus, partnerships, and delivery modalities (including mobile, outreach, and remote approaches) accordingly, while retaining the capacity to scale up emergency protection response when needed.
- Ensure sound and effective management of the portfolio and donor compliance, including timely spending of grants to achieve program goals, budget forecasting and spending plans, workplans, partner support plans, timely recruitment, accurate grant reporting, and use and distribution of supplies and resources. Actively participate in grant management meetings.
- Work closely with the Regional Protection Lead and VPRU Technical Advisors to ensure relevant support, tools, guidance, and other resources are provided and integrated into programming.
- Ensure close alignment and coherence with IRC country, regional, and global strategy, as well as with local Health and MHPSS programs.
- Proactively identify, assess, monitor, and implement measures to reduce or control risks that may impact program delivery, quality, or compliance, including contingency and preparedness planning for deteriorating-context scenarios.
- Be accountable for safeguarding and PSEAH across the protection team and partners, particularly as outreach, cash, legal assistance, and community-based modalities scale, ensuring programming does not create new risks of exploitation and abuse.
- Promote joint work across all protection teams (CP, WPE, PRoL) to enhance the quality of programming and a holistic approach to addressing safety risks, and promote protection mainstreaming across sectors and field teams.
- Develop and ensure adherence to the internal Standard Operating Procedures for integrated protection, adapting them as the operating context evolves.
- Work with protection staff and MEAL/information management teams to analyze program performance and impact and identify course-correction actions needed, and facilitate the strengthening of program management capacities across the team.
- Work with other sectors (Economic Recovery and Development, Health, and Early Childhood Development) to improve integration and coordination within programs.

### Safety outcome strategy delivery

- Ensure timely, high-quality, survivor-centered individual assistance, including specialized case management, PSS, legal assistance, safe spaces, and responsive information, through direct, mobile, and partner delivery, reaching those at greatest risk.
- Scale evidence-based prevention and community-led approaches, including Safe at Home, community-led social norms change, and community-based early warning and risk monitoring, adapted to acute, protracted, and transitional settings.
- Strengthen crisis-responsive social work systems with MoSAL and partners, including case management standards, workforce capacity, safe and integrated information management, and referral pathways.
- Move programming from vulnerability-based to risk-based, using PRA findings and the Protection Analytical Framework to target those most exposed to harm.
- Integrate conflict-sensitive, social cohesion approaches among IDPs, returnees, and host communities into protection programming.

### Program development

- Identify opportunities for, design, and develop evidence-based concept notes and proposals for prevention and response programming, including protection monitoring, information dissemination, and community-based protection programming, in addition to integration with other sectors, in collaboration with country program senior management, business development staff, and Technical Advisors.
- Design programs and budgets with built-in flexibility (for example, adaptable modalities, scale-up and scale-down options, and links to emergency response mechanisms) so they remain relevant as the context evolves.
- Collaborate with Syrian partners on identifying business development opportunities and designing new interventions.
- Develop protection assessments and analysis for the purpose of program development.
- Provide input on proposals from other sectors to ensure protection is mainstreamed.
- Anticipate, plan, and manage programmatic and structural transitions.

### Program quality, research, learning, and innovation

- Ensure protection programming is GEDI-informed and applies an intersectional lens across design, implementation, MEAL, and partnerships, including use of the GEDI Marker.
- Lead the annual Protection Risk Analysis (PRA) cycle and ensure its findings inform the protection strategy, SAP priorities, and program design.
- Identify research and learning agendas aimed at improving evidence generation feeding into programming.
- Use the Protection Analytical Framework to regularly analyze risks, trends, and protection threats, and adapt programming accordingly to ensure interventions remain relevant and responsive. Ensure protection risk analysis is disaggregated and intersectional (e.g., gender, age, disability, displacement status) so that programming reaches those most at risk.
- Lead protection assessments and context-appropriate research aimed at generating a strong evidence base for IRC protection programming and informing IRC advocacy.
- Support the greater sharing and use of research and learning within IRC’s program sectors, including by contributing to program development and design, to ensure interventions are responsive to needs and informed by a sound understanding of the environment in Syria.
- Identify, monitor, and report unmet needs, and explore the IRC’s potential to address them within the parameters of the SAP and sector priorities, while preventing duplication with other actors and taking advantage of synergies.
- Provide guidance to the protection team on tools and strategies to ensure programming is based on input from communities, local partners, and local/national stakeholders, a thorough understanding of the context, and technical best practices. Ensure programs reflect standards of quality and innovation and are adapted based on monitoring data.
- Work with the MEAL team to develop, adapt, and implement appropriate monitoring and evaluation systems, and support teams to use evidence, learning, and community feedback to inform programming and decision-making.
- Lead development of innovative approaches and toolkits for protection in Syria, and support learning on their effectiveness.
- Support the roll-out of new IRC tools to improve program quality, including the Project Cycle Meeting approach, the IMPACT Standards, and the updated Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System.
- Conduct regular reflection or program review meetings with field-based staff to assess the level of achievement and draw on learning and data trends (including client feedback) to inform program design and management decisions, and adapt programming in a timely manner.

### Coordination and representation

- Represent IRC Syria’s protection program with donors, UN agencies, and coordination bodies, alongside country leadership.
- Represent IRC in its role as a lead protection actor and host of the Protection Co-Coordination Cluster. Attend relevant coordination forums inside Syria and participate in working groups within and outside the UN cluster system, and in technical meetings for consortium projects (directly or via an appropriate delegate).
- Establish and maintain solid and trusted relationships with protection stakeholders, networks, and government agencies (including MoSAL), donors, UN agencies, and international and local civil society organizations (including women-led and women’s rights organizations) that support IRC’s scaling and sustainability objectives. Engage authorities in a principled, conflict-sensitive, and selective manner, in line with the SAP, and work with stakeholders in Syria to influence national protection strategies and initiatives, to ensure greater investment in protection and greater access to protection services.
- Lead voice and thought leadership on protection in Syria, formulating advocacy positions with the Advocacy team and feeding IRC and multi-agency advocacy, informed by PRA findings and program evidence.
- Regularly coordinate with internal program and operational stakeholders, the Regional Protection Lead, VPRU Technical Advisors, Airbel (Research and Development), and other IRC colleagues.
- Collaborate closely with other program departments to ensure that linkages between programs are made and programs gain from training and best practices.

### Partnerships and localization

- Lead responsibility for strategically developing and maintaining partner relationships with MoSAL, local civil society organizations, and women-led and women’s rights organizations, contributing to SAP partnership targets (share of budget to local partners, strategic partnerships, CSO support, and community protection committees) and moving beyond transactional partnerships toward capacity sharing and locally led delivery.
- Engage women-led and women’s rights organizations directly in protection analysis, program design, monitoring, and advocacy.
- Work closely with the IRC Partnerships team to ensure the IRC’s partnership strategic objectives are achieved.
- Ensure regular performance monitoring of partners to achieve the project’s set objectives, and provide sustained technical support, mentoring, and guidance rather than one-off trainings.
- Work closely with the Partnerships team and relevant protection staff to draft and/or review partnership priorities and stakeholder analysis, identifying strategic partners when needed to jointly achieve protection outcomes for vulnerable populations.
- Take part in periodic Partnerships meetings, such as the Partnerships Working Group and/or Partnerships Review meetings.

### Staff performance management, learning, and development

- Plan, organize, recruit, supervise, and develop the team needed to achieve program goals and maximize national ownership and leadership. Develop and implement remote management and capacity-building approaches.
- Build a flexible, multi-skilled team, with surge and contingency arrangements that can adapt as the structure, funding, and operating context evolve.
- Coach, train, supervise, and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting annual performance objectives, providing regular and timely positive and constructive performance feedback, and providing documented semi-annual and probationary performance reviews.
- Hold high-quality meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, at minimum monthly.
- Provide a measurable development plan, including on-the-job learning, to strengthen technical capacity, exchange knowledge within the team, and provide guidance on career paths.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promote a strong team spirit, and provide oversight and guidance to enable staff to perform successfully in their positions.
- Approve and manage time, attendance, and leave requests to ensure adequate departmental coverage, and ensure monthly, accurate timesheet submission.
- As required, identify staff performance issues and work with Human Resources to document and address these in accordance with the National Staff Employment Policies.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions for national and international staff care needs.
- Look for opportunities to support staff in their career growth where appropriate.
- Adhere to and act in accordance with the IRC Global HR Policies and Procedures, and communicate through word and example a high standard of compliance with all applicable policies and regulations.

## Job requirements

### Education

- Degree in Law, Human Rights, Social Science, international relations, psychology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.

### Work experience

- 8 years of professional experience in humanitarian response, preferably in protection programming, with at least 3 years in a managerial position, including staff management. Demonstrated experience managing large teams, preferably across multiple project sites. Experience in two or more areas of protection (CP, GBV, PRoL) is highly desirable.
- Experience in one or more of the following is highly desirable: legal identity, HLP, and civil documentation; explosive ordnance risk; social cohesion and conflict-sensitive programming; social work systems, case management standards, and workforce strengthening; evidence-based prevention models (e.g., Safe at Home).
- Prior experience working in emergency settings or insecure environments is preferred.
- Previous experience working on integrated and multi-sectoral programs is preferred.
- Experience working in Syria and/or MENA.

### Demonstrated skills and competencies

- Demonstrated ability to lead and adapt strategy in fragile, rapidly changing, insecure, and politically sensitive contexts, working with ambiguity and making sound, evidence-based decisions under uncertainty, including pivoting between emergency response and recovery or systems-strengthening work.
- Demonstrated experience using international human rights standards in protection programming.
- Strong strategic thinking, critical analysis, and proposal writing skills, with demonstrated experience developing and implementing programmatic strategies.
- Demonstrated commitment to and skills in GEDI and intersectional approaches.
- Ability to preempt risks and challenges, and to devise and implement mitigation strategies through efficient decision-making. Strong risk management skills and agility are desirable.
- Strong leadership, staff and budget management, and capacity-building skills.
- Excellent written, presentation, and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical matters to a range of audiences; cultural sensitivity, flexibility, and ability to improvise.
- Strong planning, reporting, monitoring, and evaluation skills. Experience implementing programming that utilizes ICT, including in the collection and management of qualitative and quantitative data, is desired.
- Excellent representation and liaison skills with external parties, and the ability to manage multi-level relationships with donors, government officials, UN agencies, INGOs, and NGOs.
- Demonstrated experience managing projects with stakeholders and team members without direct managerial oversight.
- Ability to work productively and accurately under pressure in a fast-paced environment, with sound judgment on when to handle problems independently and when to flag them to leadership.
- Ability to collaborate effectively with colleagues in remote and distant, diverse teams.
- INGO experience is required, and private sector experience is desirable.
- Capable of applying skills and knowledge in a range of capacities, including direct implementation, advisory functions, training, and the transfer of technical knowledge and management skills to others.
- Professional discretion and integrity, and the ability to handle complex situations diplomatically.
- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values, and the IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Works well in and promotes teamwork; comfortable in a multicultural environment.
- Mastery of MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

### Language and travel

- Language: fluent English and Arabic.
- Travel: nationwide travel across Syria, minimum 30%, subject to security and access conditions, plus occasional regional and global meetings.

## Key working relationships

**Position reports to:** Deputy Director for Programs (DDP), with close working relationships with the Regional Protection Lead and VPRU Technical Advisors.

**Position directly supervises:** Protection team staff, as per the approved country structure.

**Internal contacts:** Health, ERD, Education Technical Coordinators, Regional Protection Lead, VPRU Technical Unit and Grants Department, MEAL, Partnerships, Advocacy, Country Safeguarding Lead, Supply Chain, Finance, HR, Research, Evaluation and Learning Technical Unit, Airbel, and other sectors.

**External:** UN bodies, local and national authorities (including MoSAL), donors, clusters, and working groups.

## Professional standards

IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in the IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work, Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

### Returning national candidates

We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC’s operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

### Accountability to clients

IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its Client Responsiveness (CR) Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

### Gender equality

IRC is committed to narrowing the gender gap in leadership positions. We offer benefits that provide an enabling environment for women to participate in our workforce including parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols and other supportive benefits and allowances.

### Diversity and inclusion

At IRC MENA, we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. Organizations that are diverse in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, nationality, and perspective are validated to be better organizations. More importantly, creating a safe workspace environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best is the right thing to do. So, bring your whole self to work.

IRC is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive, respectful, and safe work environment where all persons are treated fairly, with dignity and respect. In keeping with our core values of Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality, IRC strives to maintain a work environment built on mutual respect in which all individuals treat each other professionally, and free of bias, prejudice, and harassment. IRC expressly prohibits and will not tolerate discrimination, harassment, retaliation, or bullying of IRC Persons in any work setting. All IRC staff, wherever they are located, are accountable for creating an environment free of discrimination, harassment, bullying, and retaliation.

jobs.title: Professional Workshop Facilitation and Master of Ceremonies Services for Thailand PrEP Consultation, to be held on 15 December 2027
jobs.description:
## **Request for Consultant Services Proposal (RFP)**

**Background**

Thailand has made substantial progress in its HIV response, achieving significant reductions in new HIV infections over the past decade. Despite these achievements, further efforts are needed to meet national HIV prevention targets and accelerate progress toward ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030. Expanding access to and effective utilization of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) remains a key priority within the national HIV prevention strategy.

To support this goal, FHI 360 will convene the **Thailand PrEP Consultation**, to be held on **15 December 2026** at United Nations Conference Centre in Bangkok, Thailand. This national consultation will be convened to bring together key stakeholders from government agencies, healthcare providers, community-based organizations, researchers, and other key stakeholders. The consultation will review progress in PrEP implementation, discuss opportunities and challenges in service delivery, identify priority actions for strengthening HIV prevention programs, and align stakeholders on strategic directions for the introduction and future scale-up of long-acting injectable lenacapavir (LEN) and other HIV prevention interventions through 2030.

Given the importance of ensuring effective facilitation, participant engagement, and smooth event flow, the organizer seeks to engage a qualified Master of Ceremonies (MC) to support the planning and delivery of the consultation. The MC will be responsible for guiding the agenda, introducing speakers and sessions, facilitating transitions, and helping maintain participant engagement throughout the event.

**Scope of Work**

The selected Consultant shall be responsible for the comprehensive planning and delivery of professional Master of Ceremonies (MC) and facilitation services for the **Thailand PrEP Consultation**, in close coordination with FHI 360. The responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

**Task 1: Pre-Event Preparation**

**Task 4: Coordination During Workshop**

jobs.title: Thai-to-English Translation Services for Community-Based Organization (CBO) Certification and HIV/STI Service Standards Documents
jobs.description:
## **Request for Proposal (RFP)**

**Background**

FHI 360, through the Meeting Targets and Maintaining Epidemic Control (EpiC) Project, supports strengthening community-led HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) services and quality assurance systems across Asia. As part of this effort, EpiC collaborates with government and community partners to document, strengthen, and promote effective service delivery models and quality standards.

In Thailand, the Division of AIDS and STIs (DAS), Department of Disease Control, Ministry of Public Health, has developed a series of technical guidance documents, training curricula, quality monitoring tools, and assessment standards supporting Community-Based Organization (CBO) Certification and community-based HIV/STI service delivery. These materials support implementation of Reach and Recruit (RR) and Reach, Recruit, Test, Treat, Prevent, and Retain (RRTTPR) service standards and promote consistent quality of services delivered by certified community-based organizations.

To facilitate technical review, regional learning, knowledge exchange, and potential adaptation by partner countries, FHI 360 seeks qualified translation service providers to translate selected technical documents from Thai into English. The assignment covers five technical documents totalling approximately 302 source pages and 98,100 source-language words. The translated materials will be used for technical review, dissemination, donor communication, and regional adaptation. The detailed scope of services is provided below.

**Scope of Work**

The selected Consultant will provide professional Thai-to-English translation services for a package of technical documents related to Community-Based Organization (CBO) Certification and HIV/STI Service Standards. The assignment includes:

**Task 1: Translation Planning and Terminology Review (TR-1)**

- Review all source documents and reference materials.
- Establish a translation methodology and terminology management approach.
- Identify key technical terms requiring harmonization across documents.
- Develop an initial bilingual terminology framework for use throughout the assignment.

**Deliverable**: TR-1: Translation Workplan and Terminology Framework

**Task 2: Translation of Technical Documents (TR-2)**

- Translation: Translate all assigned materials from Thai into English, including narrative text, technical guidance, training materials, tables, figures, assessment tools, forms, checklists, annexes, appendices, and references.
- Language and terminology consistency: Ensure consistent language and terminology throughout the translation package.
- Document layout and formatting: Integrate all translated content into the original document layout, preserving the source documents’ structure, headings, numbering, tables, charts, and general formatting to the extent possible.

**Deliverable**: TR-2: Draft Translation Package

**Task 3: Editing, Proofreading, and Quality Assurance (TR-3)**

- Independent editing by a qualified reviewer.
- Proofreading and grammatical review.
- Terminology consistency checks.
- Verification of completeness against source documents.
- Formatting review.

The editor/reviewer must be different from the translator who performed the initial translation.

**Deliverable**: TR-3: Revised Translation Package

**Task 4: Revision and Finalization (TR-4)**

- Incorporate one consolidated round of comments provided by FHI 360 and designated reviewers.
- Resolve terminology, formatting, and consistency issues.
- Finalize all translated documents for publication and dissemination.

**Deliverable**: TR-4: Final Translation Package

**Task 5: Glossary Development and Final Submission (TR-5)**

- Finalize the bilingual glossary of technical terminology.
- Ensure consistency between glossary entries and translated documents.
- Submit all final materials in the required formats.

**Deliverable**: TR-5: Final Bilingual Glossary

**Translation Package**

**Estimated Words**

- **Guidelines for Assessment of HIV and STI Service Standards in Communities (RRTTPR Model)** (Assessment Guidelines): 68 pages, approximately 22,100 words.
- **Guidelines for Assessment of Reach and Recruit (RR) Service Standards** (Assessment Guidelines): 52 pages, approximately 16,900 words.
- **Training Curriculum for Community-Based HIV and STI Services (RR)** (Training Curriculum): 121 pages, approximately 39,300 words.
- **Guidelines for Quality Monitoring and Supervision of Certified Community-Based Organizations** (Technical Guideline): 52 pages, approximately 16,900 words.
- **Quality Monitoring and Supervision Tool and Assessment Form** (Assessment Tool): 9 pages, approximately 2,900 words.

**Total estimated volume:** 302 pages and approximately 98,100 words.

*The estimated volume is provided for planning and quotation purposes only and may vary slightly based on the final source files.*

**Deliverables and Schedule**

The assignment is expected to commence during the first week of December 2026. The timeline below is indicative. The Consultant shall propose a delivery schedule demonstrating their ability to complete all deliverables by 26 February 2027, allowing adequate time for FHI 360 review and contractor revisions.

**Deliverable ID**

**Deliverable**

**Indicative Due Date**

**Notes**

**TR-1**

Translation Workplan and Terminology Framework

Within 5 business days of assignment commencement

Includes the translation methodology, terminology management approach, quality-assurance process, and detailed delivery schedule.

**TR-2**

Draft Translation Package

Within 28 business days of assignment commencement

Complete draft English translations of all assigned materials. Bidders may propose phased submissions to facilitate earlier review.

**TR-3**

Revised Translation Package

Within 5 business days of receipt of FHI 360’s consolidated comments

Incorporates consolidated technical and editorial feedback. For planning purposes, allow 5 business days for FHI 360’s review of the draft package.

**TR-4**

Final English translations incorporating all agreed revisions, submitted in editable formats and ready for design and layout.

**TR-5**

**Location of Work:** This is a home-based assignment. The contractor may perform the work remotely from their location and shall provide the equipment, software, and internet connectivity necessary to complete the assignment.

The contractor shall be available for virtual meetings and coordination with FHI 360 during Thailand business hours (GMT+7), as reasonably required. All communications, document submissions, reviews, and feedback processes will be conducted electronically.

**Qualifications:** The contractor shall demonstrate:

jobs.title: Grants Coordinator (National / International)-Damascus
jobs.description:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 350 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery.

Our longstanding experience in the country to date provides a strong foundation for the IRC to further adapt and expand its programming across Syria, in order to respond to the new realities, with a greater focus on resilience and recovery initiatives. Alongside this, the IRC also It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and actively engaging in advocacy efforts.

Since 2012, the IRC has been at the forefront of providing lifesaving healthcare, protection, and economic recovery support across Syria. From hospitals and mobile clinics to specialized protection services and pioneering cash assistance, our programs serve the most vulnerable with dignity and care. We are also proud to nurture early childhood development through the "Ahlan Simsim" program, supporting families affected by conflict. Join us in making a lasting impact where it’s needed most. The IRC is currently funded by GFFO, BHA, ECHO, FCDO, GAC BMZ among other donors and working local organizations to ensure organizational delivery of quality and impactful services across Syria.

**Job overview:**

The IRC Syria Grants Coordinator will report to and work with the Deputy Director of Programs (DDP) for the Syria Country Program to maintain quality grants coordination. Reporting to the DDP, this position will work closely with all departments and staff including Program Coordinators, technical coordinators, finance, and operations, on compliance, donor relations, business development, and reporting. The Coordinator sitting in Damascus will supervise a team of 3 Grants Managers and Officers located in different locations.

The IRC Syria Grants Coordinator will additionally liaise with the Middle East Regional office in Amman, as well as IRC Headquarters colleagues in NY, Germany and the UK.

**Responsibilities**

**Program Design & Proposal Development**

- Support the DDP in cultivating donor relationships in Syria and the Region.
- Track upcoming opportunities by priority sectors in the country program
- Support the update and management of the BD strategy for Syria
- Support the DDP and technical leads in comprehensive business development and develop funding proposals, appropriate to the context and aligned with the country-level Strategic Action Plan.
- Lead proposal development initiatives, providing overall coordination function between HQ IRC’s global technical advisors, partners, finance, operations, HR, and program focal points to ensure smooth and timely proposal development processes.
- Serve as team lead for all proposals, working with and /or overseeing other key roles (e.g. regional support team, consultants) when needed and as resources are available to support them.
- Ensure proposals are tracked with standard IRC tracking tools (e.g. OTIS, Internal tracker)
- In collaboration with MEAL Coordinator, utilize needs assessments contextual analysis results to inform project design
- Monitor major donor trends (policies, strategic directions, etc.) and funding opportunities through regular research and monitoring of information on relevant websites and/or other sources.
- Support program growth aligned with strategic priorities through liaising and collaborating with respective technical units in program design, researching context, gaps, needs assessments, and viable new funding opportunities.
- Ensure the identification, appraisal, and mapping of partners is carried out in a constructively and consistently, and that strategic partners are appropriately engaged in pre-positioning and proposals development processes.
- Interpreting donor solicitations and donor-specific rules and regulations to ensure a responsive and compliant proposal design
- Support proposal budget develop and ensure responsiveness and that it matches the technical narrative.
- Consolidate written inputs into a cohesive proposal narrative; write non-technical sections such as the management and past performance sections.
- Edit full technical proposal and budget narrative for coherence, length, uniformity, and responsiveness to the solicitation.
- Ensure timely submission of quality proposals

**Grants Management and Compliance**

- Review and negotiate donor contracts and agreements
- Review any request for extension and amendments in coordination with the DDP and maintain a tracker for IRC and partners payments and expenditure per each grant
- Manage and provide overall oversight of the grants portfolio and regularly update the grants tracker for dissemination internally and to Awards Management Unit
- Ensure open, timely and accurate information flow within the Grants Unit and between the Unit and relevant departments
- Ensure the submission of timely and high-quality reports (including narrative, financial and MEAL) to donors, including the development and update of regular funding and reporting trackers and schedules for dissemination to relevant staff
- Maintain strong oversight of the portfolio and pipeline, including grant opening and closing dates to ensure timely submission of all related deliverables
- Provide technical guidance on IRC and donor regulations to ensure compliance within operations, program implementation and reporting
- Raise compliance issues proactively with program staff and the DDP, and SMT for timely action and keep senior management informed of any projected inabilities to meet contractual obligations, reports submission and of spend rates/signification budget variances.
- Manage and/or support all agreements reviews, revisions, amendments, and budget realignments, including relevant approvals
- Leads the Grants Unit to coordinate closely with finance teams and review project spending plans and financial health to ensure effective spending amendments, and closeout activities
- In coordination with DDP, conduct project lessons learned meeting during project closeout phase

***Staff Performance Management, Learning & Development***

- Develop and implement remote management capacity-building approaches to build the strengths of the teams in Syria.
- Coach, train, supervise, and mentor direct-report staff, including communicating clear expectations, setting annual performance objectives, providing regular and timely positive and constructive performance feedback, and providing documented semi-annual performance reviews.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Approve and manage time, attendance and leave requests to ensure adequate departmental coverage; ensure monthly, accurate timesheet submission and carry out probationary reviews.
- Hold high-quality meetings with each direct report on a regular and predictable basis, minimally on a monthly basis.
- Provide a measurable development plan including on-the-job learning with the aim of strengthening technical capacity, exchanging knowledge within the team and providing guidance on career paths.
- As required, identify staff performance issues and work with Human Resources to document and address these in accordance with the National Staff Employment Policies.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Promote and monitor staff care and well-being. Model healthy work-life balance practices. Support appropriate interventions in response to identified staff care needs of both national and international staff.
- Look for opportunities to support staff in their career growth, where appropriate
- Adhere to and act in accordance with the IRC Global HR Policies and Procedures and communicate through word and example a high standard of compliance with all applicable policies.

**Partnerships**

- Contribute to achievement of goals related to the SAP partnerships ambition including identification and onboarding of Strategic Partners
- Embody and model IRC values related to partnerships (partner as equals, partner first) and facilitate this approach in implementation of IRC programs
- Support development and maintenance of strategic partnerships.
- Support negotiation of partner sub award agreements in coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator, Award Management Unit and Compliance Unit

**Representation and Advocacy**

- In coordination with the DDP, actively develop and maintain effective working relationships with stakeholders including local communities, donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs, and other relevant actors.
- Liaise with county and national governments, donors, NGOs, and other operational partners in Syria via attendance at meetings, consultations and other forums.
- In coordination with the DDP, assist in organizing donor visits by supporting staff in the smooth design and running of field visits.

**Country Program Management and Strategic Planning**

- Actively participate in and contribute to strategy discussions, including SAP revision processes
- Stay updated on new IRC priorities, policies, or process updates and ensure Grants & Partnerships and MEAL units are informed of any changes.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education**

A degree in International Studies, Development, or a related field is required. Alternatively, a Bachelor’s degree combined with substantial experience in grants management and excellent writing skills may be considered. Equivalent experience in a similar role may also be accepted in place of formal education.

**Work Experience**

- At least 8 years of demonstrated field-based experience with humanitarian grants management, possibly including experience working with sub-grantee partners to build their capacity to access and account for resources. 5 years of this experience should be working in relief and development contexts.
- At least 3 years in a managerial position, including staff management

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Excellent writing skills and experience in writing proposals/concept notes.
- Strong understanding and knowledge of USAID, PRM, FCDO, UN SIDA, FCDO, USG, GFFO, EU, ECHO and private donor rules and regulations.
- Proven competency with program design, M&E, proposal writing (including logical frameworks) and building budgets.
- Excellent management and coordination skills.
- Solid ability to provide team- building, coaching, and development for staff as well as encourage cross-functional collaboration and cooperation.
- Ability to work independently while being a strong team player.
- Excellent relationship-building, interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively represent IRC at forums and with donors.
- Full professional competency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook.
- High attention to detail and excellent time management skills
- Excellent leadership and management skills including coaching, mentoring and managing teams
- Politically astute, with well-developed diplomatic and negotiating skills.
- Superior oral and written communication skills, with ability to express ideas and concepts clearly and persuasively with senior internal and external stakeholders.
- Extensive representation and fundraising success, including prior experience with European, US and other international and private donors.
- Established capacity to deal with ambiguity in stressful situations.
- Strong commitment to IRC’s vision, mission and core values.
- Proven ability to design and lead training engagements with staff and partners to enhance skills and adapt to changing program demands

**Language/Travel:**

**Travel**: minimum 10% percent travel

**Language**: Fluency in English, written and spoken is mandatory, and Arabic is desirable

**Key Working Relationships:**

***Position Reports to***: Deputy Director for Programs, with close working relationships with Technical Advisors

***Position directly supervises***: Grants Managers

***Internal contacts:*** Awards Management Unit, MEAL, Program Coordinators, Supply Chain, Finance, HR, Partnerships Research Evaluation and Learning Technical Unit

***External***: Clusters and working group

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

jobs.title: Regional Analyst - West & Central Africa region
jobs.description:
**About INSO**

Founded in 2011, the International NGO Safety Organization (INSO) is an international NGO that supports humanitarian aid workers by establishing safety coordination platforms in insecure contexts. INSO provides registered NGOs with a range of free services, including real-time incident tracking, analytical reports, safety-related data and mapping, crisis management support, staff orientations, and training. INSO provides daily support to more than 1,500 NGOs operating in 24 of the world’s most insecure countries. INSO is registered in the Netherlands, with its headquarters located in The Hague, a city renowned for its international focus on peace and justice.

**INSO West Africa and Lake Chad Basin**

Since 2013, INSO has supported the humanitarian community across the region and is looking to establish a regional presence for West Africa at the request of the NGO community. This position is based in Dakar, Senegal, and reports to the Regional Director, under the technical guidance of the Global Analysis Team at Headquarters.

**Job Summary**

As Regional Analyst, you will assist NGOs working in, but not limited to, the Central Sahel, the West African Coastal States, and parts of the Lake Chad Basin through analysis of broader trends and dynamics, such as regional or contextual developments that shape humanitarian safety and access in the region.

**Major** **Responsibilities**

*Service Delivery*

- Prepare and produce reports to help NGO partners assess prevalent regional conflict dynamics and their impact on humanitarian safety and access.
- Initiate delivery of regional services, designing outputs in line with partner requirements and priorities.
- Manage and deliver ad hoc products on emerging regional challenges to humanitarian safety and access.
- Contribute to other countries’ office products and inform decision-making at the regional level.
- Offer a responsive, tailored analysis service directly to INSO’s NGO partners upon their request.
- Convene and contribute to regional NGO coordination meetings and fora with humanitarian counterparts to discuss regional safety and access.

*Local acceptance*

- Build a network of partners and interlocutors working on humanitarian activities in West Africa and Lake Chad, including NGOs, UN agencies, government representatives, and other actors involved in security coordination and information sharing.
- Establish a clear role for INSO within the humanitarian security architecture in West Africa.

*Representation*

When requested and in coordination with the Coastal Countries CD

- Represent the organization at the country and regional levels, and ensure adherence to INSO mission, policies, and principles.
- Build and maintain strong networks with government agencies, NGOs, the UN, Red Cross, donors, embassies, humanitarian coordination platforms, and security bodies while maintaining independence.
- Proactively seek opportunities to represent INSO at relevant events and forums
- Effectively represent and protect INSO’s principles of independence, impartiality, and neutrality; promote INSO as an integral member of the humanitarian community.
- Stay updated on political, security, and humanitarian developments in West Africa and Lake Chad Basin region, and provide regular strategic analysis.

*Program strategy and management*

- Assist the Country Director in the development of a regional strategy through consultation with internal and external stakeholders.
- Liaise and coordinate with INSO’s Global Analysis Team to enable analytical capacity building in the countries’ offices when needed.

**Requirements**

- A minimum of 5 years of work experience in an analytical capacity, preferably working on conflict or post-conflict contexts in West Africa and the Lake Chad region
- Experience working in NGOs, international organisations, consultancy, or journalism
- Exemplary command of French and at least professional fluency in English is required.
- Proven ability to provide operationally relevant analysis to a wide-ranging audience
- The administrative ability to travel to all countries in West Africa
- Demonstrable understanding of humanitarian safety practices and their application
- Excellent networking, diplomatic, and representative communication skills
- Graduate-level education in political science, history, or humanitarian studies, or a related field, or equivalent work experience

**Nice-to-have**

- Experience delivering a partner-focused advisory service
- Experience designing and delivering products based on close partner engagement
- Existing regional experience and/or information networks
- Experience in insecure/conflict-affected environments
- Experience in staff capacity development and training
- Detailed understanding of INSO’s mandate & services

**Core Competencies**

- Critical Thinking - Ability to analyse complex situations, question assumptions, and develop sound, practical solutions through logical reasoning.
- Communication - Ability to convey information clearly, build positive relationships, and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.
- Organisation - Ability to plan, prioritise, and manage tasks efficiently while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
- Autonomy - Ability to work independently, take initiative, and make informed decisions while remaining accountable for results.
- Teamwork - Ability to contribute positively to team objectives through reliability, collaboration, cultural awareness, and mutual support.

**INSO’s Safeguarding Policy**

INSO is fully committed to safe recruitment, selection and vetting of all potential new staff, trustees and volunteers. We ensure rigorous compliance with our Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy throughout the recruitment process. INSO is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and the selected candidate will be required to undergo the relevant misconduct disclosure checks as part of the final hiring steps.

**Terms & Conditions**

12-month renewable contract, based in Dakar, Senegal. €5000 per month salary, 4 calendar days of annual leave per month and 3 days of R&R every 3 months without allowance, global medical coverage (excluding USA) and AD&D insurance.

jobs.title: Transparency and Compliance Assistant
