- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP.

In Ukraine, UNDP has been working since 1993 with the Government and local authorities, partners across the UN system, civil society and local communities to help identify and develop targeted solutions to the country’s development challenges. We work in close collaboration with several key ministries, departments, and agencies in a robust, integrated manner in three thematic priorities/portfolios:

• Inclusive Development, Recovery and Peacebuilding,

• Democratic Governance, and

• Energy and Environment.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine, through its Energy and Environment Portfolio, supports national and local authorities in restoring, modernizing and transforming Ukraine’s energy and public infrastructure in line with the principles of sustainability, resilience, energy security and transparency. Since the full-scale war, UNDP has placed particular emphasis on ensuring continuity of essential public services while supporting Ukraine’s green and resilient recovery. Within this framework, UNDP works closely with the Ministry of Energy of Ukraine, the Ministry for Development of Communities and Territories of Ukraine (MDCT), local authorities and other national and international partners to implement programmes aimed at improving the energy performance of public infrastructure, increasing the use of renewable energy sources and strengthening the capacity of municipalities to plan and manage sustainable energy investments.

The Project Manager will lead the implementation of the Accelerating the Energy Decentralization and Green Transformation in Ukraine project, that supports the development and deployment of decentralized renewable energy solutions as part of Ukraine’s green recovery and energy transformation. The project will promote localized renewable energy solutions in selected oblasts and municipalities, with interventions identified through participatory approaches and tailored to local energy needs and conditions. The project combines infrastructure investments with technical assistance and institutional capacity development. It will assess the technical and economic feasibility of renewable energy solutions and develop recommendations on de-risking mechanisms, financing approaches and policy or regulatory measures required to create a more enabling environment for renewable energy investment at the sub-national level.

Job Purpose

The Project Manager will directly manage the Accelerating the Energy Decentralization and Green Transformation in Ukraine project and other related projects within the Energy and Environment Portfolio, in line with evolving projects needs and the portfolio’s approach and contribute to the efforts of the UNDP Country Office in the respective programmatic area. The Project Manager will supervise the project team, coordinate implementation with participating UN agencies and relevant partners, and support successful project delivery through strategic planning, implementation oversight, capacity development, monitoring and assurance, advocacy, and knowledge management.

The incumbent will work under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the UNDP Deputy Resident Representative (Programme) and in close day-to-day collaboration with the Energy and Environment Portfolio Specialist (Team Leader) in the UNDP country office.

The Project Manager will prioritize gender equality and women’s empowerment within all implementations and promote UNDP’s mandate as a gender-responsive organization with zero tolerance for any kind of discriminatory and abusive behavior, including sexual harassment, sexual exploitation, and abuse.

Impact of results:

Effective performance of the Project Manager will contribute to the timely and high-quality delivery of project results, strengthened partnerships with national and international stakeholders, improved institutional and technical capacities, and the advancement of Ukraine’s decentralized, resilient and green energy transformation.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams to strengthen horizontal collaboration and maximize synergies across the portfolio.

Duties and Responsibilities

1) Provide strategic leadership for effective project planning and implementation:

- Lead strategic planning of the Accelerating the Energy Decentralization and Green Transformation in Ukraine project, including formulation of annual project work plan (AWP) as well as plans for budget, HR, procurement, and overall project implementation.

- Provide quality and timely management of the project life cycle, including meeting programmatic and financial deliverables in adherence to project documents and applicable UNDP policy and programme management procedures and Government standards, rules, and regulations. Act as a senior advisor on issues related to project activities.

- Provide direction, guidance and direct supervision of Accelerating the Energy Decentralization and Green Transformation in Ukraine project personnel, including technical experts, to ensure activities are implemented in a timely manner as planned. Undertake technical review of project documents produced by the project team and partners, and ensure high technical standards are met.

- Ensure all project interventions integrate a gender equality perspective/gender equality mainstreaming to the extent local context allows.

- Ensure proper execution of all administrative activities associated with project implementation that includes building and sustaining effective liaison with the CO’s functional areas and units (i.e., programme, M&E, finance, HR, procurement, and supply management).

- Ensure timely delivery of technical, operational, financial and administrative outputs in accordance with approved plans.

- Oversee procurement-related requirements for project implementation, including preparation and/or quality assurance of terms of reference, technical specifications and requirements for goods, works and services, in coordination with relevant UNDP units.

- Ensure appropriate transfer and handover of project outputs and deliverables to national beneficiaries and other relevant stakeholders, in line with applicable UNDP procedures.

- Contribute to resource mobilization efforts, including identification of funding opportunities and development of approaches to support the expansion and sustainability of project activities.

- Identify opportunities for synergies with other projects within UNDP and beyond to advance the key objectives and grow its focus, ensure active engagement at related Thematic Team.

2) Build and maintain UNDP’s strategic partnerships:

- Substantively contribute to the harnessing of effective partnerships and lead the identification and onboarding process for implementing partners.

- Cultivate and maintain strong relationships and strategic linkages with implementing and development partners, government officials, businesses, NGOs, other national and regional stakeholders, and beneficiaries to support and ensure accurate interpretation of key objectives, and to promote inclusive project implementation.

- Communicate relevant and critical information with key implementing partners and members of project governing bodies and substantively contribute to project visibility efforts. Make recommendations to the EE Team Leader and CO management team on activities with potential for scale-up, replicability and synergies.

- Provide technical support to the implementing partners and act as a liaison between UNDP and the partners.

- Maintain regular dialogue and coordination with donors and development partners, including participation in relevant donor coordination mechanisms, intergovernmental meetings and other strategic coordination platforms.

- Support effective functioning of project governance mechanisms, including preparation for Project Board meetings, timely provision of substantive inputs and follow-up on agreed decisions and actions.

- Promote a safe and enabling environment free of any kind of discrimination and abusive behavior.

3) Monitor and report on progress in implementing project activities and achieving the targets set:

- Provide leadership and technical advice to the Accelerating the Energy Decentralization and Green Transformation in Ukraine project in developing baselines and indicators for project monitoring and evaluation and coordinate the finalization of detailed results framework. Ensure strategies, processes, systems, and mechanisms are in place to effectively fulfill projects and financial monitoring, evaluation, quality assurance and reporting requirements.

- Lead implementation of the monitoring, evaluation, and results framework to identify plan deviations, underperformance, and other problems. Support diagnosing problems and ensure accountability for corrective actions within agreed upon tolerances to achieve results. Conduct field visits as required to verify project activities relative to stated targets and provide regular field updates to UNDP EE Team Lead and CO management.

- Proactively perform risk assessments to identify and document risks related to the project, including operational, financial, legal, contractual, social, environmental, reputation and safety risks. Design mitigation measures and keep appropriate project governing bodies informed. Develop and complete regular reviews of risk management matrix for the project.

- Coordinate the preparation of corporate, donor and government reports in line with the reporting schedule and UNDP and donor requirements. Ensure provision of ad hoc reports and information requested by relevant entities.

- Ensure accurate monitoring of project financial resources, expenditures and financial reporting, in coordination with relevant UNDP units and in accordance with applicable internal control requirements.

- Facilitate project monitoring, evaluation and audit activities and ensure timely follow-up on recommendations and agreed actions.

- Ensure project information and implementation progress are accurately maintained in relevant UNDP corporate management systems, in accordance with applicable procedures.

- Ensure proper operational and financial closure of the project.

4) Lead knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area(s) and UNDP.

- Identify capacity building needs and opportunities. Ensure appropriate training and other relevant capacity building activities are organized and implemented in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia. Lead workshops with senior level officials and stakeholders.

- Ensure project results, lessons learned, good practices and relevant experience are systematically documented, communicated and used to inform future programming, replication and scale-up.

- Proactively identify and pursue opportunities for the documentation and communication of best practices, project results, and lessons learned under the project.

- Actively participate in and make substantive contributions to external networks and communities of practice to promote advocacy for UNDP’s work and opportunities for collaboration in addressing development trends. Represent UNDP in relevant technical meetings and working groups under the direction of CO management.

- Support establishment of knowledge platforms and innovative mechanisms for capturing and disseminating knowledge from the project; and ensure development of knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

- Contribute to development and implementation of the project communications and visibility approach, ensuring appropriate visibility of UNDP, donors and project results in accordance with applicable requirements.

- Support outreach activities, including relevant seminars, workshops, conferences and public-facing events, and contribute to preparation of communication and advocacy materials.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Manage and supervise Project personnel

Competencies

Core: Full list of UNDP Core Competencies can be found here

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

- Business Direction & Strategy System thinking • Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Business Development Knowledge Facilitation • Ability to animate individuals and communities of contributors to participate and share, particularly externally.

- Business Management Project Management • Ability to plan, organize, prioritize, and control resources, procedures, and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Business Management Communication • Ability to communicate in a clear, concise, and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience • Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels

- Partnership Management Relationship Management • Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust, and mutual understanding

- 2030 Agenda: People Gender • Gender and Energy

- 2030 Agenda: Peace Conflict Prevention, Peacebuilding and Responsive Institutions • Infrastructure for Peace

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Economics, Business Administration, Public Administration, Energy, Political Sciences, International Economic Relations, Social Sciences, or related field is required, or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 7 years (with a Master’s degree) or 9 years (with a Bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible experience at the international level in project management, quality assurance, management advisory services, monitoring and evaluation of development projects, and partnership management, including engagement with international development cooperation partners is required.

- Demonstrated experience in project planning and implementation related to green recovery and energy sector recovery and rehabilitation is an asset. Experience in advancing the Build Back Better (BBB) and Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principles are desirable.

- Extensive experience in the design and management of large-scale projects in cooperation with relevant public- and private-sector stakeholders at both national and local levels is desirable.

- Strong experience in stakeholder coordination in the energy sector is desirable.

- Experience engaging with institutions and development partners from the Republic of Korea, including government agencies and other Korean development cooperation institutions, particularly in energy recovery, infrastructure rehabilitation, and green transition, is a strong asset. Previous programme/project management experience within the UN system is an asset.

- Proven ability to draft, edit and produce proposals, advisory and analytical documents, and results-focused reports. Experience preparing documentation and coordinating reporting processes for international development partners, including Korean development cooperation institutions, is an advantage.

- Experience using computers and standard office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) is required.

- Basic proficiency in Korean is an asset.

jobs.location: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

At the country level, UNV Field Units (FUs) and designated UNV personnel are responsible for promoting volunteerism through the mobilization of UN Volunteers across the UN system in the areas of peace, development, human rights and humanitarian assistance. FUs represent and position UNV within the respective countries, particularly within the UN country team, adopting a client-oriented and solutions-based approach.

As UNV is the systemwide service administered by UNDP, FUs are hosted within relevant UNDP offices, collaborating closely with the UNDP resident representative and the UN resident coordinator system. The UNV country coordinator ensures compliance with UNV and UNDP policies, rules, and regulations.

Scope of Work

- Promote Volunteer Mobilization

- Position UNV as a system-wide service provider supporting UN partners to achieve their programmes and UNSDCF goals. Develop and implement country-level volunteer mobilization strategies aligned with UNV’s Strategic Framework and partner demand.

- Participate in UN collective planning processes (CCA, UNSDCF, humanitarian response plans, thematic task forces) to integrate volunteerism in their implementation.

- Present UNV’s value proposition to maximize contributions of UN Volunteers, and guide partners in developing volunteer assignment descriptions.

- Support local talent outreach and acquisition efforts in alignment with corporate strategies.

- Promote Online Volunteering as a core component of UNV’s offer.

- Monitor mobilization trends, track key performance indicators, and use corporate tools (CRM, BI reports, UVP) for informed decision-making.

- Facilitate executive, operational, and partnership missions by UNV.

2. Build Strategic Partnerships

- Build and sustain effective relationships with UN partners to promote UNV’s mandate and services.

- Analyze country strategies (UNSDCF, agency strategies) to identify opportunities for volunteer mobilization.

- Maintain business intelligence on UN programming, funding and workforce trends to diversify partnerships and forecast volunteer demand.

- Engage regularly the heads of agencies, their management teams and senior programme and operations staff to support volunteer mobilization, collaborating proactively to identify opportunities.

- In coordination with the RO and ERCS, map and pursue SVF mobilization opportunities.

- Engage with government, civil society, private sector, and development partners in close coordination with other UN entities as may be required to realize agreed objectives.

3. Ensure Duty of Care

- Support host entities with guidance and best practices to ensure successful volunteer assignments.

- Work closely with UNDSS, the UN Designated Official for security, and host agencies to ensure the safety, security, and inclusion of UN Volunteers. Provide timely support during security evacuations.

- Ensure volunteers receive appropriate briefings, orientation, and guidance from host entities on arrival and benefit from appropriate supervision throughout their assignment.

- Brief the volunteer on expected code of conduct and other relevant factors for a successful experience; be available to answer questions.

- Conduct regular field visits to volunteer locations and monitor volunteer well-being and provide guidance on critical administrative aspects.

- Facilitate regular engagement with and among volunteers (e.g., town halls, networking, and community activities) to strengthen volunteer experience and well-being.

4. Promote Advocacy on Volunteerism

- Align communications with volunteer mobilization and talent acquisition goals, develop impactful volunteer stories in collaboration with the RO and External Relations and Communications Section (ERCS), promote UNV at national, regional and global levels.

- Stay informed of national volunteer initiatives, policies and strategies, including those supported by the UN system, and share relevant updates with Volunteer Advisory Services Section.

- Stay informed of host countries’ aspirations to promote national volunteer talent through fully funded UNV assignments domestically and abroad, share relevant updates with ERCS on emerging demand for UNV solutions, and support their implementation if needed.

- Stay informed of the International Volunteer Day and other volunteer recognition efforts by national counterparts and, where appropriate, collaborate around respective activities in close coordination with UN country teams and upon advice from the RO and ERCS.

- Encourage volunteers to act as advocates and disseminate their experiences as advocates and ambassadors of volunteer action.

5. Ensure Effective Field Unit Management

- Lead and coordinate the FU to ensure effective and efficient service delivery and a collaborative work environment.

- Supervise, empower and ensure performance and accountability of FU team members. Provide coaching and oversight to ensure consistency and client orientation in the FU’s communication with all clients.

- Develop, monitor, and manage the FU’s annual work plan and budget in compliance with performance targets and UNDP regulations.

- Liaise with UNDP programme and operations teams to ensure administrative support, alignment with local protocol, and facilitate cooperation on critical issues such as visas for international volunteers.

- Ensure that the FU undertake assigned transactions in the Volunteer Management Cycle in accordance with corporate SOPs. Escalate operational and reputational risks and other significant issues promptly to the RO.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the regional manager and direct supervision of the portfolio manager or specialist in the Regional Office (RO), the country coordinator manages the FU and leads UNV’s engagement at the country level.

The role’s primary purpose is to ensure that UNV effectively anticipates and responds to the needs of the UN system and partners by mobilizing qualified volunteers and promoting volunteerism across sectors. This includes strategic positioning, partnership building, advocacy, and contribution to UNV’s Strategic Framework implementation.

The country coordinator works under the general guidance of the UN resident coordinator to position UNV and its services within the UN system and liaises regularly with the UNDP resident representative for support. The incumbent also collaborates closely with the UNDP country office for administrative matters, participates in UN country team activities as invited (including joint UN programme, operations, communications teams and other subsidiary groups of UNCT), and may represent UNV in joint coordination mechanisms with government and non-government stakeholders.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

- Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Systems Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgment to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

Integration within the UN System

- Ability to identify and integrate the capacity and assets of the UN system and engage in joint work. Knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations

Results-based Management

- Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools

Partnerships Management

- Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends

Event planning and execution

- Ability to plan, manage and execute of public and private events to ensure that they support and amplify individual communications and advocacy initiatives, as well as UNV's overall brand and mandate

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Social Sciences, International Development, Project Management, Public/Business Administration or related fields is required, OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with Master’s degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience preferably in a humanitarian, development and/or peace related field is required

Required skills:

- Experience in partnerships and management

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Work experience with the United Nations is an asset

- Experience in advocacy, public relations, or communication is an asset

- Experience in programme reporting, monitoring and evaluation is an asset

- Experience in volunteer management and/or promotion of volunteerism is an asset

- Experience in working in digital platforms and tools, including CRM and ERP systems is an asset

Languages:

- Fluency in English and French is required

- Working knowledge of an other UN official language is desirable

Disclaimer:

- Only short-listed applicants will be contacted

- The successful candidate will hold a UNDP IPSA contract

- This vacancy announcement is open to tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Under the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, the organization focuses on four strategic objectives: Prosperity for All, Effective Governance, Crisis Resilience, and Healthy Planet, supported by the accelerators of Digital and Artificial Intelligence (AI) Transformation, Gender Equality, and Sustainable Finance. These priorities are underpinned by a commitment to human rights and leaving no one behind.

The UNDP Pacific Multi-Country Office (MCO), headquartered in Fiji, serves ten Pacific Island countries: Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia (FSM), Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI), Republic of Naoero, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu, while also supporting regional initiatives. UNDP's Pacific programme is guided by the Multi-Country Programme Document (MCPD) 2023-2027, which is aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) 2023-2027, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, the SAMOA Pathway, and the 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent. The programme promotes integrated approaches to resilience, climate action, inclusive growth, governance, and sustainable development across the Pacific region.

The UNDP Pacific Sub-Office in Pohnpei, established in 2021, serves FSM, Kiribati, Republic of Naoero, Palau, and RMI, working closely with the Fiji MCO to deliver development programmes and support national priorities. Through its programme portfolio, UNDP provides strategic policy advice, technical assistance, programme oversight, partnership development, resource mobilization, and knowledge sharing to governments and development partners across the Northern Pacific.

UNDP has maintained a longstanding presence in Solomon Islands since 1999 and is recognized as a trusted development partner supporting national priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals. Its programme portfolio spans governance, peacebuilding, access to justice, anti-corruption, gender equality, youth and women's empowerment, climate resilience, disaster risk management, environmental sustainability, and digital transformation. jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The islands of Bougainville are an integral yet autonomous region of Papua New Guinea (PNG). In 2001, the Bougainville Peace Agreement (BPA) was signed between the national Government of Papua New Guinea (GoPNG) and leaders representing the people of Bougainville. The BPA marked the end of a decade-long civil conflict in which up to 20,000 men and women died and many more were left traumatized, without family, access to basic services, education and infrastructure. The UN has supported peacebuilding and post-conflict transition in Bougainville since the establishment in 1998 of the UN Political Office in Bougainville (UNPOB). The subsequent Observer Mission for Bougainville (UNOMB) facilitated and monitored the three key tenets of the BPA: a referendum on the independence of Bougainville, weapons disposal and the establishment of good governance, and the transfer of powers and functions (generally referred to as the ‘draw down’ of powers).

Autonomy arrangements came into force in 2001, and the first Autonomous Bougainville Government (ABG) was established in 2005. Following this, the non-binding Bougainville Referendum was held in 2019, in which 97.7% of the population of the region voted for independence. Subsequent agreements and documents, including the 2021 Sharp Agreement and Wabag Road Map took steps to outline the process of the transfer of functions and powers to Bougainville ahead of the 2025-2027 timeline for Independence.

The BPA stipulates that following the referendum, the two parties to the agreement will consult over its results, with the outcome subject to ratification by the National Parliament. Following several rounds of post-referendum consultations, a Joint Supervisory Body (JSB) resolution was signed in 2024 which agreed the engagement of an independent Moderator to support the Government of PNG and ABG in their consultations. In September 2024, Prime Minister Hon. James Marape and President Hon. Ishmael Toroama requested the UN to support engagement of a Moderator and establishment of an independent Secretariat to support the Moderator’s programme. The Moderator supported consultations which led to the signing of the Melanesian Agreement in June 2025, a key milestone in the Bougainville Peace Process which outlines a pathway forward in accordance with both the national Constitution and the Bougainville Peace Agreement. The Melanesian Agreement reflects a shared commitment to a close, peaceful, and enduring relationship, and commits the parties to exploring the creation of a ‘Melanesian Framework’ with agreed timelines for a pathway forward. The Agreement also calls for UN support with monitoring and implementation to ensure progress and sustained commitment. In turn, in 2026, the UN provided a package of support based on an Independent Facilitator Consultation Mechanism to support third party facilitation of continued dialogue between the parties.

Twenty-five years after the signing of the BPA, the Autonomous Region of Bougainville is entering a decisive, uncertain and time-sensitive phase of its post-conflict transition. The referendum results and outcomes from joint consultations are due to be submitted to Papua New Guinea’s Parliament in late 2026, and Bougainville has identified September 2027 as a proposed political milestone to announce future arrangements regarding its self-governance. The ongoing political process therefore represents a narrow but critical window for proactive engagement for sustaining peace and reinforcing reconciliation to secure the foundations of a prosperous future for the region.

In Bougainville, development, peace, and security expectations remain high yet understanding of possible future scenarios varies across communities. To sustain peace during this period, UN interventions must therefore address the risk that uncertainty around the political process, combined with limited access to accurate and timely information, misinformation/disinformation, unresolved grievances and trauma, and uneven institutional readiness, could erode confidence and trigger localized or wider instability.

In recent years, UNDP programming has sought to meetBougainvillean aspirations of peacebuilding and reconciliation, ensuring peace dividends and longer-term socio-economic recovery. A dynamic range of UNDP projects include flagship Innovation Hubs to pave the way for Bougainville women, youth and innovators to create employment and entrepreneurial opportunities by providing improved access to business development skills and services; support to gender transformative peacebuilding through joint programming on Women, Peace and Security; parliamentary strengthening support to the Bougainville House of Representatives, including dedicated support to the joint parliamentary Women’s Caucus of PNG; support to civil society organisations; and rollout of renewable solar system for communities in South Bougainville to build resilience through expansion of renewable energy access. This area-based and multi-sectoral approach to development reflects the need for holistic and well-integrated programming to maximize development opportunities in Bougainville, while strengthening governance, service delivery and oversight institutions.

In the emerging context outlined above, UNDP wishes to enhance the technical capacities, local ownership and coordination of its governance and peacebuilding programming support at a critical juncture in Bougainville’s peace and development journey. As part of a new UN Peacebuilding Fund joint project ‘Sustaining Peace for Bougainville’s Future’, convened by UNDP, a Programme Coordinator is sought to drive forward work on local peacebuilding, dialogue and reconciliation, and institution-building, as part of broader management of area-based programming in Bougainville.

Position Purpose

To launch the new Sustaining Peace joint project, UNDP is seeking a Programme Coordinator who will work directly with the participating UN organizations (PUNO) and in close coordination with ABG and GoPNG (including the National Coordination Office for Bougainville Affairs, NCOBA) to ensure the successful implementation of the project. The Programme Coordinator will serve as technical lead on governance, peacebuilding and post-conflict transition in Bougainville, overseeing conflict and political economy analysis and ensuring the quality of UNDP technical support on local peacebuilding, strategic communications, public sector reform and community development (including livelihoods).

The Programme Coordinator will work to establish effective implementation of joint project activities to ensure technical coherence and greater impact. The position will support the translation of strategic and programmatic decisions taken by the Programme Steering Committee (PSC) to the planning of activities while also advising the PSC on potential implications of those decisions practically and strategically. The Programme Coordinator will lead the joint project management team of all PUNOs of Sustaining Peace to facilitate and be closely involved in the joint planning, monitoring, coordination and reporting of work plan activities to optimize cooperation, co-creation, mutual support, economies of scale and complementarity of joint action (including site selection, phasing of activities) based on the comparative advantages of the various UN agencies for maximum impact.

Alongside management of the Sustaining Peace joint project, the Programme Coordinator will oversee broader UNDP programmatic interventions in Bougainville, working in close coordination with the Autonomous Bougainville Government and local civil society organisations to ensure an integrated area-based approach. The position will be closely involved in advising the implementation of multisectoral activities (including UNDP’s governance, gender equality, economic transformation and environment programming) in Bougainville. The incumbent will work closely with internal and external counterparts, including Government, national institutions, civil society, private sector etc, to ensure successful delivery of the UN and UNDP programmes at the local level.

The Programme Coordinator will report directly to the Assistant Resident Representative (Governance, Peace and Gender), while working under the strategic guidance of the UNDP Resident Representative and Deputy Resident Representative. The incumbent will work in consultation with the Office of the UN Resident Coordinator and Buka-based Liaison Officer of the Department for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs. The position will be based at the UN’s Joint Field Office in Buka (Bougainville).

The Programme Coordinator will act as the head of UN/UNDP Field office in Buka (Bougainville), while providing support and oversight of the UNDP’s projects with activities operating in the region. The Programme Coordinator supervises relevant project staff working in Bougainville, ensuring cross-unit cooperation and coordination, while working closely with the UNDP Operations Manager on the operational management of the Buka Office.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Lead High -Level Technical Advisory: Governance, Institutions and Post-Conflict Transition

• Carry out high-quality conflict analysis and mapping and oversee establishment of a planned early warning and early action system under the Sustaining Peace project and support the design of conflict sensitive programmatic adaptations when needed by UNDP and PUNOs

• Ensure quality of UNDP technical support on local peacebuilding, strategic communications, public sector reform and community development (including livelihoods), including direct technical leadership of peacebuilding, mediation, prevention and reconciliation initiatives

• Lead provision of high-quality technical advisory and capacity development support to ABG and GoPNG mandated departments on conflict prevention, peacebuilding and Bougainville Affairs, and to local conflict monitoring and mediation actors to strengthen sustainable local infrastructures for peace

• Maintain working relationships with key governance and peace stakeholders at local and institutional levels, including key ABG departments, development partner implementing agencies and CSO networks.

2. Lead Effective Management of UN/UNDP Sustaining Peace in Bougainville Programme

• Organize biannual Programme Steering Committee meetings providing secretarial support on behalf of the participating UN agencies and facilitate the decision making of the steering committee, including providing programmatic information and background documents

3. Ensure Programme Design, Development and Knowledge Management

• Ensure regular strategic engagement with ABG and GoPNG (including NCOB), and UNRCO and DPPA, ensuring political and conflict sensitivity of activities amidst to the ongoing political process

• Establish regular communication and alignment with key stakeholders and coordination mechanisms, and respective development, humanitarian and private sector actors operating in Bougainville

• Provide timely and effective critical analysis of political, social, economic and environmental matters that impact UN programming in Bougainville and/or UN’s capacity to deliver in the operating context.

• Maintain situational awareness of evolving operational environment including through establishing and maintain an informal information network to facilitate information sharing.

• Lead the development of UN/UNDP programmes to support the ABG’s reform initiatives, development plans and financing of critical governance and service delivery functions, with a focus on gender equaity

• Deliver strategic recommendations on programme direction and possible areas for future assistance.

• Support the development of policy options and programme development for UN in Bougainville.

• Produce or support production of key knowledge products (research papers, data profiles) as well as substantial communications (articles, blogs).

Lead knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing, and advocacy

4. Strategic Partnerships, Reporting, Resource Mobilization and Donor Liaison

• Maintain strategic relationships with ABG and relevant GoPNG departments and key actors

• Lead resource mobilization for governance, peace building, humanitarian, development and resilience efforts, by maintaining close liaison with the development partners, civil society and the private sector.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with existing, new and/or potential donors, including site visits and other orientation activities

• Maintain strong relationships with relevant IFIs at provincial and national levels

• Prepare regular progress reports on implementation of the Programme, as required by donors and/or requested by ABG or other key stakeholders

• Perform other work-related tasks to support reporting and resource mobilization for UNDP and other participating United Nations Agencies.

5. People management and Operational Management of the UN/UNDP Field Office in Bougainville

• Manage the UN/UNDP Field office in Buka (Bougainville), while working closely with the UNDP Operations Manager on the operational management of the Buka Office.

• Manage and oversee programme t personnel working in Bougainville, ensuring cross-unit cooperation and coordination, gender equality, and prevention of sexual exploitation, harassment and abuse

• Oversee security planning and reporting including support to PUNO travel and security planning during project implementation, with regular engagement with UNDSS

• Ensure that the field office, staff oversight, and UNDP assets, including vehicles, are managed in compliance with UNDP’s policies and procedures.

• Establish regular coordination with local stakeholders, partners and suppliers to support the delivery of UN/UNDP programmes and activities in Bougainville.

Right to select multiple candidates
