jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Within UNDP’s Bureau for Management Services (BMS), the Office of Human Resources (OHR), is the Management Consulting Team (MCT), which is constituted of a group of management consulting practitioners available on request to support UNDP offices and units worldwide to improve strategic and organizational effectiveness in line with UNDP’s Strategic Plan and corporate investments in organizational effectiveness and agility. This group is anchored by a core team of management advisors and consultants based in Bonn, who coordinate and deliver management consulting services globally in a participatory manner

Position Purpose

Under the guidance and supervision of the Chief of the Management Consulting Team (MCT), the Management Data Analyst is expected to contribute to support overall organizational effectiveness by making substantive contributions to MCT advisory engagements with internal and external stakeholders, including country offices and headquarters units. The Management Data Analyst undertakes research, data collection, and data analysis; develops data analysis tools and applications; manages databases and data platforms; supports internal coordination and knowledge management; and participates in all MCT engagements using a client, quality, and results-oriented approach. The Management Data Analyst works in close collaboration with the team members in developing content and in the delivery of organizational effectiveness advisory services.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling of multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1. Undertake research, data collection, and analysis in support of UNDP’s organizational effectiveness focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Undertake research, data collection, and analysis related to organizational performance, organizational effectiveness, and business process reviews;

- Undertake end-to-end data analysis workflows from data collection, data wrangling, data exploration, data modelling, data analysis, data communication, and visualization;

- Create and maintain databases, dashboards, and data management workflows in coordination with BMS/ITM as applicable;

- Develop methodologies, tools, and software applications related to data analysis and organizational performance;

- Make continuous improvements to organizational performance analytics; and

- Support forward-looking analysis on organizational performance to highlight opportunities for MCT engagements.

2. Participate in client advisory engagements and make contributions in support of business transformation engagements focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Undertake research, data collection, analysis and visualization of information from diverse sources in support of MCT client engagements, including financial modelling and statistical analysis;

- Support development of technical proposals, business cases, and implementation plans/roadmaps;

- Support preparation for and participate in interviews, focus groups and workshops as required;

- Support drafting of written outputs and end-of-engagement reports, as required;

- Follow up with engagement clients on recommendations, as required; and

- Proactively seek, analyze, and apply data sets relevant for MCT engagements.

3. Support data/knowledge management and coordination:

- Maintain MCT’s data and knowledge platforms, including dashboards;

- Develop and maintain MCT’s codebase, database, and data management tools and workflows

- Contribute to the development of templates and standard operating procedures;

- Perform administrative support functions to ensure smooth operations; and

- Support internal coordination, communication, and knowledge management efforts.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is a pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1 : Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

- Digital & Innovation — Data collection: Being skilled in Data Sorting, Data Cleaning, Survey Administration, Presentation and Reporting, including collection of Real-Time Data

- Business Management — Business Analysis: Ability to analyse business processes, business requirements, and identify and define solutions that will maximize the value delivered by an organization to its stakeholders.

- Information Management & Technology — Data management and analytics: Ability to structure data, develop dashboards and visualizations. Design data warehouses, data lakes or data platform concepts. Familiarity with Machine learning, natural language processing or generation, and the use of artificial intelligence to support predictive analytics.

- Business Direction & Strategy — Business Acumen: Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization

- Business Management — Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making

- Business Management — Customer Satisfaction/Client Management: Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide input to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate clients' upcoming needs and concerns.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (Master’s Degree or equivalent) in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Computational Sciences, Business Administration, or related fields, is required, or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s Degree) in the above-mentioned areas with an additional 2 years of relevant work experience will be considered in lieu of the master’s degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of two (2) years with a Master’s degree or four (4) years with a Bachelor’s degree of progressively relevant work experience in research, data collection, analysis, and supporting business transformation engagements is required;

- Knowledge and experience of data science/analytics methodologies and approaches is required;

- Advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages, data modelling, statistical analysis and visualization tools required (e.g. SQL, R, Power BI) is required;

- Demonstrated experience in database and cloud computing platforms required (e.g. Azure, Fabric) is desirable;

- Demonstrated hands-on experience in programming languages, libraries and frameworks for use in data science/analytics (e.g. Python, D3.js, DAX) is required;

- Knowledge of practical applications of predictive analytics and generative AI desirable, including experience assessing and validating AI-generated outputs to ensure accuracy, relevance, and consistency;

- Experience in performance improvement, business process reengineering, organizational effectiveness/organization development, process consultation, or management consulting is a distinct advantage;

- Exposure to international development work is an advantage. Knowledge of the UN/UNDP system is desirable.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required

- Working knowledge of another UN language is desirable.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

For all new UNDP fixed-term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

jobs.description:

Nationals of Jordan are not eligible to apply due to the restriction that nationals of the country where the position is located cannot be considered.

https://www.undp.org/jposc

Background

UNRWA | United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees

The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) provides essential services and humanitarian assistance to Palestine refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank. Its services include education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure rehabilitation, microfinance and emergency assistance.

The Department of Legal Affairs advises on and promotes the consistent interpretation and application of international law throughout the Agency. It develops strategies to promote and implement relevant areas of public international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, refugee law and United Nations law. Particular emphasis is placed on the status and mandate of the Agency, the privileges and immunities of the Agency and its personnel, related responsibilities, and the observance of humanitarian principles.

The Department also provides legal advice and training on the interpretation and application of the Agency’s regulatory framework, including General Assembly resolutions, Staff and Financial Regulations and Rules, associated administrative issuances, and organizational directives. It advises Headquarters and Field departments on governance and management matters, particularly those involving administrative, contractual and procurement law. In addition, the Department provides technical expertise and advice on amendments to the Agency’s regulatory framework, including the drafting of regulations and rules, as well as the preparation and review of legal opinions on complex or sensitive financial matters, particularly those concerning the interpretation of the Agency’s Financial Regulations and Technical Instructions.

Furthermore, the Department reviews drafts of all types of Agency contractual instruments and arrangements, including complex contracts for the procurement of goods and services, memoranda of understanding with partners, and funding agreements. It also provides related training to strengthen the consistent interpretation, application and implementation of the Agency’s contractual and legal requirements.

Training component: Learning elements and expectations

Upon completion of the assignment the JPO will have/ will be able to:

- Legal research, analysis and application of international and general law.

- Legal drafting, advisory work and case management.

- Understanding of UNRWA’s mandate, operations and institutional framework.

- Interpersonal, communication and stakeholder coordination skills.

- Professional judgement, discretion, confidentiality and ethical conduct

The JPO training programme includes the following learning elements:

- Year 1 – Induction and practical learning: Structured induction, guided legal reading, mandatory UN training, daily on-the-job learning, progressive case management and potential Field Operations visits, followed by a review of learning needs and a development plan for Year 2.

- Year 2 – Advanced legal practice and collaboration: Increased responsibility for complex legal matters, including litigation, legal opinions, contracts and procurement, alongside participation in legal training and coordination across UNRWA and the wider UN system, strengthening legal expertise, professional judgement and stakeholder engagement.

- Year 3 – Consolidation and career development: Consolidation of legal expertise through progressively independent work, continued mentoring and feedback, and career development discussions to identify further learning needs and future opportunities within the UN system.

- Duty Travel and Training Allowance (DTTA) : An annual allowance of USD 4,000 supports relevant learning activities, duty travel and professional development related to the assignment.

Content and methodology of supervision:

- Director, Department of Legal Affairs. Purpose: direct supervision, guidance, advice, task assignment, performance monitoring and evaluation. Frequency: daily, through regular meetings, review of deliverables, and feedback on progress and quality of work.

- Heads of the General Law Unit and the International Law Unit. Purpose: substantive guidance, coordination and advice on assigned legal cases and activities across both Units. Frequency: as required, through regular interaction and review of ongoing work.

- Legal advisers and counterparts across the UN system: Purpose: professional exchange, coordination and exposure to legal practice across the UN system. Frequency: as required, through the legal advisers’ coordination mechanism.

- The Associate Legal Officer’s individual workplan will be based on the Department’s annual workplan and will define substantive activities and expected outputs. Progress will be monitored through regular discussions, review of assigned cases and deliverables, and ongoing feedback. The Associate Legal Officer will also participate in official meetings with the Director, as applicable and contribute to follow-up actions, ensuring practical exposure to the Agency’s legal mandate and the work of the Department.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Associate Legal Officer will report to the Director of Legal Affairs and work under their direct daily supervision, with full immersion in the Department’s daily work and activities. The role will have a cross-cutting focus, working closely with both the General Law Unit (covering international administrative law, commercial and institutional matters, and litigation), and the International Law Unit (covering privileges and immunities, protection, neutrality, international human rights mechanisms, and international humanitarian law). The JPO will handle a diverse portfolio of cases across both Units, participate in official meetings and related follow-up actions, gain a thorough understanding of the Agency’s legal mandate in a highly politicised context, and engage with legal advisers across the UN system.

Responsibilities (summary of duties/tasks):

1. Supports the Department’s Legal Advisory Work (30%)

• Participates in the daily work and activities of the General Law and International Law Units, gaining exposure to the full range of legal matters handled by the Department.

• Supports the Director of Legal Affairs in providing legal advice to UNRWA leadership and Directors of Divisions and Departments, including on sensitive and complex legal issues.

• Develops a comprehensive understanding of the Department’s legal functions, priorities and advisory responsibilities.

2. Manages an Assigned Portfolio of Legal Matters and Projects (30%)

• Handles an assigned portfolio of legal cases and issues across the General Law and International Law Units, under the direct supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

• Contributes to litigation and matters arising under the Agency’s internal justice system, the preparation and review of diplomatic correspondence, including notes verbal, and the provision of legal opinions on international law issues.

• Reviews commercial contracts and supports legal aspects of procurement and other operational activities.

• Undertakes designated legal projects to strengthen the Agency’s legal practices and frameworks, including the development of standard agreement templates for engagement with partners.

• Liaises with relevant Agency stakeholders, including Human Resources, Partnerships and the Executive Office, under the guidance and supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

3. Participates in Official Meetings and Follow-up Actions (25%)

• Participates in meetings led by the Director of Legal Affairs and other senior legal officers on substantive, operational and strategic legal matters.

• Contributes to meeting preparation and follow-up, including conducting legal research, drafting documentation and supporting the implementation of agreed actions.

• Develops an understanding of UNRWA’s management structures, decision-making processes and engagement with governments, beneficiaries, partners and other stakeholders.

5. Engages in Legal Coordination Across the United Nations System (15%)

• Participates, through the Director of Legal Affairs, in coordination and information-sharing with legal advisers and counterparts across the United Nations system.

• Gains exposure to the work of the United Nations Office of Legal Affairs and other UN legal offices, including inter-agency coordination mechanisms on legal matters.

• Develops an understanding of common legal issues, institutional practices and approaches to legal advice and coordination across the UN systems.

Competencies

Key competencies

- Excellent oral and written communication skills, including strong legal drafting and analytical skills.

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multicultural environment, maintaining confidentiality and discretion at all times.

- Legal Research and Analysis

- Negotiation and Problem-Solving

- Stakeholder Engagement

- Teamwork and Collaboration

- Planning and Organizing

- Analytical Skills

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Master degree or equivalent in law or a Bachelor’s degree in law plus a minimum of 2 years of paid and relevant working experience. Admission to practice at a national Bar.

- In exceptional cases candidates with a Bachelor’s degree plus a minimum of 4 years relevant working experience can be considered.

- Substantive parts of the candidates’ academic training (Bachelor and/or Master) must have taken place in a developing country that appears on the list of eligible countries. eligible-countries-DC-JPOs.pdf

Working experience:

- Minimum of 2 years relevant working experience after obtaining first university degree in the legal field, with an exposure to development and humanitarian activities of international organisations being an asset.

- Minimum of 4 years relevant working experience for candidates with a Bachelor’s degree.

- Specialisation in public international law and/or the law of international organisations is an asset.

- Experience in international administrative law and/or litigation is an asset.

- Work experience within the UN system should not exceed 1 year, including UNV, (paid) UN internship and UN consultancy.

- All paid work experience since obtaining Bachelor’s degree will/can be considered.

Languages:

- Fluency in English is required;

- Knowledge of Arabic or another UN official language is an asset.

Age:

Maximum age limit is 32 years as of 31 December of the year of application.

jobs.title: Intern - Communications and Outreach
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to achieve the eradication of poverty, and the reduction of inequalities and exclusion. We help countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities and build resilience in order to sustain development results.

UNDP is working to strengthen new frameworks for development, disaster risk reduction and climate change. We support countries' efforts to achieve the new Sustainable Development Goals, which will guide global development priorities through 2030. The key 2030 Agenda principle of leaving no one behind and stamping out inequality is at the core of everything we do.

UNDP focuses on helping countries build and share solutions in three main areas:

- Sustainable development

- Democratic governance and peacebuilding

- Climate and disaster resilience

In all our activities, we encourage the protection of human rights and the empowerment of women, minorities and the poorest and most vulnerable.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Duties and Responsibilities

Working in UNDP Country Office in Thailand and under the direct supervision of the UNDP Communications and Outreach Officer (Head of Communications), the UNDP Communications Intern will work to raise the profile of UNDP Thailand in the media and among Government Agencies, (I)NGOs and other partners, manage the office’s website and general communications requirements, and provide Thai-language editing services to the office team.

The intern will assist in the following duties and responsibilities:

Communications and Outreach (50%):

- Assist in the preparation of promotional/advocacy materials for UNDP outreach, assisting in preparation of presentations, reporting, etc.

- Strengthen social media outreach; support producing new content for social media accounts, drafting messaging in both Thai and English.

- Assist with producing graphic visuals using Microsoft Powerpoint, Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator or any other data visualization tools.

- Assist with media production (e.g., video) using Adobe Premiere Pro, Capcut or any other data visualization tools

Administrative (40%):

- Support communications team on technical and administrative requirements as needed (e.g., planning meetings/workshops, procurement, media)

- Provide back-up translation services when required

- Maintain an up-to-date list of contact media addresses, publication distribution lists.

- Co-manage the UNDP Thailand website to increase digital presence

- Support drafting press releases, op-eds and other text-based outreach materials; copy-writing and proofread; Thai-English translation.

- Assist UNDP staff in media outreach and information dissemination-related activities.

Other (10%):

- Support other/ad hoc activities as seen relevant and needed

Competencies

- Interest and motivation in working in an international organization;

- Good analytical skills in gathering and consolidating data and research for practical implementation;

- Outgoing and initiative-taking person with a goal oriented mind-set;

- Communicates effectively when working in teams and independently;

- Good in organizing and structuring various tasks and responsibilities;

- Displays cultural, gender, religion, race, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability;

- Responds positively to feedback and differing points of view;

- Consistently approaches work with energy and a positive, constructive attitude.

- Strong communication and persuasion skills

- Excellent research and analytical skills

- Results driven, able to meet targets/deadlines

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Candidates must meet one of the following educational requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree (newly graduated or in the final year of study) or pursuing a Master’s degree in related field in Communications, Journalism, Social Sciences or related field; or

- Currently in the final year of a Bachelor’s degree; or

- Currently enrolled in a Master’s degree; or

- Have graduated no longer than 1 year ago from a bachelor’s or master’s degree or equivalent studies.

Language skills:

- Fluent in English- both written and spoken in addition to native proficiency in Thai required;

- Knowledge of other UN languages is an advantage.

INTERNSHIP CONDITIONS

- UNDP will not pay interns for internship but will provide a stipend in the amount of THB 8,302.50 monthly in accordance with the provisions of the UNDP internship policy; all other expenses connected with it will be borne by me or my sponsoring Government or institution;

- UNDP accepts no responsibility for costs arising from accidents and/or illness or death incurred during the internship;

- Interns are not eligible to apply for, or be appointed to, any post in UNDP during the period of the internship;

- Interns must provide proof of enrolment in health insurance plan;

- Interns are not staff members and may not represent UNDP in any official capacity;

- Interns are expected to work full time but flexibility is allowed for education programmes;

- Interns need to obtain financing for subsistence and make own arrangements for internship

Disclaimer

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Executive Coordinator
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme is the United Nations system-wide service for volunteerism. Established by the General Assembly in 1970 and administered by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), UNV mobilizes qualified, motivated and diverse volunteers to support United Nations mandates in development, peace and security, human rights and humanitarian action, while promoting volunteerism as an important means of implementing the 2030 Agenda.

UNV works with organizations of the United Nations system, Member States, national and local institutions, civil society and communities. Its distinctive value lies in connecting the UN system with people and communities through volunteers, providing flexible talent and capacity solutions to UN entities while generating evidence, partnerships and policy support for volunteerism. The programme has evolved into a substantial global operation, with more than 17,000 UN Volunteers deployed in 172 countries in 2025, supported by close to 500 global personnel in UNV headquarters in Bonn, six regional offices and over sixty country presences and multi-country field units.

The current strategic context requires UNV to consolidate previous expansion and relevance as the system-wide service, while at the same time furthering its agility, efficiency, digital maturity, operational and financial resilience, and close alignment with the evolving needs of UN Country Teams and programme countries.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Executive Coordinator reports to UNDP Administrator and leads UNV within the policy, strategic and institutional framework established by the UN General Assembly, the UNDP/UNFPA/UNOPS Executive Board, UNDP Strategic Plan and the UNV Strategic Framework. The position combines the responsibilities of executive leader, strategic manager, and principal advocate of UNV.

The Executive Coordinator provides the overall vision, strategic direction and executive leadership required to fulfill UNV’s mandate and to translate the policy direction of the General Assembly and Executive Board into organizational priorities, strategies and partnerships. The incumbent leads the mobilization and stewardship of human, financial, institutional and partnership resources; represents UNV with Member States, UN entities and external stakeholders; and ensures that the programme operates with integrity, efficiency, transparency, accountability and strong results orientation.

The Executive Coordinator ensures that UNV remains responsive to Member States and UN partners while maintaining a strong focus on volunteer quality, inclusion, duty of care and the experience of volunteers throughout the service cycle.

The Executive Coordinator leads UNV in a way that continuously modernizes its service offer and promotes the strategic relevance of volunteerism in the UN system and beyond. He/she is accountable for positioning UNV as a trusted, effective and innovative system-wide service that enables the United Nations to draw on the skills, commitment and local knowledge of volunteers, while advancing recognition of volunteerism as a means of achieving peace and development.

In addition, the Executive Coordinator has delegated responsibility for coordinating daily management of common premises and common services for the organizations of the UN system at the UN Bonn campus, including related administrative, managerial and policy issues, as well as liaising with the Federal Government of Germany, the State Government of North Rhine-Westphalia and the City Municipality of Bonn on such matters.

1) Strategic leadership, planning and management

- Provide overall strategic leadership to UNV and translate General Assembly resolutions, Executive Board decisions, relevant UN system priorities and UNDP policies into organizational strategies, partnerships and practices.

- Lead the design and implementation of the UNV Strategic Frameworks, ensuring clear institutional priorities, implementation arrangements, measurable results, effective innovations and systematic monitoring of performance.

- Position UNV as an agile, fit-for-purpose and people-centered UN system-wide service, continuously adapting volunteer modalities, operating models and services to changing UN and country-level needs. Leads the institution in a way that continuously modernizes its service offer.

- Promote decentralization and appropriate delegation of authority so that UNV can respond effectively to country and regional requirements while maintaining corporate standards and accountability.

- Foster an organizational culture based on integrity, innovation, collaboration, inclusion, learning and service to UN partners and volunteers.

- Ensure that organizational structures, policies, business processes, digital capabilities and workforce arrangements remain aligned with strategic objectives.

- Inform and consult UNDP Administrator and senior UNDP leadership and ensure that UNV's governance and management arrangements remain consistent with its status as a UNDP-administered system-wide service.

2) External relations, representation and advocacy

- Serve as the principal spokesperson and representative of UNV with Member States, UN entities, civil society, academia, the private sector and other stakeholders. Contribute to intergovernmental dialogue on volunteerism, including follow-up to relevant General Assembly resolutions, Secretary-General reports, international observances and global policy processes. In doing so, demonstrates strong partnerships acumen and intuitional judgement.

- Advocate for volunteerism as a cross-cutting means of implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals and as a contributor to peace and security, human rights and humanitarian action.

- Sustain high-level partnerships for the integration of volunteerism into national plans and policies. Maintain strategic engagement with Resident Coordinators and UN Country Teams and promote the inclusion of volunteerism in Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks and country programming.

- Position UNV as a source of credible evidence, policy advice and innovation on volunteerism, including through research, data, knowledge products and global advocacy.

- Mobilize support for inclusive volunteerism, with particular attention to participation by women, young and older people, persons with disabilities, people from developing countries and other groups that may face barriers to participation.

- Strengthen UNV's public profile while ensuring communications are evidence-based, consistent with UN values and focused on the contribution of volunteers to tangible results. Represent UNV at high-level international forums and public events, communicating its mandate, results and strategic priorities with clarity and credibility.

3) Results and resources management

- Ensure that UNV delivers the results approved by its governing bodies and that organizational performance is systematically measured, analyzed, communicated and used for decision-making.

- Oversee the effective and transparent management of UNV's financial, human, digital and other resources, consistent with UNDP policies, UN rules and applicable accountability frameworks.

- Safeguard the financial sustainability of UNV, strengthen the resource base, diversifying strategic partnerships, and maintain appropriate balances between institutional resources and requirements.

- Provide strategic stewardship of the Special Voluntary Fund and other flexible resources, ensuring that they are deployed where they can respond to emergencies and/or generate catalytic and innovative high-value impact.

- Oversee enterprise-level risk management, internal controls, audit follow-up and evaluation, ensuring that risks are identified early and addressed decisively.

- Strengthen data-driven management, including the use of artificial intelligence, digital tools, analytics and evidence to improve organizational performance, decision-making, cost-effectiveness and efficiency gains.

- Report transparently on results, resources, risks and performance to the Executive Board, UNDP leadership, Member States and other relevant stakeholders.

4) People, innovation and organizational effectiveness

- Champion the principle that UNV's central asset is its people: UN Volunteers, staff and the communities and partners with whom they work. Translates general duty of care commitments onto practical arrangements and initiatives.

- Ensure that volunteerism is delivered through high-quality, safe, inclusive and meaningful assignments, with appropriate duty of care throughout the volunteer life cycle.

- Oversee continued modernization of volunteer management, including flexible, short-term, part-time, remote and other modalities responsive to the evolving needs of UN entities and programme countries.

- Ensure that innovation, digital transformation, automation and responsible use of data and emerging technologies improve service quality, accessibility, speed and efficiency.

- Encourage experimentation and learning while maintaining appropriate safeguards, ethical standards and accountability.

- Strengthen UNV's ability to identify emerging needs and rapidly adapt its operating model, particularly in fragile, conflict-affected, humanitarian and crisis contexts.

- Foster a culture of continuous improvement in which evidence from volunteers, host entities, programme countries, evaluations and operational experience informs policy and management decisions.

- Promote leadership development, collaboration across headquarters, regional and field structures, and a shared organizational identity centered on service, solidarity, professionalism and measurable impact.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent oversees the entire personnel of United Nations Volunteers.

Competencies

Core:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 4: Prioritize team workflow, mobilize resources, drive scalable results/strategic impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 4: Easily navigate complexity, encourage/enable radical innovation, has foresight

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 4: Create systems and processes that enable learning and development for all

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 4: Proactively initiate/lead organizational change, champion new systems/processes

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 4: Able to make difficult decisions in challenging situations, inspire confidence

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 4: Construct strategic multi-partner alliances in high-stakes situations, foster co-creation

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 4: Create ethical culture, identify/address barriers to inclusion

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross Functional and Technical:

- Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system. Business Acumen: Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization. Effective Decision Making: Ability to take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources.

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organizations programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment. Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Partnership Management - Relationship Management: Ability to build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Finance - Development Finance Expertise: Ability to develop and work with innovative financing mechanisms and instruments, e.g. social/development impact bonds, guarantees, climate finance, etc.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in Social or Political Sciences, Economics, Public or Business Administration, Management or related field.

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with two additional years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of a master's degree.

Experience:

- More than 15 years of relevant experience that combines policy, partnerships and programme leadership engagement, and strategic resource management is required.

- Progressively senior management experience with international organizations or Member States’ public service, with clear demonstration of high-level engagement in diplomacy, intergovernmental processes, and international political or development matters is required.

- Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership and position an organization effectively within a broader international context is required.

- Demonstrated experience in driving institutional modernization and change is required.

- Solid experience and proven track record in leading other managers and teams with integrity and duty of care is required.

- Demonstrated partnership acumen, ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with key partners, with strong communication and advocacy skills is required.

- Experience and demonstrated results in working on sustainable development issues at country level is a strong asset.

- Solid understanding of the UN system and intergovernmental processes is an asset.

- Knowledge of UN(DP) policies, rules and regulations is an asset.

- Experience of working on peace and security and humanitarian action is an asset.

- Experience in managing substantial regional or global operations is an asset.

- Experience in managing digital transformations is an asset.

- Experience of managing volunteer programmes or serving as a UN Volunteer is an asset.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency in another official UN language is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Programme de Stages du PNUD Djibouti
jobs.description:
Contexte

Le PNUD intervient dans environ 170 pays et territoires pour contribuer à l’éradication de la pauvreté, réduire les inégalités et favoriser l’inclusion ainsi que la résilience pour soutenir le développement durable. En tant qu’agence de développement des Nations Unies, le PNUD joue un rôle clé dans l'accompagnement des pays vers l’atteinte des Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD). Sur la base de l’UNSDCF 2025‑2030, aligné sur la Vision Djibouti 2035 et le Plan National de Développement 2022‑2024, le Bureau Pays du PNUD a élaboré un nouveau Programme Pays 2025‑2030 articulé autour de deux piliers :

- Gouvernance et Cohésion sociale

- Diversification économique et Résilience aux changements climatiques

L’objectif principal du programme pays du PNUD Djibouti est d’accélérer l’atteinte des objectifs de développement durable (ODD). Il aborde les défis liés au développement, aux risques climatiques, à l’adaptation et à l’atténuation du changement climatique, encourage un financement innovant et inclusif, renforce la résilience et lutte contre la pauvreté, les inégalités de genre, les disparités géographiques et l’exclusion. Il promeut la durabilité environnementale grâce à des stratégies intégrées et renforce les capacités institutionnelles nationales.

Objectif du stage

Le stage offre aux participants une immersion professionnelle enrichissante dans les opérations du PNUD tout en contribuant aux activités clés du bureau, notamment la communication, la gestion des activités programmatique et le support IT aux operations du bureau pays. Le bureau recherchent 3 stagiaires qui auraient l’une de ses compétences.

Objectifs principaux du stage:

Renforcer l’expérience académique des étudiants de niveau supérieur par une mise en pratique directe au sein du PNUD et une participation à ses projets de développement à Djibouti.

Familiariser les étudiants avec l’environnement de travail d’une organisation multilatérale et approfondir leur compréhension des objectifs et actions du PNUD a Djibouti.

Responsabilités et tâches principales

Tâches en Communication

Sous la supervision directe du/de la chargé(e) de communication :

- Création de contenu : Contribuer à la conception et production de supports imprimés et digitaux (brochures, rapports, newsletters, publications réseaux sociaux).

- Gestion des réseaux sociaux : Produire des contenus visuels dynamiques pour Twitter, Facebook, YouTube (infographies, animations, vidéos).

- Contenu multimédia : Préparer des visuels, retoucher des photos et contribuer à la production de vidéos courtes illustrant les actions du PNUD.

- Couverture d’événements : Appuyer la couverture photo/vidéo lors d’ateliers, conférences et visites de terrain.

- Appui aux campagnes : Concevoir des supports en ligne/hors ligne pour les campagnes de sensibilisation (Journées internationales, plaidoyer public...).

- Mise à jour du site web & réseaux : Contribuer au maintien des plateformes du PNUD Djibouti.

- Partenariats et mobilisation de ressources : Appuyer la préparation de notes conceptuelles, présentations et profils donateurs.

- Rédaction & coordination : Aider à la rédaction de communications aux partenaires, mise à jour de la base de contacts, suivi de réunions.

- Gestion des connaissances : Participer à la création et diffusion de rapports, études de cas, success stories et autres produits de connaissance.

2. Tâches en Gestion de Programme

Sous la supervision du/de la chargé(e) de programme :

- Préparation de documents : Mise en forme de rapports, propositions, présentations ; conformité aux standards du PNUD.

- Organisation d’événements : Soutien logistique pour ateliers, réunions et formations (coordination, salles, participants).

- Support administratif : Impression, diffusion de documents, classement physique et électronique.

- Communication interne/externe : rédaction de courriels, newsletters, diffusion d’informations.

- Recherche & collecte de données : Compilation de données, bonnes pratiques, success stories ; appui à la création d’infographies.

- Support transversal : Collaboration avec différentes unités et contribution aux produits de connaissance.

3. Tâches en Technologies de l’Information (ICT)

Sous la supervision de l’Associé TIC :

- Support opérationnel TIC : Installation, configuration et maintenance du matériel et des logiciels. Assistance technique aux utilisateurs. Participation aux tests et au dépannage des systèmes.

- Documentation & rapports : Contribution à la documentation technique et aux rapports de performance. Mise à jour des registres d’actifs TIC.

- Support général : Gestion de l’inventaire du matériel informatique. Appui aux prestataires externes lors des interventions.

- Renforcement des connaissances : Participation aux formations internes, partage de connaissances et propositions d’amélioration.

- Collaboration : Travail en équipe, communication avec les utilisateurs, contribution aux projets TIC.

Compétences requises

Maîtrise de l’outil informatique : MS Office

Eligibilité

Les candidats doivent répondre à l’un des critères suivants :

a) Être inscrit dans un programme de 2ᵉ cycle (Master ou plus) en communication, développement économique, études environnementales ou IT.

b) Être en dernière année d’un 1er cycle universitaire (Licence ou équivalent).

c) Être récemment diplômé d’un programme cité ci‑dessus et commencer le stage dans l’année suivant l’obtention du diplôme.

d) Être inscrit dans un programme professionnel postuniversitaire incluant un stage.

Langues

- Maîtrise du français .

- La connaissance de l’anglais est un atout.

Informations pour les candidats concernant les rosters du PNUD

Note : Le PNUD se réserve le droit de sélectionner un ou plusieurs candidats à partir de cet avis de vacance. Nous pouvons également conserver les candidatures et considérer les candidats postulant à ce poste pour d’autres postes similaires au sein du PNUD.

Non-discrimination

Le PNUD applique une politique de tolérance zéro à l’égard de l’exploitation et des abus sexuels, des comportements sexuels inappropriés, du harcèlement sexuel et de l’abus d’autorité. Tous les candidats sélectionnés feront donc l’objet de contrôles rigoureux de références et d’antécédents, et devront respecter ces normes et principes. Le PNUD est un employeur garantissant l’égalité des chances et l’inclusion, qui ne pratique aucune discrimination fondée sur la race, le sexe, l’identité de genre, la religion, la nationalité, l’origine ethnique, l’orientation sexuelle, le handicap, la grossesse, l’âge, la langue, l’origine sociale ou tout autre statut.

Avertissement concernant les arnaques

Les Nations Unies ne facturent aucuns frais de candidature, de traitement, de formation, d’entretien, de test ou autres dans le cadre du processus de candidature ou de recrutement. Si vous recevez une demande de paiement, veuillez l’ignorer. Par ailleurs, veuillez noter que les emblèmes, logos, noms et adresses peuvent être facilement copiés et reproduits. Vous êtes donc invité à faire preuve d’une vigilance particulière lorsque vous soumettez des informations personnelles sur Internet.

jobs.title: Monitoring and Evaluation and Risk Management-Team Lead (Open to all applicants).
jobs.location: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Central Africa is home to the second largest tropical rainforest in the world. Forest loss is accelerating despite ongoing efforts, as government action alone has not been sufficient to establish an effective balance between the interests of the forest and of economic development.

On this basis, a coalition of willing donors – Norway, European Union, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Belgium, Netherlands, and South Korea – together with Central African partner countries – Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Cameroon, the Republic of Congo, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea, and the Republic of Gabon – have entered in 2015 into a collaborative partnership to establish in partnership with the United Nations, the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI). The objective of this initiative is to recognize and preserve the value of the forests in the region to mitigate climate change, reduce poverty, and contribute to sustainable development. This objective will be attained through the implementation of country-led, national scale REDD+ and Low Emissions Development (LED) investment frameworks that include policy reforms and measures to address the drivers of deforestation and forest degradation and promote sustainable development.

The CAFI Trust Fund is the principal means to implement the Central African Forest Initiative. It is administered by the MPTF-Office (http://mptf.undp.org/factsheet/fund/AFI00). As per the updated Fund Terms of Reference and the direct cost Secretariat project document, the UNDP Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) is hosting the CAFI Secretariat providing the secretariat administrative services under the oversight of the CAFI Executive Board and other participating UN organizations (UNDP, UNCDF, FAO, UN-Habitat, UNFPA, and UNEP).

Established by the Executive Board, the CAFI Secretariat was created to support the fund management coupled with policy and programmatic dialogue and portfolio administration, strongly based on result-based management and solid reporting methods. With the intensification of CAFI presence in countries and solid increase in investment programmes and related digital innovations, including but not limited to the introduction of Payment for Environmental Services, a Technical Assistance Facility, Private Sector projects, it is fundamental that the Secretariat provides high-efficiency M&E services to support the Trust Fund objectives. This requires an M&E Unit led by an expert Head of M&E that can efficiently work across all CAFI partner countries and portfolio accordingly namely DRC, Cameroon, Republic of Congo and Gabon, embracing and helping to expand CAFI’s digital ecosystem in support of M&E in general and performance-based programming in particular.

Position Purpose

Under the strategic guidance of the Head of Secretariat, the Team Lead f the Monitoring and Evaluation and Risk Management Unit promotes results-based management and a programme effectiveness approach, by leading the design and implementation of innovative and effective monitoring, evaluation and learning frameworks, systems and tools, and implements a robust approach to risk management across the investment portfolio of the Trust Fund, serving the Executive Board in risk-based decision making approach. Where relevant, the Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management will also support programme quality assurance and developing relevant systems. The Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management provides technical support on M&E and reporting practices to the business unit`s senior management as well as programme and project teams. The Team Lead of M&E & Risk Management promotes a collaborative, efficient, client-focused, evidence-based, and portfolio management approach.

The Team Lead of M&E and risk leads a team of personnel working on M&E and RBM, and as applicable, quality assurance work; collaborates closely with Programme, Operations and project teams in other branches and across partners and donors, programme staff in other UN agencies, and Government officials, technical advisers and experts, NGOs, and other organizations on programme implementation and monitoring and evaluation issues and practices.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Lead in designing and implementing the monitoring and evaluation frameworks, systems, and tools at Fund level and conduct quality assurance of the overall Fund’s portfolio.

• Develop integrated monitoring and evaluation (M&E) and results-based management (RBM) policies, frameworks, systems/tools and plans at Fund level, in line with CAFI’s Terms of Reference and CAFI’s Manual of Operations and its related policies towards programmes, projects and initiatives, to inform on their adequate implementation, and ensure their effectiveness and compliance with the Fund programming and reporting requirements.

• Development, continued improvement and implementation of CAFI M&E and Learning policy and strategies/Plans (e.g. the Fund’s evaluation strategy/plan), as well as related guidelines, minimum standards, procedures and templates.

• Develop SOPs and guidelines for CAFI Secretariat staff, partner countries and implement organizations.

• Coordinate partner countries in adapting, if and as required, CAFI’s M&E framework, procedures and tools to their context, while ensuring full alignment with CAFI’s.

• Participate in CAFI’s annual planning processes, defining targets and harmonized indicators to ensure consistency with CAFI’s policies across CAFI’s portfolio of programmes and projects.

• Contribute to the elaboration and mapping of business processes and procedures in programme and project oversight that includes providing input to establishment of quality assurance processes, guidance notes, protocols, tools, checklists, and sharing best practices.

• Provide technical, innovative and policy advice on M&E and RBM requirements and activities to programme and project managers, staff concerned with monitoring and evaluation, and consultants and/or members of the evaluation team. Collaborate with Programme and project teams on developing integrated development approaches.

• Ensure gender equality, disability inclusion, and Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principles are an integral part of programmes and operations and that these considerations are fully mainstreamed into programming and reflected in project design, monitoring, reporting, and evaluations in line with the UNDP Gender Equality and Disability Inclusion Strategies, UNSDG Operational Guide for Country Teams on LNOB, and available regional guidance.

• Develop the evaluation plan and ensure its timely implementation in line with CAFI standards for the CAFI funded programs/projects, Letters of Intent and the Trust Fund (such as independent evaluations, mid-term reviews, tranche releases).

• Ensure monitoring of data collection by projects, analyze and exploit data combining layers of maps, photo and satellite images, text and statistics.

• Facilitate the development and implementation of spatial monitoring through a dedicated structured geographic information system integrating data acquisition, administration, processing, analysis and dissemination, with support from specialized personnel.

• Support the implementation and growth of CAFI’s ecosystem of digital tools in support of efficiency and transparency, in synergy with colleagues from the programming and PES teams (specifically CAFI Connect and CAFI PES).

2.) Lead coordination of monitoring, reporting, evaluation and results-based management of CAFI programmes and projects.

• Oversee implementation and application of efficient and evidence-based results monitoring, and as applicable, quality assurance work for programme and project development and delivery using integrated portfolio management approach as well as the CAFI Connect tool and the CAFI PES dashboard

• Ensure timely identification of potential implementation problems and bottlenecks and advise the management and programme/project teams on strategies/corrective measures to address them.

• Lead the cross-cutting reviews, studies and evaluations of the M&E unit.

• Manage and coordinate third-party monitoring and/or any other data collection intervention.

• Review and approve all plans and Terms of Reference (TOR) for project and programme mid-term reviews, evaluations, and assessments. Participate in consultant and evaluation team recruitment and selection. Review and provide input on evaluation inception reports, evaluation methodology, and draft evaluation reports for quality assurance and compliance purposes.

• Ensure the optimal use of evaluation findings and recommendations. Provide guidance and input in the preparation of timely management responses and key actions to all evaluations; consolidate evaluation findings to assess effectiveness and impact of programmes/projects; and develop a communication/dissemination plan to incorporate into recommendations for improvement by projects and partners. Follow up on implementation of evaluation recommendations by project teams.

• Facilitate collation of monitoring and evaluation of impact results and/or data/information in a format that is relevant for evidence-based policy, communications and/or development interventions.

• Drive the application of CAFI’s social and environmental safeguards as applicable as part of the reporting exercises and the programme evaluation strategy.

• Lead the development of funded evaluation plans that accompany the development of programme documents and oversee the timely implementation of evaluations in the plan.

• Provide support, as applicable, in ensuring projects are designed, implemented, and completed in line with RBM and quality standards and programme and project management policies and procedures.

• Provide input into the independent verification of land use projects as per relevant EB decisions.

3.) Provide substantive contributions to capacity building and facilitate knowledge building and sharing on monitoring, evaluation, and results-based management

• Contribute to the assessment of capacity needs and elaboration of capacity development plans, tools, and methodologies. Design, organize and lead training activities; and participate in preparing knowledge packages on RBM, monitoring and evaluation, data collection/survey methods, gender mainstreaming and portfolio approach programme and project teams as well as national partners and key stakeholders.

• Lead the identification, synthesis, documentation, and dissemination of key lessons learned and good practices derived from monitoring and evaluation activities on what works, what does not work, and/or revised theories of change to identify innovative ideas for their scaling or replication.

• Provide sound contributions to local and global networks, communities of practice, and other knowledge management mechanisms. Proactively participate in regional and international fora on relevant thematic areas (including engaging in thematic discussions, contributing with analytical papers, etc.).

4.) Lead solid and efficient Reporting

• Ensure donor reports are timely prepared in line with established requirements. Prepare Results Reports, analysis of results of projects, and other periodic information and reports for the Executive Board, government partners, donor community and other key stakeholders. Advise on data use and interpretation to assess country programme results, improve programme quality, identify trends, and inform future decision-making processes.

• With direct support from CAFI’s Reporting Specialist, facilitate the reporting exercises across CAFI`s portfolio of funded projects, incorporation of lessons learned from previous exercises and semi-annual reporting to the Executive Board on the compliance of the reporting function. Provide regular update to the Executive Board on project and portfolio performance based on the information in the CAFI Connect and CAFI PES dashboard and narrative reports.

• Lead the organization and execution of accountability sessions with implementing partners to drive performance and reinforce a results culture

5.) Lead Implementation of Risk Management Framework across CAFI Portfolio

• Develop and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework for the Trust Fund, maintaining updated all related Policies and SOPs.

• Identify and assess risks across key categories, taking due diligence and reporting as per Risk Policies in place.

• Conduct risk assessments at portfolio, program, and country levels.

• Lead and guide funded projects in conducting risk due diligence.

• Maintain and regularly update a risk register.

• Design and implement risk mitigation strategies and internal controls.

• Advise program teams and implementing partners on risk reduction measures, compliance requirements and preventive controls such as procurement safeguards and financial oversight

• Ensure integration of risk management into program design and approval processes.

• Drive the development and oversee the implementation of contingency and risk response plans.

• Co-lead fiduciary risk oversight by working in collaboration with Management Specialist to monitor financial management reports from implementing organizations.

• Proactively track risk indicators and early warning signals to identify emerging threats; escalate critical risks to accordingly and propose corrective actions

• Contribute to the preparation of annual reports and portfolio reviews with a risk perspective.

• In collaboration with the Policy Dialogue Unit, conduct due diligence assessments of implementing partners in regard to their Institutional capacity, Governance systems and financial management capabilities

• Lead the risk due diligence for all prospective partners and new program designs to ensure risk is integrated into all approval processes

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervises M&E Specialist (IPSA) and MRV and Compliance Manager (IPSA)

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction and Strategy-System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management-Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment

Business Management & Monitoring & Evaluation:

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks.

- Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

Business Management & Risk Management: Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

Partnership Management & Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

2030 Agenda: Engagement & Effectiveness: Programmatic Risk Management and Analysis.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Development/Development Studies, Economics, Statistics, Business Management, Social Policy, or related field is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in monitoring and evaluation, programme and/or team management working with quality assurance instruments, results-based management models, and multiple stakeholders is required.

- Proven experience in the Monitoring & Evaluation of a large Fund is required.

- Experience and proven technical knowledge of the results-based management cycle and monitoring and evaluation is required.

- Proven experience in designing monitoring and evaluation systems and designing development projects or integrated portfolios is required.

- Proven ability to work with quantitative and qualitative data and appropriately use qualitative data /information collection tools in innovative ways is required.

- Demonstrated experience in using GIS tools (e.g. QGIS, ArcGis), mobile data collection tools (e.g. Kobo toolbox, ODK), remote sensing applications and data treatment software (e.g. SPSS) is an asset.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), and web-based management systems, and up-to-date, advanced knowledge of data management tools and database packages is required.

- Experience in designing, implementing and/or managing assessments and/or data collection exercises/processes is desired.

- Experience in using project management or project portfolio management softwares (e.g. TECPRO, MSPRO) is an advantage.

- Certification in Enterprise Risk Management or related is desired.

- Expertise in fiduciary oversight and financial controls is desired.

- Experience conducting applied research projects and reporting on findings is desired.

Languages:

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required

- Fluency in written and spoken French is required

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement
